questions.text: A function $f : A \to B$ defined as $f(x) = 2x$ is both one-one and onto. If $A = \{1, 2, 3, 4\}$, then find the set $B$.
A relation $R$ is defined on a set of real numbers $\mathbb{R}$ as $R = \{(x, y) : x \cdot y \text{ is an irrational number}\}$. Check whether $R$ is reflexive, symmetric and transitive or not.

answer.text:
$R=\{(x,y):x\cdot y \text{ is an irrational number}\}$.
Reflexive: $(1,1)\notin R$ as $1\cdot 1=1$ is rational (a counter-example). $\therefore R$ is not reflexive.
Symmetric: Let $(x,y)\in R\therefore x\cdot y$ is irrational $\therefore y\cdot x$ is irrational $\therefore (y,x)\in R$. $\therefore R$ is symmetric.
Transitive: $(1,\sqrt2)\in R$, $(\sqrt2,2)\in R$ but $(1,2)\notin R$ (a counter-example). $\therefore R$ is not transitive.

questions.text: A function $f : [-4, 4] \to [0, 4]$ is given by $f(x) = \sqrt{16 - x^2}$. Show that $f$ is an onto function but not a one-one function. Further, find all possible values of '$a$' for which $f(a) = \sqrt{7}$.

answer.text:
Onto: Let $y=\sqrt{16-x^2}\Rightarrow y\geq0$
Squaring we get $x^2=16-y^2\Rightarrow x=\pm\sqrt{16-y^2}$
For each $y\in[-4,4]$, $x$ is a real number, $\therefore 0\leq y\leq4\Rightarrow R_f=[0,4]=$ co-domain $\therefore f$ is an onto function.
One-One: $f(-1)=f(1)=\sqrt{15}$ but $-1\neq1$, $\therefore f$ is not a one-one function.
$f(a)=\sqrt7\Rightarrow\sqrt{16-a^2}=\sqrt7\Rightarrow a=\pm3$

questions.text: Show that a function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ defined as $f(x) = \dfrac{5x - 3}{4}$ is both one-one and onto.

answer.text:
Let $x_1,x_2\in\mathbb R$ (Domain) such that $f(x_1)=f(x_2)$
$\Rightarrow\dfrac{5x_1-3}{4}=\dfrac{5x_2-3}{4}\Rightarrow 5x_1=5x_2\Rightarrow x_1=x_2$. $\therefore f$ is one-one.
Let $y\in\mathbb R$ (co-domain). Then $f(x)=y$ for some $x$, if $y=\dfrac{5x-3}{4}$, i.e., if $x=\dfrac{4y+3}{5}\in\mathbb R$ (Domain).
Thus, for every $y\in\mathbb R$ (co-domain) there exists $\dfrac{4y+3}{5}\in\mathbb R$ (domain) such that $f\!\left(\dfrac{4y+3}{5}\right)=y$.
$\therefore$ Range of $f=\mathbb R=$ co-domain of $f$. Hence $f$ is onto.

questions.text: If $N$ denotes the set of all natural numbers and $R$ is the relation on $N \times N$ defined by $(a, b)\ R\ (c, d)$, if $ad(b + c) = bc(a + d)$. Show that $R$ is an equivalence relation.

answer.text:
Reflexive: $(a,b)\,R\,(a,b)\ \forall\,(a,b)\in N\times N$ since $ab(b+a)=ba(a+b)$ is always true.
Symmetric: Let $(a,b)\,R\,(c,d)$. Then $ad(b+c)=bc(a+d)\Rightarrow bc(a+d)=ad(b+c)\Rightarrow(c,d)\,R\,(a,b)$.
Transitive: Let $(a,b)\,R\,(c,d)$ and $(c,d)\,R\,(e,f)$. Then $ad(b+c)=bc(a+d)$ and $cf(d+e)=de(c+f)$
$\Rightarrow\dfrac1c+\dfrac1b=\dfrac1d+\dfrac1a$ and $\dfrac1e+\dfrac1d=\dfrac1f+\dfrac1c$
Adding, $\dfrac1b+\dfrac1e=\dfrac1a+\dfrac1f\Rightarrow af(b+e)=be(a+f)\Rightarrow(a,b)\,R\,(e,f)$
$\therefore R$ is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, hence an equivalence relation.

questions.text: Let $f : R - \left\{-\dfrac{4}{3}\right\} \to R$ be a function defined as $f(x) = \dfrac{4x}{3x + 4}$. Show that $f$ is a one-one function. Also, check whether $f$ is an onto function or not.

answer.text:
One-one: Let $f(x_1)=f(x_2)\Rightarrow\dfrac{4x_1}{3x_1+4}=\dfrac{4x_2}{3x_2+4}$
$\Rightarrow 12x_1x_2+16x_1=12x_1x_2+16x_2\Rightarrow x_1=x_2\Rightarrow f$ is one-one.
Onto: Let $y\in\mathbb R$. $y=\dfrac{4x}{3x+4}\Rightarrow 3xy+4y=4x\Rightarrow x(3y-4)=-4y\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{4y}{4-3y}$
$x$ is real if $y\neq\dfrac43$. So $R_f=\mathbb R-\left\{\dfrac43\right\}\neq$ co-domain of $f$. So $f$ is not onto.

questions.text: Let $A = \{3, 5\}$. Then number of reflexive relations on $A$ is :

An organization conducted bike race under two different categories — Boys and Girls. There were 28 participants in all. Among all of them, finally three from category 1 and two from category 2 were selected for the final race. Ravi forms two sets B and G with these participants for his college project. Let $B = \{b_1, b_2, b_3\}$ and $G = \{g_1, g_2\}$, where B represents the set of Boys selected and G the set of Girls selected for the final race. Based on the above information, answer the following questions : (I) How many relations are possible from B to G ? (II) Among all the possible relations from B to G, how many functions can be formed from B to G ? (III)(a) Let $R : B \to B$ be defined by $R = \{(x, y) : x \text{ and } y \text{ are students of the same sex}\}$. Check if $R$ is an equivalence relation.  OR  (III)(b) A function $f : B \to G$ be defined by $f = \{(b_1, g_1), (b_2, g_2), (b_3, g_1)\}$. Check if $f$ is bijective. Justify your answer.

answer.text:
(I) Number of relations from $B$ to $G=2^{3\times2}=2^{6}=64$.
(II) Number of possible functions from $B$ to $G=2^{3}=8$.
(III) $R=\{(x,y):x \text{ and } y \text{ are students of the same sex}\}$ is an equivalence relation as it is reflexive, symmetric and transitive.

questions.text: A relation $R$ on set $A = \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5\}$ is defined as $R = \{(x, y) : |x^2 - y^2| < 8\}$. Check whether the relation $R$ is reflexive, symmetric and transitive.

answer.text:
(a) Reflexive: $|x^2-x^2|=0<8\ \forall\,x\in A\Rightarrow(x,x)\in R$, so $R$ is reflexive.
Symmetric: Let $(x,y)\in R$, then $|x^2-y^2|<8\Rightarrow|y^2-x^2|<8\Rightarrow(y,x)\in R$, so $R$ is symmetric.
Transitive: $(1,2),(2,3)\in R$ as $|1^2-2^2|<8$ and $|2^2-3^2|<8$, but $|1^2-3^2|=8\not<8\Rightarrow(1,3)\notin R$.
Hence $R$ is not transitive.

questions.text: A function $f$ is defined from $\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ as $f(x) = ax + b$, such that $f(1) = 1$ and $f(2) = 3$. Find function $f(x)$. Hence, check whether function $f(x)$ is one-one and onto or not.

answer.text:
$f(x)=ax+b$; solving $a+b=1$ and $2a+b=3$ gives $a=2,\ b=-1$, so $f(x)=2x-1$.
Let $f(x_1)=f(x_2)\Rightarrow2x_1-1=2x_2-1\Rightarrow x_1=x_2$, hence $f$ is one-one.
Let $y=2x-1,\ y\in\mathbb{R}$ (codomain) $\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{y+1}{2}\in\mathbb{R}$ (domain), and $f\!\left(\dfrac{y+1}{2}\right)=y$, hence $f$ is onto.

questions.text: Show that a function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ defined by $f(x) = \dfrac{2x}{1 + x^2}$ is neither one-one nor onto. Further, find set A so that the given function $f : \mathbb{R} \to A$ becomes an onto function.

answer.text:
Let $f(x_1)=f(x_2)$ for some $x_1,x_2\in\mathbb{R}$, then $\dfrac{2x_1}{1+x_1^2}=\dfrac{2x_2}{1+x_2^2}$
$\Rightarrow(x_1-x_2)(1-x_1x_2)=0\Rightarrow x_1=x_2$ or $x_1x_2=1$; so if $x_1x_2=1,\ x_1\neq x_2$. Hence $f$ is not one-one.
Let $y=f(x)$. If $y\neq0$, $yx^2-2x+y=0\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{2\pm\sqrt{4-4y^2}}{2y}$
For $x$ to be real, $4-4y^2\ge0\Rightarrow y^2\le1\Rightarrow-1\le y\le1$
Range $=[-1,1]\neq$ codomain, hence $f$ is not onto.
For the function to become onto, $A=[-1,1]$.

questions.text: A relation R is defined on $N \times N$ (where N is the set of natural numbers) as : $(a, b)\ R\ (c, d) \Leftrightarrow a - c = b - d$. Show that R is an equivalence relation.

answer.text:
Reflexive: $a-a=b-b\Rightarrow(a,b)\,R\,(a,b)\ \forall\,(a,b)\in N\times N$, so $R$ is reflexive.
Symmetric: $(a,b)\,R\,(c,d)\Rightarrow a-c=b-d\Rightarrow c-a=d-b\Rightarrow(c,d)\,R\,(a,b)$, so $R$ is symmetric.
Transitive: $(a,b)\,R\,(c,d)$ and $(c,d)\,R\,(e,f)\Rightarrow a-c=b-d,\ c-e=d-f\Rightarrow a-e=b-f\Rightarrow(a,b)\,R\,(e,f)$, so $R$ is transitive.
Thus $R$ is an equivalence relation.

questions.text: A relation R on set $A = \{-4, -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4\}$ be defined as $R = \{(x, y) : x + y \text{ is an integer divisible by 2}\}$. Show that R is an equivalence relation. Also, write the equivalence class $[2]$.

answer.text:
For reflexive : clearly $x + x$, i.e. $2x$, is an integer divisible by $2$.
$\Rightarrow (x, x) \in R \Rightarrow R$ is reflexive.
For symmetric : $(x, y) \in R \Rightarrow x + y$ is an integer divisible by $2$.
$\Rightarrow y + x$ is an integer divisible by $2 \Rightarrow (y, x) \in R$, so $R$ is symmetric.
For transitive : $(x, y) \in R \Rightarrow x + y$ is an integer divisible by $2$,
and $(y, z) \in R \Rightarrow y + z$ is an integer divisible by $2$.
so, $(x + z) + 2y$ is an integer divisible by $2$.
$\Rightarrow x + z$ is an integer divisible by $2 \Rightarrow (x, z) \in R$, so $R$ is transitive.
Hence $R$ is an equivalence relation.
Equivalence class $[2] = \{-4, -2, 0, 2, 4\}$

questions.text: Let $A = \mathbb{R} - \{5\}$ and $B = \mathbb{R} - \{1\}$. Consider the function $f : A \to B$, defined by $f(x) = \dfrac{x - 3}{x - 5}$. Show that $f$ is one-one and onto.

answer.text:
Let $f(x_1)=f(x_2)$ for some $x_1,x_2\in A$: $\dfrac{x_1-3}{x_1-5}=\dfrac{x_2-3}{x_2-5}$
$\Rightarrow(x_1-3)(x_2-5)=(x_2-3)(x_1-5)\Rightarrow x_1=x_2$, so $f$ is one-one.
Let $y=f(x)=\dfrac{x-3}{x-5}\Rightarrow y(x-5)=x-3\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{5y-3}{y-1}$
$x$ is defined for all values of $y$ except $y=1$, so Range $=\mathbb{R}-\{1\}$ and codomain is $\mathbb{R}-\{1\}$.
Since Range $=$ codomain, $f$ is onto. Thus $f$ is one-one and onto.

questions.text: Check whether the relation S in the set of real numbers $\mathbb{R}$ defined by $S = \{(a, b) : \text{where } a - b + \sqrt{2} \text{ is an irrational number}\}$ is reflexive, symmetric or transitive.

answer.text:
Reflexive: $a-a+\sqrt2=\sqrt2$ is irrational $\Rightarrow(a,a)\in S$, so $S$ is reflexive.
Symmetric: $(a,b)\in S\Rightarrow a-b+\sqrt2$ is irrational, but $b-a+\sqrt2$ may not be. E.g. $(\sqrt2,1)\in S$ as $2\sqrt2-1$ is irrational, but $(1,\sqrt2)\notin S$ as $1-\sqrt2+\sqrt2=1$ is not irrational. So $S$ is not symmetric.
Transitive: $(1,\sqrt3)\in S$ and $(\sqrt3,\sqrt2)\in S$ (as $\sqrt3-\sqrt2+\sqrt2=\sqrt3$ is irrational), but $(1,\sqrt2)\notin S$. So $S$ is not transitive.
Thus $S$ is reflexive but neither symmetric nor transitive.

questions.text: Students of a school are taken to a railway museum to learn about railways heritage and its history. An exhibit in the museum depicted many rail lines on the track near the railway station. Let L be the set of all rail lines on the railway track and R be the relation on L defined by $R = \{(l_1, l_2) : l_1 \text{ is parallel to } l_2\}$. On the basis of the above information, answer the following questions : (i) Find whether the relation R is symmetric or not. (ii) Find whether the relation R is transitive or not. (iii)(a) If one of the rail lines on the railway track is represented by the equation $y = 3x + 2$, then find the set of rail lines in R related to it.  OR  (iii)(b) Let S be the relation defined by $S = \{(l_1, l_2) : l_1 \text{ is perpendicular to } l_2\}$, check whether the relation S is symmetric and transitive.

answer.text:
(i) Let $(l_1,l_2)\in R\Rightarrow l_1\parallel l_2\Rightarrow l_2\parallel l_1\Rightarrow(l_2,l_1)\in R$, $\therefore R$ is a symmetric relation.
(ii) Let $(l_1,l_2),(l_2,l_3)\in R\Rightarrow l_1\parallel l_2,\ l_2\parallel l_3\Rightarrow l_1\parallel l_3\Rightarrow(l_1,l_3)\in R$, $\therefore R$ is a transitive relation.
(iii) The set is $\{l:l\text{ is a line of type }y=3x+c,\ c\in\mathbb{R}\}$

questions.text: A class-room teacher is keen to assess the learning of her students the concept of \"relations\" taught to them. She writes the following five relations each defined on the set $A = \{1, 2, 3\}$ : $R_1 = \{(2, 3), (3, 2)\}$; $R_2 = \{(1, 2), (1, 3), (3, 2)\}$; $R_3 = \{(1, 2), (2, 1), (1, 1)\}$; $R_4 = \{(1, 1), (1, 2), (3, 3), (2, 2)\}$; $R_5 = \{(1, 1), (1, 2), (3, 3), (2, 2), (2, 1), (2, 3), (3, 2)\}$. The students are asked to answer the following questions about the above relations : (i) Identify the relation which is reflexive, transitive but not symmetric. (ii) Identify the relation which is reflexive and symmetric but not transitive. (iii)(a) Identify the relations which are symmetric but neither reflexive nor transitive.  OR  (iii)(b) What pairs should be added to the relation $R_2$ to make it an equivalence relation ?

Let R be a relation defined over N, where N is set of natural numbers, defined as \"mRn if and only if m is a multiple of n, m, n $\in$ N.\" Find whether R is reflexive, symmetric and transitive or not.

answer.text:
Let $x\in N$. Then $x$ is a multiple of itself $\Rightarrow xRx$. Hence, $R$ is reflexive.
We have $2,8\in N$ such that $8$ is a multiple of $2\Rightarrow 8R2$. But $2$ is not a multiple of $8$, so $2$ is not $R$-related to $8$. Therefore, $R$ is not symmetric.
Let $x,y,z\in N$ such that $xRy,\ yRz$. Then $x=my,\ y=nz$ for some $m,n\in N\Rightarrow x=mnz\Rightarrow x=pz$, where $p=mn\in N$. Hence $xRz$. Therefore, $R$ is transitive.

questions.text: A school is organizing a debate competition with participants as speakers $S = \{S_1, S_2, S_3, S_4\}$ and these are judged by judges $J = \{J_1, J_2, J_3\}$. Each speaker can be assigned one judge. Let R be a relation from set S to J defined as $R = \{(x, y) : \text{speaker } x \text{ is judged by judge } y, x \in S, y \in J\}$. Based on the above, answer the following : (i) How many relations can be there from S to J ? (ii) A student identifies a function from S to J as $f = \{(S_1, J_1), (S_2, J_2), (S_3, J_3), (S_4, J_1)\}$. Check if it is bijective. (iii)(a) How many one-one functions can be there from set S to set J ?  OR  (iii)(b) Another student considers a relation $R_1 = \{(S_1, S_2), (S_2, S_4)\}$ in set S. Write minimum ordered pairs to be included in $R_1$ so that $R_1$ is reflexive but not symmetric.

answer.text:
(i) The number of relations $=2^{4\times3}=2^{12}$
(ii) Since $S_2$ and $S_3$ have been assigned the same judge $J_2$, the function is not one-one. Hence, it is not bijective.
(iii)(a) There cannot exist any one-one function from $S$ to $J$ as $n(S)>n(J)$. Hence, the number of one-one functions from $S$ to $J$ is $0$.

questions.text: If $f : \mathbb{R}^+ \to \mathbb{R}$ is defined as $f(x) = \log_a x$ $(a > 0$ and $a \neq 1)$, prove that $f$ is a bijection. ($\mathbb{R}^+$ is a set of all positive real numbers.)

answer.text:
$f(x)=\log_a x\ (a>0,\ a\neq1)$
Let $x_1,x_2\in R^+$ such that $f(x_1)=f(x_2)\Rightarrow\log_a x_1=\log_a x_2\Rightarrow x_1=x_2\Rightarrow f$ is one-one.
Let $f(x)=y\Rightarrow\log_a x=y\Rightarrow a^y=x$
$\therefore$ for every $y\in R$, there exists $x\in R^+$; hence $f$ is onto.
$\therefore f$ is a bijection.

questions.text: Show that the function $f : N \to N$, where N is a set of natural numbers, given by $f(n) = \begin{cases} n - 1, & \text{if n is even} \\ n + 1, & \text{if n is odd} \end{cases}$ is a bijection.

answer.text:
Let $f(x)=f(y)$. Let $x$ and $y$ be both odd or both even. Then either $x+1=y+1$ or $x-1=y-1$, giving $x=y$.
The case $x$ odd and $y$ even is rejected: $x+1=y-1$ gives $x-y=-2$, not possible as an odd and an even number cannot differ by $2$. Hence $f$ is one-one.
For onto: Let $f(x)=y$ gives $x=y+1$ or $x=y-1$. If $y$ is odd, $x$ is even and if $y$ is even, $x$ is odd. Range $=N=$ co-domain, hence $f$ is onto.
As $f$ is both one-one and onto, hence $f$ is a bijection.

questions.text: Let $f : A \to B$ be defined by $f(x) = \dfrac{x - 2}{x - 3}$, where $A = \mathbb{R} - \{3\}$ and $B = \mathbb{R} - \{1\}$. Discuss the bijectivity of the function.

answer.text:
Let $x_1,x_2\in A$ such that $f(x_1)=f(x_2)\Rightarrow\dfrac{x_1-2}{x_1-3}=\dfrac{x_2-2}{x_2-3}\Rightarrow x_1=x_2$, $\therefore f$ is one-one.
For each $y\in B$, there exists $x=\dfrac{3y-2}{y-1}\in R-\{3\}$ such that $f(x)=y$, $\therefore f$ is onto.
$\Rightarrow f$ is one-one and onto, i.e. $f$ is a bijective function.

questions.text: Show that the function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ defined by $f(x) = 4x^3 - 5$, $\forall\,x \in \mathbb{R}$ is one-one and onto.

answer.text:
One-One: Let $x_1,x_2\in R$ such that $f(x_1)=f(x_2)\Rightarrow4x_1^3-5=4x_2^3-5\Rightarrow x_1^3=x_2^3\Rightarrow x_1=x_2$, $\therefore f$ is one-one.
Onto: $x\in R\ (D_f)\Rightarrow x^3\in R\Rightarrow4x^3-5\in R\Rightarrow f(x)\in R$, $\therefore R_f=$ co-domain$(f)$, $\therefore f$ is an onto function.
$\Rightarrow f$ is one-one and onto both.

questions.text: Let R be a relation defined on a set N of natural numbers such that $R = \{(x, y) : xy \text{ is a square of a natural number}, x, y \in N\}$. Determine if the relation R is an equivalence relation.

answer.text:
Reflexive: For any $x\in N$, $x\cdot x=x^2$, which is the square of the natural number $x\Rightarrow(x,x)\in R$. $\therefore R$ is a reflexive relation.
Symmetric: Let $(x,y)\in R\Rightarrow xy$ is a square of a natural number $\Rightarrow yx$ is a square of a natural number (since $xy=yx$) $\Rightarrow(y,x)\in R$. $\therefore R$ is a symmetric relation.
Transitive: Let $(x,y),(y,z)\in R\Rightarrow xy=a^2,\ yz=b^2$ for some $a,b\in N$. $\therefore\dfrac{a^2}{y}=x,\ \dfrac{b^2}{y}=z\in N\Rightarrow xz=\dfrac{a^2}{y}\cdot\dfrac{b^2}{y}=\left(\dfrac{ab}{y}\right)^2$, where $\dfrac{ab}{y}\in N\Rightarrow(x,z)\in R$. $\therefore R$ is a transitive relation.
Hence, $R$ is an equivalence relation.

questions.text: A relation R is defined on Z, the set of integers, as $R = \{(x, y) : |x - y| \text{ is divisible by a prime number '}p\text{'}, x, y \in Z\}$. Check whether R is an equivalence relation or not.

answer.text: Let $x\in\mathbb{Z}$. Then $|x-x|=0$, which is divisible by the prime $p$, so $(x,x)\in R$; thus $R$ is reflexive. Let $(x,y)\in R$, so $|x-y|$ is divisible by $p$; since $|x-y|=|y-x|$, $(y,x)\in R$; thus $R$ is symmetric. Let $(x,y),(y,z)\in R$, so $|x-y|$ and $|y-z|$ are divisible by $p$; then $(x-y)+(y-z)=x-z$ is divisible by $p$, so $|x-z|$ is divisible by $p$ and $(x,z)\in R$; thus $R$ is transitive. Since $R$ is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, $R$ is an equivalence relation.

questions.text: A function $f : \mathbb{R} - \left\{\dfrac{3}{5}\right\} \to \mathbb{R} - \left\{\dfrac{3}{5}\right\}$ is defined as $f(x) = \dfrac{3x + 2}{5x - 3}$. Show that $f$ is one-one and onto.

answer.text: Let $x_1,x_2\in\mathbb{R}-\left\{\dfrac{3}{5}\right\}$ with $f(x_1)=f(x_2)$: $\dfrac{3x_1+2}{5x_1-3}=\dfrac{3x_2+2}{5x_2-3}\Rightarrow 15x_1x_2-9x_1+10x_2-6=15x_1x_2+10x_1-9x_2-6\Rightarrow x_1=x_2$. Hence $f$ is one-one. For $y\in\mathbb{R}-\left\{\dfrac{3}{5}\right\}$, solving $\dfrac{3x+2}{5x-3}=y$ gives $x=\dfrac{3y+2}{5y-3}\in\mathbb{R}-\left\{\dfrac{3}{5}\right\}$, and $f\!\left(\dfrac{3y+2}{5y-3}\right)=y$. Hence $f$ is onto. Therefore $f$ is one-one and onto.

questions.text: (a) Check whether $f : \mathbb{R} - \{3\} \to \mathbb{R}$ defined as $f(x) = \dfrac{x - 2}{x - 3}$ is onto or not. (b) Check whether $f : Z \times Z \times Z \to Z$ (where Z is the set of integers) defined as $f(x, y) = (2y, 3x)$ is injective or not.

answer.text: $f:\mathbb{R}-\{3\}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=\dfrac{x-2}{x-3}$. Let $y=\dfrac{x-2}{x-3}\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{3y-2}{y-1}$, which requires $y\neq 1$. So the range $R_f=\mathbb{R}-\{1\}\neq\mathbb{R}$ (the codomain). Hence $f$ is not onto.

questions.text: Show that $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ defined as $f(x) = \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1 + x^2}}$ is one-one but not onto.

answer.text: $f(x)=\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1+x^2}}$. One-one: $f(x_1)=f(x_2)\Rightarrow x_1^2(1+x_2^2)=x_2^2(1+x_1^2)\Rightarrow x_1^2=x_2^2\Rightarrow x_1=x_2$ (both of the same sign, rejecting $x_1=-x_2$). Onto: $y=\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1+x^2}}\Rightarrow x=\pm\sqrt{\dfrac{y^2}{1-y^2}}$, defined only for $y\in(-1,1)$, so the range is $(-1,1)\neq\mathbb{R}$ (the codomain). Hence $f$ is one-one but not onto.

questions.text: Let $A = \mathbb{R} - \{3\}$ and $B = \mathbb{R} - \{1\}$. A function $f : A \to B$ is defined by $f(x) = \left(\dfrac{x - 2}{x - 3}\right)$. Find whether $f$ is one-one and onto.

answer.text: $f:\mathbb{R}-\{3\}\to\mathbb{R}-\{1\}$, $f(x)=\dfrac{x-2}{x-3}$. One-one: $f(a)=f(b)\Rightarrow(a-2)(b-3)=(b-2)(a-3)\Rightarrow a=b$. Onto: $y=\dfrac{x-2}{x-3}\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{3y-2}{y-1}$, defined for all $y\neq 1$, so the range is $\mathbb{R}-\{1\}$, the codomain. Hence $f$ is both one-one and onto (bijective).

questions.text: Let $n$ be a fixed positive integer. A relation R is defined in set Z such that $R = \{(x, y) : (x - y) \text{ is divisible by } n,\ \forall\, x, y \in Z\}$. Determine if R is an equivalence relation.

answer.text: $R=\{(x,y):(x-y)\text{ is divisible by }n\}$ on $\mathbb{Z}$. Reflexive: $x-x=0$ is divisible by $n$. Symmetric: $x-y=np\Rightarrow y-x=n(-p)$ is divisible by $n$. Transitive: $x-y=np$ and $y-z=nr\Rightarrow x-z=n(p+r)$ is divisible by $n$. Hence $R$ is an equivalence relation.

They select the student participants on the basis of an essay writing competition. 7 students out of 80 are selected for the project and are categorized into two sets such that : Girl students belong to Set $A = \{G_1, G_2, G_3, G_4\}$, Boy students belong to Set $B = \{B_1, B_2, B_3\}$. Based on the above information, answer the following questions : (i) How many relations are possible from Set $A \to$ Set $B$ ? (ii) Let R be a relation from $A \to B$ such that $R = \{(G_1, B_1), (G_2, B_2), (G_3, B_2), (G_4, B_3), (G_1, B_2)\}$. Is R an injective function ? Justify your answer. (iii)(a) Let the relation R from $A \to A$ be such that $R = \{(x, y),\ x, y \in A,\ x \text{ and } y \text{ are students from the same colony in the city}\}$. Verify if R is an equivalence relation.  OR  (iii)(b) Verify if any function $f : B \to A$ is bijective. Give reason to support your answer.

answer.text: Set $A=\{G_1,G_2,G_3,G_4\}$ ($n=4$) and $B=\{B_1,B_2,B_3\}$ ($n=3$). (i) The number of relations from $A$ to $B$ is $2^{4\times 3}=2^{12}=4096$. (ii) $R=\{(G_1,B_1),(G_2,B_2),(G_3,B_2),(G_4,B_3),(G_1,B_2)\}$ is not an injective function; in fact it is not a function at all, since $G_1$ has two images $B_1$ and $B_2$. (iii)(a) The relation ``$x$ and $y$ are students from the same colony'' is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, hence an equivalence relation. OR (iii)(b) No function $f:B\to A$ can be bijective, because $n(B)=3<n(A)=4$, so $f$ cannot be onto (surjective).

questions.text: A relation R defined on set $A = \{1, 2, 3\}$ is $R = \{(1, 1), (3, 3), (1, 2)\}$. Check whether R is an equivalence relation. Verify. Write the smallest relation $R_1$ such that $R \cup R_1$ becomes an equivalence relation on $A = \{1, 2, 3\}$.

answer.text: $R=\{(1,1),(3,3),(1,2)\}$ on $A=\{1,2,3\}$. Since $(1,2)\in R$ but $(2,1)\notin R$, $R$ is not symmetric. For $R\cup R_1$ to be an equivalence relation it must be reflexive and symmetric, so we must include $(2,2)$ and $(2,1)$. The smallest such $R_1=\{(2,2),(2,1)\}$.

answer.text:
$\text{LHS}=f(\alpha)f(-\beta)=\begin{bmatrix}\cos\alpha&-\sin\alpha&0\\\sin\alpha&\cos\alpha&0\\0&0&1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\cos\beta&\sin\beta&0\\-\sin\beta&\cos\beta&0\\0&0&1\end{bmatrix}$
$=\begin{bmatrix}\cos\alpha\cos\beta+\sin\alpha\sin\beta&\cos\alpha\sin\beta-\sin\alpha\cos\beta&0\\\sin\alpha\cos\beta-\cos\alpha\sin\beta&\sin\alpha\sin\beta+\cos\alpha\cos\beta&0\\0&0&1\end{bmatrix}$

answer.text:
$|A|=1+\cot^2 x=\csc^2 x$; \ $\operatorname{adj}A=\begin{bmatrix}1&-\cot x\\\cot x&1\end{bmatrix}$
$A^{-1}=\dfrac{\operatorname{adj}A}{|A|}=\dfrac{1}{\csc^2 x}\begin{bmatrix}1&-\cot x\\\cot x&1\end{bmatrix}$; \ $A'=\begin{bmatrix}1&-\cot x\\\cot x&1\end{bmatrix}$
$A'A^{-1}=\dfrac{1}{\csc^2 x}\begin{bmatrix}1-\cot^2 x&-2\cot x\\2\cot x&1-\cot^2 x\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}\sin^2 x-\cos^2 x&-2\sin x\cos x\\2\sin x\cos x&\sin^2 x-\cos^2 x\end{bmatrix}$
$=\begin{bmatrix}-\cos2x&-\sin2x\\\sin2x&-\cos2x\end{bmatrix}$

answer.text:
Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}50&60&35\\40&45&50\end{bmatrix}$ (Day I, Day II) and $B=\begin{bmatrix}150\\175\\180\end{bmatrix}$ be the day-wise sale and the selling price per subject, respectively.
Total sales day-wise $=\begin{bmatrix}50&60&35\\40&45&50\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}150\\175\\180\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}24{,}300\\22{,}875\end{bmatrix}$ (Day I, Day II)
Total sales in two days $=$ ₹$24{,}300+$ ₹$22{,}875=$ ₹$47{,}175$
Profit $=$ ₹$47{,}175-$ ₹$35{,}000=$ ₹$12{,}175$

answer.text: Let $S=\begin{bmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{bmatrix}$. With $P=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1\\3&4\end{bmatrix}$, $Q=\begin{bmatrix}5&2\\7&4\end{bmatrix}$, $R=\begin{bmatrix}2&5\\3&8\end{bmatrix}$: $PQ=\begin{bmatrix}3&0\\43&22\end{bmatrix}$. $PQ-RS=O\Rightarrow RS=PQ\Rightarrow S=R^{-1}(PQ)=\begin{bmatrix}8&-5\\-3&2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}3&0\\43&22\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-191&-110\\77&44\end{bmatrix}$.

questions.text: If $A = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 2 \\ 5 & -7 \end{bmatrix}$, then find $A^{-1}$ and use it to solve the following system of equations : $3x + 5y = 11$, $2x - 7y = -3$.

answer.text:
$\operatorname{adj}A=\begin{bmatrix}-7&-2\\-5&3\end{bmatrix}$, \ $|A|=-31$, \ $A^{-1}=\dfrac{-1}{31}\begin{bmatrix}-7&-2\\-5&3\end{bmatrix}$
Given system of equations is $\begin{bmatrix}3&5\\2&-7\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}11\\-3\end{bmatrix}$, which is $A'X=B$
$\Rightarrow X=(A')^{-1}B=(A^{-1})'B=\dfrac{-1}{31}\begin{bmatrix}-7&-5\\-2&3\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}11\\-3\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2\\1\end{bmatrix}$
$\therefore x=2,\ y=1$

Solve the following system of equations by matrix method : $x + 2y + 3z = 6$, $2x - y + z = 2$, $3x + 2y - 2z = 3$.

answer.text:
Given system is $\begin{bmatrix}1&2&3\\2&-1&1\\3&2&-2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}6\\2\\3\end{bmatrix}$
$AX=B\Rightarrow X=A^{-1}B$; \ $|A|=35\neq0$
$A_{11}=0,\ A_{12}=7,\ A_{13}=7$; \ $A_{21}=10,\ A_{22}=-11,\ A_{23}=4$; \ $A_{31}=5,\ A_{32}=5,\ A_{33}=-5$
$\therefore\ A^{-1}=\dfrac{1}{35}\begin{bmatrix}0&10&5\\7&-11&5\\7&4&-5\end{bmatrix}$
$\Rightarrow X=\dfrac{1}{35}\begin{bmatrix}0&10&5\\7&-11&5\\7&4&-5\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}6\\2\\3\end{bmatrix}=\dfrac{1}{35}\begin{bmatrix}35\\35\\35\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1\\1\\1\end{bmatrix}$
$\therefore\ x=1,\ y=1,\ z=1$

answer.text:
$AB=\begin{bmatrix}1&0&0\\0&1&0\\0&0&1\end{bmatrix}=I\Rightarrow B^{-1}=A$
The given system of equations can be written as $B^{T}X=C$, $X=\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}$, $C=\begin{bmatrix}3\\2\\3\end{bmatrix}$
$X=(B^{T})^{-1}C=(B^{-1})^{T}C=A^{T}C$
$\Rightarrow X=\begin{bmatrix}-3&2&2\\-2&1&1\\-4&2&3\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}3\\2\\3\end{bmatrix}\Rightarrow\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1\\-1\\1\end{bmatrix}\therefore x=1,\ y=-1,\ z=1$

Find the inverse of the matrix $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & -2 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$. Using the inverse, $A^{-1}$, solve the system of linear equations $x - y + 2z = 8$; $2y - 3z = 1$; $3x - 2y + 4z = 3$.

answer.text:
$A=\begin{bmatrix}1&-1&2\\0&2&-3\\3&-2&4\end{bmatrix}$; \ $|A|=1(8-6)+1(0+9)+2(0-6)=-1\neq0$, $\therefore A$ is invertible.
$\operatorname{adj}A=\begin{bmatrix}2&0&-1\\-9&-2&3\\-6&-1&2\end{bmatrix}\Rightarrow A^{-1}=\dfrac{1}{|A|}\operatorname{adj}A=\begin{bmatrix}-2&0&1\\9&2&-3\\6&1&-2\end{bmatrix}$
The given system can be written as $AX=B$, where $X=\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}$, $B=\begin{bmatrix}1\\1\\3\end{bmatrix}$
$\Rightarrow X=A^{-1}B=\begin{bmatrix}-2&0&1\\9&2&-3\\6&1&-2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1\\1\\3\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1\\2\\1\end{bmatrix}\therefore x=1,\ y=2,\ z=1$

questions.text: If $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$, find $A^{-1}$ and use it to solve the following system of equations : $x - 2y = 10$, $2x - y - z = 8$, $-2y + z = 7$.

answer.text:
$|A|=1\neq0$, hence $A^{-1}$ exists.
$\operatorname{Adj}A=\begin{bmatrix}-3&2&2\\-2&1&1\\-4&2&3\end{bmatrix}$, \ $A^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}-3&2&2\\-2&1&1\\-4&2&3\end{bmatrix}$
$AX=B\Rightarrow\begin{bmatrix}1&-2&0\\2&-1&-1\\0&-2&1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}10\\8\\7\end{bmatrix}$
$X=A^{-1}B=\begin{bmatrix}-3&2&2\\-2&1&1\\-4&2&3\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}10\\8\\7\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0\\-5\\-3\end{bmatrix}$
$\Rightarrow x=0,\ y=-5,\ z=-3$

questions.text: If $A = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & a & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & x \\ 3 & 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$ and $A^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 & 1 \\ -8 & 7 & -5 \\ b & y & 3 \end{bmatrix}$, find the value of $(a + x) - (b + y)$.

answer.text:
$AA^{-1}=I$
$\begin{bmatrix}-1&a&2\\1&2&x\\3&1&1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1&-1&1\\-8&7&-5\\b&y&3\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1&0&0\\0&1&0\\0&0&1\end{bmatrix}$
$-5+b=0\Rightarrow b=5$; \ $5-5a=0\Rightarrow a=1$
$4+y=0\Rightarrow y=-4$; \ $3x-9=0\Rightarrow x=3$
$\therefore\ (a+x)-(b+y)=(1+3)-(5-4)=3$

$A^{-1}=\dfrac{\operatorname{adj}A}{|A|}=\dfrac{1}{1200}\begin{bmatrix}75&150&75\\110&-100&30\\72&0&-24\end{bmatrix}$

In all, 50 students were given the scholarships and monthly expenditure incurred by the school on scholarships was Rs. 1,80,000. Based on the above information, answer the following questions : (i) Express the given information algebraically using matrices. answer.text:
$|A|=1(6)-2(3)-3(4)=-12\neq0$, $\therefore\ A^{-1}$ exists.
$\operatorname{adj}A=\begin{bmatrix}6&-6&-6\\-3&3&-3\\4&0&-4\end{bmatrix}$, \ $A^{-1}=-\dfrac{1}{12}\begin{bmatrix}6&-6&-6\\-3&3&-3\\4&0&-4\end{bmatrix}$

$X=A^{-1}B=-\dfrac{1}{12}\begin{bmatrix}6&-6&-6\\-3&3&-3\\4&0&-4\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1\\2\\3\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2\\[2pt]\frac12\\[2pt]\frac23\end{bmatrix}$
$\therefore\ x=2,\ y=\dfrac12,\ z=\dfrac23$

questions.text: Find the product of the matrices $\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 2 & 3 & 2 \\ 3 & -3 & -4 \end{bmatrix}$ and $\begin{bmatrix} -6 & 17 & 13 \\ 14 & 5 & -8 \\ -15 & 9 & -1 \end{bmatrix}$ and hence solve the system of linear equations : $x + 2y - 3z = -4$, $2x + 3y + 2z = 2$, $3x - 3y - 4z = 11$.

answer.text:
$\begin{bmatrix}1&2&-3\\2&3&2\\3&-3&-4\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}-6&17&13\\14&5&-8\\-15&9&-1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}67&0&0\\0&67&0\\0&0&67\end{bmatrix}=67I$
$\Rightarrow\begin{bmatrix}1&2&-3\\2&3&2\\3&-3&-4\end{bmatrix}^{-1}=\dfrac{1}{67}\begin{bmatrix}-6&17&13\\14&5&-8\\-15&9&-1\end{bmatrix}$
$\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}=\dfrac{1}{67}\begin{bmatrix}-6&17&13\\14&5&-8\\-15&9&-1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}-4\\2\\11\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3\\-2\\1\end{bmatrix}\Rightarrow x=3,\ y=-2,\ z=1$

questions.text: A school wants to allocate students into three clubs : Sports, Music and Drama, under following conditions : (a) The number of students in Sports club should be equal to the sum of the number of students in Music and Drama clubs. (b) The number of students in Music club should be 20 more than half the number of students in Sports club. (c) The total number of students to be allocated in all three clubs are 180. Find the number of students allocated to different clubs, using matrix method.

answer.text:
Let $x,y,z$ be the number of students allocated to Sports, Music and Drama clubs respectively.
Here $x=y+z,\ y=\dfrac{x}{2}+20,\ x+y+z=180\Rightarrow x-y-z=0,\ x-2y=-40,\ x+y+z=180$
$AX=B$ where $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&-1&-1\\1&-2&0\\1&1&1\end{bmatrix}$, $B=\begin{bmatrix}0\\-40\\180\end{bmatrix}$, $X=\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}$
$|A|=-4\neq0\Rightarrow A^{-1}$ exists; $\operatorname{adj}A=\begin{bmatrix}-2&0&-2\\-1&2&-1\\3&-2&-1\end{bmatrix}$
$A^{-1}=\dfrac{1}{|A|}\operatorname{adj}A=\dfrac14\begin{bmatrix}2&0&2\\1&-2&1\\-3&2&1\end{bmatrix}$
$X=A^{-1}B=\dfrac14\begin{bmatrix}2&0&2\\1&-2&1\\-3&2&1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}0\\-40\\180\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}90\\65\\25\end{bmatrix}$
$\therefore$ Number of students allocated in Sports, Music and Drama are $90,\ 65$ and $25$ respectively.

questions.text: Given $A = \begin{bmatrix} -4 & 4 & 4 \\ -7 & 1 & 3 \\ 5 & -3 & -1 \end{bmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & -2 & -2 \\ 2 & 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$, find $AB$. Hence, solve the system of linear equations : $x - y + z = 4$, $x - 2y - 2z = 9$, $2x + y + 3z = 1$.

answer.text:
$AB=\begin{bmatrix}8&0&0\\0&8&0\\0&0&8\end{bmatrix}=8I$
The system of equations is equivalent to the matrix equation $BX=C$, where $C=\begin{bmatrix}4\\9\\1\end{bmatrix},\ X=\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}$
$\Rightarrow X=B^{-1}C$. Since $AB=8I\Rightarrow B^{-1}=\dfrac18A$
$X=\dfrac18\begin{bmatrix}-4&4&4\\-7&1&3\\5&-3&-1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}4\\9\\1\end{bmatrix}=\dfrac18\begin{bmatrix}24\\-16\\-8\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3\\-2\\-1\end{bmatrix}$
$\therefore x=3,\ y=-2,\ z=-1$

questions.text: If $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 0 \\ -2 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$, then find $A^{-1}$. Hence, solve the system of linear equations : $x - 2y = 10$, $2x - y - z = 8$, $-2y + z = 7$.

answer.text:
$|A|=1\neq0\Rightarrow A^{-1}$ exists.
$\operatorname{adj}A=\begin{bmatrix}-3&-2&-4\\2&1&2\\2&1&3\end{bmatrix}$
$A^{-1}=\dfrac{1}{|A|}\operatorname{adj}A=\begin{bmatrix}-3&-2&-4\\2&1&2\\2&1&3\end{bmatrix}$
The given system is equivalent to $A^TX=B$, where $B=\begin{bmatrix}10\\8\\7\end{bmatrix},\ X=\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}$
$\Rightarrow X=(A^T)^{-1}B=(A^{-1})^TB=\begin{bmatrix}-3&2&2\\-2&1&1\\-4&2&3\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}10\\8\\7\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0\\-5\\-3\end{bmatrix}$
$\therefore x=0,\ y=-5,\ z=-3$

questions.text: A furniture workshop produces three types of furniture — chairs, tables and beds each day. On a particular day the total number of furniture pieces produced is 45. It was also found that production of beds exceeds that of chairs by 8, while the total production of beds and chairs together is twice the production of tables. Determine the units produced of each type of furniture, using matrix method.

answer.text:
Let the numbers of chairs, tables and beds produced be $x,y,z$ respectively.
$\therefore x+y+z=45;\ -x+0\cdot y+z=8;\ x-2y+z=0$
$A=\begin{bmatrix}1&1&1\\-1&0&1\\1&-2&1\end{bmatrix},\ X=\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix},\ B=\begin{bmatrix}45\\8\\0\end{bmatrix}$
$|A|=1(0+2)-1(-1-1)+1(2-0)=6\neq0\Rightarrow A^{-1}$ exists
$AX=B\Rightarrow X=A^{-1}B$
$\operatorname{adj}(A)=\begin{bmatrix}2&-3&1\\2&0&-2\\2&3&1\end{bmatrix},\ A^{-1}=\dfrac16\begin{bmatrix}2&-3&1\\2&0&-2\\2&3&1\end{bmatrix}$
$\therefore\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}=\dfrac16\begin{bmatrix}2&-3&1\\2&0&-2\\2&3&1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}45\\8\\0\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}11\\15\\19\end{bmatrix}$
So $x=11,\ y=15,\ z=19$. Hence the numbers of chairs, tables and beds produced are $11,\ 15$ and $19$ respectively.

questions.text: Let $2x + 5y - 1 = 0$ and $3x + 2y - 7 = 0$ represent the equations of two lines on which the ants are moving on the ground. Using matrix method, find a point common to the paths of the ants.

answer.text:
The system of equations in matrices is $AX=B$, where $A=\begin{bmatrix}2&5\\3&2\end{bmatrix},\ X=\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\end{bmatrix},\ B=\begin{bmatrix}1\\7\end{bmatrix}$
The solution is $X=A^{-1}B\Rightarrow\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\end{bmatrix}=\dfrac{-1}{11}\begin{bmatrix}2&-5\\-3&2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1\\7\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3\\-1\end{bmatrix}$
Point common to the paths of the ants is $(3,-1)$.

questions.text: If $A = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 2 & 1 \\ -2 & -1 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$, find $A^{-1}$ and use it to solve the following system of equations : $-2y + z = 7$, $2x - y - z = 8$, $x - 2y = 10$.

answer.text: $A=\begin{bmatrix}0&2&1\\-2&-1&-2\\1&-1&0\end{bmatrix}$. $|A|=-2(2)+1(3)=-1\neq 0$. $\operatorname{adj}A=\begin{bmatrix}-2&-1&-3\\-2&-1&-2\\3&2&4\end{bmatrix}$, so $A^{-1}=\dfrac{1}{|A|}\operatorname{adj}A=\begin{bmatrix}2&1&3\\2&1&2\\-3&-2&-4\end{bmatrix}$. The system $-2y+z=7,\ 2x-y-z=8,\ x-2y=10$ is $A^{T}X=B$ with $X=\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}$, $B=\begin{bmatrix}7\\8\\10\end{bmatrix}$. Then $X=(A^{T})^{-1}B=(A^{-1})^{T}B=\begin{bmatrix}2&2&-3\\1&1&-2\\3&2&-4\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}7\\8\\10\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0\\-5\\-3\end{bmatrix}$. Hence $x=0,\ y=-5,\ z=-3$.

questions.text: If $\begin{bmatrix} 3 & -1 & \sin 2x \\ -7 & 4 & \cos 2x \\ -11 & 7 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$ is a singular matrix, then find all values of $x$ where $x \in \left[0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$.

answer.text: The matrix $\begin{bmatrix}3&-1&\sin 3x\\-7&4&\cos 2x\\-11&7&2\end{bmatrix}$ is singular, so its determinant is $0$: $2\cos 2x+\sin 3x=2\Rightarrow 4\sin^3 x+4\sin^2 x-3\sin x=0\Rightarrow \sin x\,(4\sin^2 x+4\sin x-3)=0\Rightarrow \sin x\,(2\sin x-1)(2\sin x+3)=0$. For $x\in\left[0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$, this gives $x=0,\ \dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

If $P = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$ and $Q = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 2 & -4 \\ -4 & 2 & -4 \\ 2 & -1 & 5 \end{bmatrix}$, find $(QP)$ and hence solve the following system of equations using matrices : $x - y = 3$, $2x + 3y + 4z = 17$, $y + 2z = 7$.

answer.text: $QP=\begin{bmatrix}6&0&0\\0&6&0\\0&0&6\end{bmatrix}=6I$, so $P^{-1}=\dfrac{1}{6}Q$. The system $x-y=3,\ 2x+3y+4z=17,\ y+2z=7$ is $PX=R$ with $X=\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}$, $R=\begin{bmatrix}3\\17\\7\end{bmatrix}$. Then $X=P^{-1}R=\dfrac{1}{6}QR=\dfrac{1}{6}\begin{bmatrix}2&2&-4\\-4&2&-4\\2&-1&5\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}3\\17\\7\end{bmatrix}=\dfrac{1}{6}\begin{bmatrix}12\\-6\\24\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2\\-1\\4\end{bmatrix}$, so $x=2,\ y=-1,\ z=4$.

questions.text: Obtain the value of $\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} 1 + x & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 + y & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 + z \end{vmatrix}$ in terms of $x$, $y$ and $z$. Further, if $\Delta = 0$ and $x$, $y$, $z$ are non-zero real numbers, prove that $x^{-1} + y^{-1} + z^{-1} = -1$.

answer.text: $\Delta=\begin{vmatrix}1+x&1&1\\1&1+y&1\\1&1&1+z\end{vmatrix}=(1+x)(1+y+z+yz-1)-z-y=xy+yz+zx+xyz$. If $\Delta=0$ then $xy+yz+zx=-xyz$; dividing both sides by $xyz$ gives $\dfrac{1}{x}+\dfrac{1}{y}+\dfrac{1}{z}=-1$, i.e. $x^{-1}+y^{-1}+z^{-1}=-1$.

questions.text: On the inauguration day of a new showroom, a lucky draw was organized and some vouchers of Rs. 1,000 and Rs. 500 were given to the lucky draw winners. On that day, a total of 60 vouchers were given. Adding the number of Rs. 1,000 vouchers to 3 times the number of Rs. 500 vouchers gives 100. Express the given information as a system of linear equations in two variables. Hence, find the number of each type of vouchers using matrix method.

answer.text: Let $x$ be the number of ₹$1000$ vouchers and $y$ the number of ₹$500$ vouchers. Then $x+y=60$ and $x+3y=100$. In matrix form $AX=B$ with $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&1\\1&3\end{bmatrix}$, $X=\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\end{bmatrix}$, $B=\begin{bmatrix}60\\100\end{bmatrix}$. $|A|=2\neq 0$, $A^{-1}=\dfrac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix}3&-1\\-1&1\end{bmatrix}$, so $X=A^{-1}B=\dfrac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix}3&-1\\-1&1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}60\\100\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}40\\20\end{bmatrix}$. Hence there are $40$ vouchers of ₹$1000$ and $20$ of ₹$500$.

answer.text: Let an apple cost ₹$x$, an orange ₹$y$ and a banana ₹$z$: $4x+3y+2z=60$, $2x+4y+6z=90$, $6x+2y+3z=70$. With $A=\begin{bmatrix}4&3&2\\2&4&6\\6&2&3\end{bmatrix}$, $|A|=50\neq 0$, so $A^{-1}$ exists. $\operatorname{adj}A=\begin{bmatrix}0&-5&10\\30&0&-20\\-20&10&10\end{bmatrix}$, and $X=A^{-1}B=\dfrac{1}{50}(\operatorname{adj}A)B=\begin{bmatrix}5\\8\\8\end{bmatrix}$. Hence an apple costs ₹$5$, an orange ₹$8$ and a banana ₹$8$.

questions.text: If $f(x) = \begin{cases} ax + b, & 0 < x \leq 1 \\ 2x^2 - x, & 1 < x < 2 \end{cases}$ is a differentiable function in $(0, 2)$, then find the values of $a$ and $b$.

answer.text:
$f(x)$ is differentiable in $(0,2)\Rightarrow f(x)$ is continuous on $(0,2)$
$\Rightarrow f(x)$ is continuous at $x=1$: $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to1^-}(ax+b)=\lim_{x\to1^+}(2x^2-x)\Rightarrow a+b=1$
Also $f(x)$ is differentiable at $x=1$: $\text{L.H.D.}(x=1)=\text{R.H.D.}(x=1)$
$\Rightarrow a=4(1)-1\therefore a=3$ & $b=1-a=-2$

questions.text: If $(x^2 + y^2)^2 = xy$, then find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$.

answer.text:
$(x^2+y^2)^2=xy$ gives $2(x^2+y^2)\left[2x+2y\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right]=x\dfrac{dy}{dx}+y$
$\Rightarrow[4y(x^2+y^2)-x]\dfrac{dy}{dx}=y-4x(x^2+y^2)$

questions.text: Let $f(x)$ be a real valued function. Then its Left Hand Derivative (L.H.D.) : $Lf'(a) = \displaystyle\lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{f(a - h) - f(a)}{-h}$; Right Hand Derivative (R.H.D.) : $Rf'(a) = \displaystyle\lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{f(a + h) - f(a)}{h}$. Also, a function $f(x)$ is said to be differentiable at $x = a$ if its L.H.D. and R.H.D. at $x = a$ exist and both are equal. For the function $f(x) = \begin{cases} |x - 3|, & x \geq 1 \\ \dfrac{x^2}{4} - \dfrac{3x}{2} + \dfrac{13}{4}, & x < 1 \end{cases}$ answer the following questions : (i) What is R.H.D. of $f(x)$ at $x = 1$ ? (ii) What is L.H.D. of $f(x)$ at $x = 1$ ? (iii)(a) Check if the function $f(x)$ is differentiable at $x = 1$.  OR  (iii)(b) Find $f'(2)$ and $f'(-1)$.

answer.text:
(i) R.H.D. of $f(x)$ at $x=1=\displaystyle\lim_{h\to0}\dfrac{f(1+h)-f(1)}{h}=\lim_{h\to0}\dfrac{|1+h-3|-|-2|}{h}=\lim_{h\to0}\dfrac{2-h-2}{h}=-1$
(ii) L.H.D. of $f(x)$ at $x=1=\displaystyle\lim_{h\to0}\dfrac{f(1-h)-f(1)}{-h}=\lim_{h\to0}\dfrac{\left[\frac{(1-h)^2}{4}-\frac{3(1-h)}{2}+\frac{13}{4}\right]-2}{-h}=\lim_{h\to0}\dfrac{h^2+4h}{-4h}=-1$
(iii)(a) Since L.H.D. of $f(x)$ at $x=1$ is the same as R.H.D. of $f(x)$ at $x=1$, $f(x)$ is differentiable at $x=1$.

questions.text: Find the value(s) of '$\lambda$', if the function $f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{\sin^2 \lambda x}{x^2}, & \text{if } x \neq 0 \\ 1, & \text{if } x = 0 \end{cases}$ is continuous at $x = 0$.

answer.text:
$\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}f(x)=\lim_{x\to0}\dfrac{\sin^2\lambda x}{x^2}=\lim_{x\to0}\left[\dfrac{\sin^2\lambda x}{(\lambda x)^2}\cdot\lambda^2\right]=\lambda^2$
Since $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=0$, $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}f(x)=f(0)$
$\Rightarrow\ \lambda^2=1\Rightarrow\lambda=\pm1$

questions.text: Differentiate $\sec^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}\right)$ w.r.t. $\sin^{-1}\left(2x\sqrt{1 - x^2}\right)$.

answer.text:
Let $x=\sin\theta$. Then $U=\sec^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-\sin^2\theta}}\right)=\sec^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\cos\theta}\right)=\sec^{-1}(\sec\theta)=\theta=\sin^{-1}x$
$\Rightarrow\ \dfrac{dU}{dx}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$
$V=\sin^{-1}\{2\sin\theta\sqrt{1-\sin^2\theta}\}=\sin^{-1}(2\sin\theta\cos\theta)=2\theta=2\sin^{-1}x$
$\Rightarrow\ \dfrac{dV}{dx}=\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$
$\therefore\ \dfrac{dU}{dV}=\dfrac{dU/dx}{dV/dx}=\dfrac12$
(Note: if the substitution is made as $x=\cos\theta$, the answer will be $-\dfrac12$.)

questions.text: If $y = \tan x + \sec x$, then prove that $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \dfrac{\cos x}{(1 - \sin x)^2}$.

answer.text:
$y=\tan x+\sec x=\dfrac{\sin x+1}{\cos x}$
$\Rightarrow\ \dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{\cos x(\cos x)+(\sin x+1)\sin x}{\cos^2 x}=\dfrac{1+\sin x}{1-\sin^2 x}=\dfrac{1}{1-\sin x}$
$\Rightarrow\ \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=\dfrac{(1-\sin x)\cdot0-1\cdot(0-\cos x)}{(1-\sin x)^2}=\dfrac{\cos x}{(1-\sin x)^2}$

questions.text: If $\sqrt{1 - x^2} + \sqrt{1 - y^2} = a(x - y)$, prove that $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1 - y^2}{1 - x^2}}$.

answer.text:
$\sqrt{1-x^2}+\sqrt{1-y^2}=a(x-y)$; \ Put $x=\sin\theta,\ y=\sin\phi$
$\Rightarrow\cos\theta+\cos\phi=a(\sin\theta-\sin\phi)$
$\Rightarrow2\cos\!\left(\dfrac{\theta+\phi}{2}\right)\cos\!\left(\dfrac{\theta-\phi}{2}\right)=2a\sin\!\left(\dfrac{\theta-\phi}{2}\right)\cos\!\left(\dfrac{\theta+\phi}{2}\right)$
$\Rightarrow\cot\!\left(\dfrac{\theta-\phi}{2}\right)=a\Rightarrow\theta-\phi=2\cot^{-1}a\Rightarrow\sin^{-1}x-\sin^{-1}y=2\cot^{-1}a$
$\Rightarrow\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-y^2}}\dfrac{dy}{dx}=0\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\sqrt{\dfrac{1-y^2}{1-x^2}}$

If $f(x) = |\tan 2x|$, then find the value of $f'(x)$ at $x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$.

answer.text:
$f(x) = -\tan 2x$, $\dfrac{\pi}{4} < x < \dfrac{\pi}{2}$
$f'(x) = -2\sec^2 2x$, $\dfrac{\pi}{4} < x < \dfrac{\pi}{2}$
$f'\!\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = -2(-2)^2 = -8$

questions.text: If $y = \operatorname{cosec}(\cot^{-1}x)$, then prove that $\sqrt{1 + x^2}\,\dfrac{dy}{dx} - x = 0$.

answer.text:
$y = \sqrt{1 + \cot^2\left(\cot^{-1}x\right)} = \sqrt{1 + x^2}$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1 + x^2}}$
$\Rightarrow \sqrt{1 + x^2}\,\dfrac{dy}{dx} - x = 0$

questions.text: If $x = e^{\cos 3t}$ and $y = e^{\sin 3t}$, prove that $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{y\log x}{x\log y}$.
questions.topic: Derivatives of Functions in Parametric Forms

answer.text:
$\dfrac{dx}{dt} = e^{\cos 3t} \times (-\sin 3t) \times 3$
$\dfrac{dy}{dt} = e^{\sin 3t} \times (\cos 3t) \times 3$
$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\frac{dy}{dt}}{\frac{dx}{dt}} = \dfrac{e^{\sin 3t} \times (\cos 3t)}{-e^{\cos 3t} \times (\sin 3t)}$
$x = e^{\cos 3t} \Rightarrow \cos 3t = \log x$
$y = e^{\sin 3t} \Rightarrow \sin 3t = \log y$
$\therefore\ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{-y\log x}{x\log y}$

questions.text: Show that : $\dfrac{d}{dx}(|x|) = \dfrac{x}{|x|}$, $x \neq 0$.

answer.text:
$\dfrac{d(|x|)}{dx} = \dfrac{d\left(\sqrt{x^2}\right)}{dx}$, $x \neq 0$
$= \dfrac{1}{2}\left(x^2\right)^{-\frac{1}{2}} \times \dfrac{d\left(x^2\right)}{dx}$
$= \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x^2}} \cdot 2x = \dfrac{x}{|x|}$

questions.text: If $x = e^{x/y}$, prove that $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\log x - 1}{(\log x)^2}$.

answer.text:
$x=e^{x/y}\Rightarrow\log x=\dfrac{x}{y}\Rightarrow y=\dfrac{x}{\log x}$
$\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{(\log x)(1)-x\left(\dfrac1x\right)}{(\log x)^2}=\dfrac{\log x-1}{(\log x)^2}$

questions.text: Check the differentiability of $f(x) = \begin{cases} x^2 + 1, & 0 \leq x < 1 \\ 3 - x, & 1 \leq x \leq 2 \end{cases}$ at $x = 1$.

answer.text:
L.H.D. at $x=1$: $\displaystyle\lim_{h\to0}\dfrac{f(1-h)-f(1)}{-h}=\lim_{h\to0}\dfrac{[(1-h)^2+1]-2}{-h}=2$
R.H.D. at $x=1$: $\displaystyle\lim_{h\to0}\dfrac{f(1+h)-f(1)}{h}=\lim_{h\to0}\dfrac{[3-(1+h)]-2}{h}=-1$
As L.H.D. $\neq$ R.H.D., $f(x)$ is not differentiable at $x=1$.

questions.text: If $x\cos(p + y) + \cos p\sin(p + y) = 0$, prove that $\cos p\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\cos^2(p + y)$, where $p$ is a constant.

answer.text:
$x\cos(p + y) + \cos p\,\sin(p + y) = 0$
$\Rightarrow x = \dfrac{-\cos p\,\sin(p + y)}{\cos(p + y)} \Rightarrow x = -\cos p\cdot\tan(p + y)$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{dx}{dy} = -\cos p\cdot\sec^2(p + y)$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{-1}{\cos p\cdot\sec^2(p + y)}$
$\Rightarrow \cos p\,\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\cos^2(p + y)$

questions.text: Find the value of $a$ and $b$ so that function $f$ defined as $f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{x - 2}{|x - 2|} + a, & \text{if } x < 2 \\ a + b, & \text{if } x = 2 \\ \dfrac{x - 2}{|x - 2|} + b, & \text{if } x > 2 \end{cases}$ is a continuous function.

answer.text:
$f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{x - 2}{-(x - 2)} + a, & x < 2 \\ a + b, & x = 2 \\ \dfrac{x - 2}{(x - 2)} + b, & x > 2 \end{cases} \Rightarrow f(x) = \begin{cases} -1 + a, & x < 2 \\ a + b, & x = 2 \\ 1 + b, & x > 2 \end{cases}$
$\displaystyle\lim_{x \to 2^-} f(x) = -1 + a$, $\displaystyle\lim_{x \to 2^+} f(x) = 1 + b$ and $f(2) = a + b$
as $f$ is continuous at $x = 2$, $\therefore\ -1 + a = 1 + b = a + b$
$\Rightarrow a = 1,\ b = -1$

If $y = \cos^3(\sec^2 2t)$, find $\dfrac{dy}{dt}$.

answer.text:
$y=\cos^3(\sec^2 2t)$
$\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{dt}=3\cos^2(\sec^2 2t)[-\sin(\sec^2 2t)]\times\dfrac{d(\sec^2 2t)}{dt}$
$\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{dt}=-3\cos^2(\sec^2 2t)\sin(\sec^2 2t)\times2\sec2t\cdot\sec2t\tan2t\cdot2$
$\therefore\dfrac{dy}{dt}=-12\cos^2(\sec^2 2t)\times\sin(\sec^2 2t)\times\sec^2 2t\times\tan2t$

questions.text: If $x^y = e^{x - y}$, prove that $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\log x}{(1 + \log x)^2}$.

answer.text:
As $x^y=e^{x-y}\Rightarrow\log(x^y)=\log(e^{x-y})$
$\Rightarrow y\log x=(x-y)\Rightarrow y=\dfrac{x}{1+\log x}$
Now, differentiating both the sides w.r.t. $x$:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{(\log x+1)\cdot1-x\left(\frac1x\right)}{(\log x+1)^2}=\dfrac{\log x}{(1+\log x)^2}$

questions.text: Given that $y = (\sin x)^x \cdot x^{\sin x} + a^x$, find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$.

answer.text:
$y=(\sin x)^x\cdot x^{\sin x}+a^x=u+a^x\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{du}{dx}+\dfrac{d(a^x)}{dx}$
where $u=(\sin x)^x\cdot x^{\sin x}\Rightarrow\log u=x\log(\sin x)+\sin x\cdot\log x$
Differentiating both sides w.r.t. $x$:
$\dfrac{du}{dx}=(\sin x)^x\cdot x^{\sin x}\left[\log(\sin x)+x\cot x+\dfrac{\sin x}{x}+\log x\cdot\cos x\right]$
$\therefore\dfrac{dy}{dx}=(\sin x)^x\cdot x^{\sin x}\left[\log(\sin x)+x\cot x+\dfrac{\sin x}{x}+\log x\cdot\cos x\right]+a^x\log a$

questions.text: Verify whether the function $f$ defined by $f(x) = \begin{cases} x\sin\dfrac{1}{x}, & x \neq 0 \\ 0, & x = 0 \end{cases}$ is continuous at $x = 0$ or not.

answer.text:
$\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}f(x)=\lim_{x\to0}x\sin\dfrac1x=0\times(\text{finite value in }[-1,1])=0=f(0)$
$\therefore\ f$ is a continuous function at $x=0$.

questions.text: Check for differentiability of the function $f$ defined by $f(x) = |x - 5|$, at the point $x = 5$.

answer.text:
$\text{L.H.D.}=\displaystyle\lim_{x\to5^-}\dfrac{|x-5|-0}{x-5}=\lim_{x\to5^-}\dfrac{-(x-5)}{x-5}=-1$
$\text{R.H.D.}=\displaystyle\lim_{x\to5^+}\dfrac{|x-5|-0}{x-5}=\lim_{x\to5^+}\dfrac{(x-5)}{x-5}=1$
L.H.D. $\neq$ R.H.D., $\therefore\ f$ is not differentiable at $x=5$.

questions.text: Find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$, if $(\cos x)^y = (\cos y)^x$.

answer.text:
Taking log on both sides of $(\cos x)^y=(\cos y)^x$: $y\log\cos x=x\log\cos y$
$\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{dx}\log\cos x+y(-\tan x)=\log\cos y+x(-\tan y)\dfrac{dy}{dx}$
$\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{\log\cos y+y\tan x}{\log\cos x+x\tan y}$

questions.text: If $\sqrt{1 - x^2} + \sqrt{1 - y^2} = a(x - y)$, prove that $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1 - y^2}{1 - x^2}}$.

answer.text:
Let $x=\sin A,\ y=\sin B$, so $A=\sin^{-1}x,\ B=\sin^{-1}y$
$\sqrt{1-x^2}+\sqrt{1-y^2}=a(x-y)\Rightarrow\cos A+\cos B=a(\sin A-\sin B)$
$\Rightarrow2\cos\!\left(\dfrac{A+B}{2}\right)\cos\!\left(\dfrac{A-B}{2}\right)=2a\cos\!\left(\dfrac{A+B}{2}\right)\sin\!\left(\dfrac{A-B}{2}\right)$
$\Rightarrow\cot\!\left(\dfrac{A-B}{2}\right)=a\Rightarrow A-B=2\cot^{-1}a\Rightarrow\sin^{-1}x-\sin^{-1}y=2\cot^{-1}a$
Differentiating: $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-y^2}}\dfrac{dy}{dx}=0\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\sqrt{\dfrac{1-y^2}{1-x^2}}$

questions.text: If $x = a\sin^3\theta$, $y = b\cos^3\theta$, then find $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$ at $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$.

answer.text:
$\dfrac{dx}{d\theta}=3a\sin^2\theta\cos\theta$, \ $\dfrac{dy}{d\theta}=-3b\cos^2\theta\sin\theta$
$\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{-3b\cos^2\theta\sin\theta}{3a\sin^2\theta\cos\theta}=-\dfrac{b}{a}\cot\theta$
$\Rightarrow\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=\dfrac{b}{a}\csc^2\theta\cdot\dfrac{d\theta}{dx}=\dfrac{b}{a}\csc^2\theta\cdot\dfrac{1}{3a\sin^2\theta\cos\theta}=\dfrac{b}{3a^2}\sec\theta\csc^4\theta$
$\Rightarrow\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\bigg|_{\theta=\pi/4}=\dfrac{4\sqrt2\,b}{3a^2}$

questions.text: If $f(x) = |x| + |x - 1|$, then which of the following is correct ?
options: $f(x)$ is both continuous and differentiable at $x = 0$ and $x = 1$.
$f(x)$ is differentiable but not continuous at $x = 0$ and $x = 1$.
$f(x)$ is continuous but not differentiable, at $x = 0$ and $x = 1$.
$f(x)$ is neither continuous nor differentiable, at $x = 0$ and $x = 1$.

questions.text: Differentiate $2^{\cos^2 x}$ w.r.t. $\cos^2 x$.

answer.text:
Let $u=2^{\cos^2 x}\Rightarrow\dfrac{du}{dx}=2^{\cos^2 x}(-2\cos x\sin x)\log2$
Let $v=\cos^2 x\Rightarrow\dfrac{dv}{dx}=-2\cos x\sin x$
Now $\dfrac{du}{dv}=\dfrac{(du/dx)}{(dv/dx)}=2^{\cos^2 x}\log2$

questions.text: If $\tan^{-1}(x^2 + y^2) = a^2$, then find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$.

answer.text:
$\tan^{-1}(x^2+y^2)=a^2\Rightarrow x^2+y^2=\tan a^2$
Differentiating both sides w.r.t. $x$: $2x+2y\dfrac{dy}{dx}=0\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-\dfrac{x}{y}$

questions.text: If $\sqrt{1 - x^2} + \sqrt{1 - y^2} = a(x - y)$, then show that $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1 - y^2}{1 - x^2}}$.

answer.text:
Let $x=\sin A,\ y=\sin B\Rightarrow A=\sin^{-1}x,\ B=\sin^{-1}y$
$\sqrt{1-x^2}+\sqrt{1-y^2}=a(x-y)\Rightarrow\cos A+\cos B=a(\sin A-\sin B)$
$\Rightarrow2\cos\!\left(\dfrac{A+B}{2}\right)\cos\!\left(\dfrac{A-B}{2}\right)=2a\cos\!\left(\dfrac{A+B}{2}\right)\sin\!\left(\dfrac{A-B}{2}\right)$
$\Rightarrow\cot\!\left(\dfrac{A-B}{2}\right)=a\Rightarrow A-B=2\cot^{-1}a\Rightarrow\sin^{-1}x-\sin^{-1}y=2\cot^{-1}a$
Differentiating both sides w.r.t. $x$: $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-y^2}}\dfrac{dy}{dx}=0\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\sqrt{\dfrac{1-y^2}{1-x^2}}$

questions.text: If $x = a\left(\cos\theta + \log\tan\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)$ and $y = a\sin\theta$, then find $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$ at $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$.

answer.text:
$x=a\!\left(\cos\theta+\log\tan\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)$
$\Rightarrow\dfrac{dx}{d\theta}=a\!\left(-\sin\theta+\dfrac{1}{\tan\frac{\theta}{2}}\times\sec^2\dfrac{\theta}{2}\times\dfrac12\right)=a\!\left(-\sin\theta+\dfrac{1}{\sin\theta}\right)=a\!\left(\dfrac{1-\sin^2\theta}{\sin\theta}\right)=a\cot\theta\cos\theta$
Also, $y=\sin\theta\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{d\theta}=\cos\theta$; $\therefore\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{\tan\theta}{a}$
Differentiating w.r.t. $x$: $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=\dfrac{\sec^2\theta}{a}\times\dfrac{d\theta}{dx}=\dfrac{\sec^3\theta\tan\theta}{a^2}$
$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\bigg|_{\theta=\pi/4}=\dfrac{2\sqrt2}{a^2}$

questions.text: If A denotes the set of continuous functions and B denotes set of differentiable functions, then which of the following depicts the correct relation between set A and B ?
If $x = e^{x/y}$, then prove that $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x - y}{x\log x}$.

answer.text:
$x=e^{x/y}\Rightarrow\log x=\dfrac{x}{y}\Rightarrow y\log x=x$
Differentiating both sides w.r.t. $x$: $\dfrac{y}{x}+\log x\dfrac{dy}{dx}=1$
$\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{x-y}{x\log x}$

questions.text: If $f(x) = \begin{cases} 2x - 3, & -3 \leq x \leq -2 \\ x + 1, & -2 < x \leq 0 \end{cases}$. Check the differentiability of $f(x)$ at $x = -2$.

answer.text:
Here $f(-2)=2(-2)-3=-7$.
$Lf'(-2)=\displaystyle\lim_{h\to0}\dfrac{f(-2-h)-f(-2)}{-h}\ (h>0)=\lim_{h\to0}\dfrac{2(-2-h)-3-(-7)}{-h}=\lim_{h\to0}2=2$
$Rf'(-2)=\displaystyle\lim_{h\to0}\dfrac{f(-2+h)-f(-2)}{h}\ (h>0)=\lim_{h\to0}\dfrac{-2+h+1-(-7)}{h}=\lim_{h\to0}\dfrac{6+h}{h}$, which does not exist, i.e. RHD does not exist.
Therefore, the function is not differentiable at $-2$.

questions.text: If $y = \log\left(\sqrt{x} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\right)^2$, then show that $x(x + 1)^2 y_2 + (x + 1)^2 y_1 = 2$.

answer.text:
The given function can be written as $y=2\log(x+1)-\log x$
$\Rightarrow y_1=\dfrac{2}{x+1}-\dfrac1x=\dfrac{x-1}{x(x+1)}$
$\Rightarrow(x+1)y_1=\dfrac{x-1}{x}=1-\dfrac1x$
$\Rightarrow(x+1)y_2+y_1=\dfrac{1}{x^2}$
$\Rightarrow x(x+1)^2y_2+x(x+1)y_1=1+\dfrac1x$
$\Rightarrow x(x+1)^2y_2+x(x+1)y_1=1+1-(x+1)y_1$
$\Rightarrow x(x+1)^2y_2+(x+1)^2y_1=2$

questions.text: If $x\sqrt{1 + y} + y\sqrt{1 + x} = 0$, $-1 < x < 1$, $x \neq y$, then prove that $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{-1}{(1 + x)^2}$.

answer.text:
$x\sqrt{1+y}+y\sqrt{1+x}=0\Rightarrow x\sqrt{1+y}=-y\sqrt{1+x}$
$\Rightarrow x^2(1+y)=y^2(1+x)\Rightarrow(x-y)(x+y)+xy(x-y)=0\Rightarrow(x-y)(x+y+xy)=0$
$x\neq y\Rightarrow x+y+xy=0\Rightarrow y=\dfrac{-x}{1+x}$
$\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{-1}{(1+x)^2}$

answer.text: $x\dfrac{dy}{dx}$

questions.text: If $f(x) = \begin{cases} 3x - 2, & 0 < x \leq 1 \\ 2x^2 + ax, & 1 < x < 2 \end{cases}$ is continuous for $x \in (0, 2)$, then $a$ is equal to :
The function $f$ defined by $f(x) = \begin{cases} x, & \text{if } x \leq 1 \\ 5, & \text{if } x > 1 \end{cases}$ is $\textbf{\textit{not}}$ continuous at :
Find $k$ so that $f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{x^2 - 2x - 3}{x + 1}, & x \neq -1 \\ k, & x = -1 \end{cases}$ is continuous at $x = -1$.

answer.text:
$\displaystyle\lim_{x\to-1}\dfrac{x^2-2x-3}{x+1}=\lim_{x\to-1}\dfrac{(x-3)(x+1)}{x+1}=\lim_{x\to-1}(x-3)=-4$
Also, $f(-1)=k$
As $f$ is continuous, $k=-4$

questions.text: Check the differentiability of function $f(x) = x\,|x|$ at $x = 0$.

answer.text:
$f(x)=x|x|=\begin{cases}-x^2,&x\le0\\x^2,&x>0\end{cases}$
$\text{LHD}=\displaystyle\lim_{h\to0}\dfrac{f(0-h)-f(0)}{-h}=\lim_{h\to0}\dfrac{-h^2-0}{-h}=0$
$\text{RHD}=\displaystyle\lim_{h\to0}\dfrac{f(0+h)-f(0)}{h}=\lim_{h\to0}\dfrac{h^2-0}{h}=0$
Since LHD $=$ RHD, $f$ is differentiable at $x=0$.

questions.text: If $f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{\sin^2 ax}{x^2}, & x \neq 0 \\ 1, & x = 0 \end{cases}$ is continuous at $x = 0$, then the value of $a$ is :

questions.text: Differentiate $\dfrac{\sin x}{\sqrt{\cos x}}$ with respect to $x$.

answer.text:
Let $y=\dfrac{\sin x}{\sqrt{\cos x}}$
$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{\sqrt{\cos x}\cos x-\sin x\left(\frac{-\sin x}{2\sqrt{\cos x}}\right)}{\cos x}$
$\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{2\cos^2 x+\sin^2 x}{2(\cos x)^{3/2}}$ or $\dfrac{1+\cos^2 x}{2(\cos x)^{3/2}}$

questions.text: If $y = 5\cos x - 3\sin x$, prove that $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + y = 0$.

answer.text:
$y=5\cos x-3\sin x\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-5\sin x-3\cos x$
$\Rightarrow\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=-5\cos x+3\sin x=-y$
$\Rightarrow\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}+y=0$

questions.text: For a positive constant '$a$', differentiate $a^{t + \frac{1}{t}}$ with respect to $\left(t + \dfrac{1}{t}\right)^a$, where $t$ is a non-zero real number.

answer.text:
Let $u=a^{t+\frac1t}\Rightarrow\dfrac{du}{dt}=a^{t+\frac1t}\log a\left(1-\dfrac{1}{t^2}\right)$
$v=\left(t+\dfrac1t\right)^a\Rightarrow\dfrac{dv}{dt}=a\left(t+\dfrac1t\right)^{a-1}\left(1-\dfrac{1}{t^2}\right)$
$\dfrac{du}{dv}=\dfrac{du/dt}{dv/dt}=\dfrac{a^{t+\frac1t}\log a}{a\left(t+\frac1t\right)^{a-1}}$

questions.text: Find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ if $y^x + x^y + x^x = a^b$, where $a$ and $b$ are constants.

answer.text:
Let $u=y^x,\ v=x^y,\ w=x^x\Rightarrow\dfrac{du}{dx}+\dfrac{dv}{dx}+\dfrac{dw}{dx}=0\quad\ldots(i)$
$u=y^x\Rightarrow\log u=x\log y\Rightarrow\dfrac1u\dfrac{du}{dx}=\dfrac{x}{y}\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\log y\Rightarrow\dfrac{du}{dx}=xy^{x-1}\dfrac{dy}{dx}+y^x\log y$
$v=x^y\Rightarrow\log v=y\log x\Rightarrow\dfrac1v\dfrac{dv}{dx}=\dfrac{y}{x}+\log x\dfrac{dy}{dx}\Rightarrow\dfrac{dv}{dx}=yx^{y-1}+x^y\log x\dfrac{dy}{dx}$
$w=x^x\Rightarrow\log w=x\log x\Rightarrow\dfrac1w\dfrac{dw}{dx}=1+\log x\Rightarrow\dfrac{dw}{dx}=x^x(1+\log x)$
$\therefore$ From (i): $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-\dfrac{x^x(1+\log x)+y^x\log y+yx^{y-1}}{xy^{x-1}+x^y\log x}$

questions.text: If $f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{\log(1 + ax) - \log(1 - bx)}{x}, & \text{for } x \neq 0 \\ k, & \text{for } x = 0 \end{cases}$ is continuous at $x = 0$, then the value of $k$ is :

answer.text: $a - b$

questions.text: If $\tan^{-1}(x^2 - y^2) = a$, where '$a$' is a constant, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is :

questions.text: Differentiate $e^{\sqrt{2x}}$ with respect to $e^{\sqrt{x}}$ for $x > 0$.

answer.text:
Let $u=\sqrt{e^{\sqrt{2x}}}$ and $v=e^{\sqrt{2x}}$
Derivative of $\sqrt v$ w.r.t. $v=\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt v}$
$\therefore$ Required derivative $=\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{e^{\sqrt{2x}}}}$

questions.text: If $(x)^y = (y)^x$, then find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$.

answer.text:
Taking log on both sides: $y\log x=x\log y$
Differentiating both sides w.r.t. $x$: $\dfrac{y}{x}+\log x\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{x}{y}\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\log y$
$\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{y(x\log y-y)}{x(y\log x-x)}$

questions.text: Differentiate $y = \sin^{-1}(3x - 4x^3)$ w.r.t. $x$, if $x \in \left[-\dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{1}{2}\right]$.

answer.text:
$x=\sin t$ gives $y=\sin^{-1}(\sin3t)=3t=3\sin^{-1}x$
$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$
Aliter: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{3-12x^2}{\sqrt{1-(3x-4x^3)^2}}$

questions.text: Differentiate $y = \cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1 - x^2}{1 + x^2}\right)$ with respect to $x$, where $x \in (0, 1)$.

answer.text:
$x=\tan t$ gives $y=\cos^{-1}(\cos2t)=2t=2\tan^{-1}x$
$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{2}{1+x^2}$
Aliter: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{-1}{\sqrt{1-\left(\frac{1-x^2}{1+x^2}\right)^2}}\cdot\dfrac{-4x}{(1+x^2)^2}$

If $f(x) = -2x^8$, then the correct statement is :

questions.text: Differentiate $\left(\dfrac{5^x}{x^5}\right)$ with respect to $x$.

answer.text:
Let $y=\dfrac{5^x}{x^5}=5^x\cdot x^{-5}\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{dx}=(5^x)'\cdot x^{-5}+5^x\cdot(x^{-5})'$
$=\dfrac{5^x}{x^5}\log5-\dfrac{5^{x+1}}{x^6}$

questions.text: If $-2x^2 - 5xy + y^3 = 76$, then find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$.

answer.text:
Differentiating $-2x^2-5xy+y^3=76$ with respect to $x$: $-4x-5y-5x\dfrac{dy}{dx}+3y^2\dfrac{dy}{dx}=0$
$\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{4x+5y}{3y^2-5x}$

questions.text: Differentiate $y = \sqrt{\log\left\{\sin\left(\dfrac{x^3}{3} - 1\right)\right\}}$ with respect to $x$.

answer.text:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{\log\left\{\sin\left(\frac{x^3}{3}-1\right)\right\}}}\cdot\dfrac{1}{\sin\left(\frac{x^3}{3}-1\right)}\cdot\cos\left(\dfrac{x^3}{3}-1\right)\cdot\dfrac{3x^2}{3}$
$=\dfrac{x^2\cot\left(\frac{x^3}{3}-1\right)}{2\sqrt{\log\left\{\sin\left(\frac{x^3}{3}-1\right)\right\}}}$

questions.text: Check whether function $f(x)$ defined as $f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{|x - 3|}{2(x - 3)}, & x < 3 \\ \dfrac{x - 6}{6}, & x \geq 3 \end{cases}$ is continuous at $x = 3$ or not.

answer.text: For $x<3$, $f(x)=\dfrac{|x-3|}{2(x-3)}=\dfrac{-(x-3)}{2(x-3)}=-\dfrac{1}{2}$, and for $x\ge 3$, $f(x)=\dfrac{x-6}{6}$. So $f(3)=\dfrac{3-6}{6}=-\dfrac{1}{2}$. $\text{LHL}=\lim_{x\to 3^{-}}\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)=-\dfrac{1}{2}$ and $\text{RHL}=\lim_{x\to 3^{+}}\dfrac{x-6}{6}=-\dfrac{1}{2}$. Since $\text{LHL}=\text{RHL}=f(3)=-\dfrac{1}{2}$, the function $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=3$.

questions.text: If $\sqrt{3}(x^2 + y^2) = 4xy$, then find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ at $\left(\dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$.

answer.text: Given $\sqrt{3}\,(x^2+y^2)=4xy$. Differentiating both sides w.r.t. $x$: $\sqrt{3}\left(2x+2y\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)=4\left(x\dfrac{dy}{dx}+y\right)$, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{2y-\sqrt{3}\,x}{\sqrt{3}\,y-2x}$. At $\left(\dfrac{1}{2},\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$, $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{2\cdot\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-\sqrt{3}\cdot\frac{1}{2}}{\sqrt{3}\cdot\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-2\cdot\frac{1}{2}}=\sqrt{3}$.

questions.text: If $x = \cos t$, $y = \cos mt$, prove that $(1 - x^2)\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} - x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + m^2 y = 0$.

answer.text: $x=\cos t$, $y=\cos mt$. Then $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=-\sin t$ and $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=-m\sin mt$, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{m\sin mt}{\sin t}$, i.e. $\sin t\,\dfrac{dy}{dx}=m\sin mt$. Differentiating both sides w.r.t. $x$: $\sin t\,\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}+\dfrac{dy}{dx}\cos t\,\dfrac{dt}{dx}=m^2\cos mt\,\dfrac{dt}{dx}$. Multiplying through by $\sin t$ and using $\dfrac{dt}{dx}=-\dfrac{1}{\sin t}$: $(1-\cos^2 t)\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}-x\,\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-m^2\cos mt$, that is $(1-x^2)\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}-x\,\dfrac{dy}{dx}+m^2y=0$.

questions.text: If $e^{-x} + e^{-y} = 2$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is :
If $x = a\sin^3 t$, $y = b\cos^3 t$, then find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ at $t = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$.
questions.topic: Derivatives of Functions in Parametric Forms

answer.text: $x=a\sin^3 t$, $y=b\cos^3 t\Rightarrow\dfrac{dx}{dt}=3a\sin^2 t\cos t$, $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=-3b\cos^2 t\sin t\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-\dfrac{b}{a}\cot t$. At $t=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$, $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-\dfrac{b}{a}$.

questions.text: Sports car racing is a form of motorsport which uses sports car prototypes. The competition is held on special tracks designed in various shapes. The equation of one such track is given as follows : $f(x) = \begin{cases} x^4 - 4x^2 + 4, & 0 \leq x < 3 \\ x^2 + 40, & x \geq 3 \end{cases}$ Based on given information, answer the following questions : (i) Find $f'(x)$ for $0 < x < 3$. (ii) Find $f'(4)$. (iii)(a) Test for continuity of $f(x)$ at $x = 3$.  OR  (iii)(b) Test for differentiability of $f(x)$ at $x = 3$.

answer.text: The track is $f(x)=\begin{cases}x^4-4x^2+4,&0\le x<3\\ x^2+40,&x\ge 3\end{cases}$ (i) For $0<x<3$, $f'(x)=4x^3-8x$. (ii) For $x\ge 3$, $f'(x)=2x$, so $f'(4)=8$. (iii)(a) $f(3)=49$; $\text{LHL}=\lim_{x\to 3^-}(x^4-4x^2+4)=49$ and $\text{RHL}=\lim_{x\to 3^+}(x^2+40)=49=f(3)$, so $f$ is continuous at $x=3$. OR (iii)(b) $\text{LHD}=84$ and $\text{RHD}=6$; since $\text{LHD}\neq\text{RHD}$, $f$ is not differentiable at $x=3$.

questions.text: The value of $k$ for which the function $f(x) = \begin{cases} x^2\sin\dfrac{1}{x}, & x \neq 0 \\ k(x + 1), & x = 0 \end{cases}$ is a continuous function, is :
If $\sin^{-1}x = y$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is :

questions.text: If $x = t + \dfrac{1}{t}$ and $y = t - \dfrac{1}{t}$, find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ at $t = 2$.
questions.topic: Derivatives of Functions in Parametric Forms

answer.text: $x=t+\dfrac{1}{t}\Rightarrow\dfrac{dx}{dt}=1-\dfrac{1}{t^2}$; $y=t-\dfrac{1}{t}\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{dt}=1+\dfrac{1}{t^2}$. So $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{t^2+1}{t^2-1}$; at $t=2$, $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{5}{3}$.

questions.text: If $(\sin x)^y = y^{\cos x}$, then find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$.

answer.text: $(\sin x)^y=y^{\cos x}\Rightarrow y\log\sin x=\cos x\log y$. Differentiating w.r.t. $x$: $y\cdot\dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x}+\log\sin x\cdot\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{\cos x}{y}\dfrac{dy}{dx}-\log y\cdot\sin x$. Hence $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{y\,(y\cos x+\log y\,\sin^2 x)}{\sin x\,(\cos x-y\log\sin x)}$.

questions.text: Differential of $e^{e^x}$ with respect to $x$ is :

answer.text: $e^x e^{e^x}$

questions.text: If $f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{\sin x}{x} + \cos x, & x \neq 0 \\ k, & x = 0 \end{cases}$ is continuous at $x = 0$, then the value of $k$ is :
The greatest integer function, $f(x) = [x]$, $0 < x < 3$ is \textbf{\textit{not}} differentiable at how many points ?

answer.text: At only two points

questions.text: Show that the function $f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{\cos x}{\frac{\pi}{2} - x}, & x \neq \frac{\pi}{2} \\ 1, & x = \frac{\pi}{2} \end{cases}$ is continuous at $x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

answer.text: $f(x)=\dfrac{\cos x}{\frac{\pi}{2}-x}$ for $x\neq\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and $f\!\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)=1$. Putting $x=\dfrac{\pi}{2}-h$: $\lim_{x\to\pi/2}\dfrac{\cos x}{\frac{\pi}{2}-x}=\lim_{h\to 0}\dfrac{\sin h}{h}=1=f\!\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$. Hence $f$ is continuous at $x=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

questions.text: Find whether the function $f(x) = \begin{cases} x - 1, & x < 2 \\ 2x - 3, & x \geq 2 \end{cases}$ at $x = 2$ is differentiable or not.

answer.text: $f(x)=\begin{cases}x-1,&x<2\\ 2x-3,&x\ge 2\end{cases}$ At $x=2$: $\text{LHD}=1$ and $\text{RHD}=2$. Since $\text{LHD}\neq\text{RHD}$, $f$ is not differentiable at $x=2$ (though it is continuous there).

questions.text: If $xy = e^{x-y}$, then find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$.

answer.text: $xy=e^{x-y}$. Differentiating: $x\dfrac{dy}{dx}+y=e^{x-y}\left(1-\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)\Rightarrow\left(x+e^{x-y}\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx}=e^{x-y}-y\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{e^{x-y}-y}{x+e^{x-y}}=\dfrac{y(x-1)}{x(y+1)}$.

questions.text: Differentiate $\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{1 + x^2} - \sqrt{1 - x^2}}{\sqrt{1 + x^2} + \sqrt{1 - x^2}}\right)$ with respect to $\cos^{-1}x^2$.

answer.text: $y=\tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{1+x^2}-\sqrt{1-x^2}}{\sqrt{1+x^2}+\sqrt{1-x^2}}\right)$. Put $x^2=\cos\theta$: $y=\tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{\cos\frac{\theta}{2}-\sin\frac{\theta}{2}}{\cos\frac{\theta}{2}+\sin\frac{\theta}{2}}\right)=\tan^{-1}\!\left(\tan\!\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}-\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)\right)=\dfrac{\pi}{4}-\dfrac{\theta}{2}$, where $\theta=\cos^{-1}x^2$. Hence the derivative with respect to $\cos^{-1}x^2$ is $\dfrac{dy}{d\theta}=-\dfrac{1}{2}$.

questions.text: If $f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{x^2 - 4x - 5}{x + 1}, & x \neq -1 \\ k, & x = -1 \end{cases}$ is continuous at $x = -1$, then the value of $k$ is :
Derivative of $\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sin x + \cos x}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$, $-\dfrac{\pi}{4} < x < \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ with respect to $x$ is :
If $y\sqrt{x^2 + 1} = \log\left(\sqrt{x^2 + 1} - x\right)$, show that $(x^2 + 1)\dfrac{dy}{dx} + xy + 1 = 0$.

answer.text: $y\sqrt{x^2+1}=\log\!\left(\sqrt{x^2+1}-x\right)$. Differentiating: $\sqrt{x^2+1}\,\dfrac{dy}{dx}+y\cdot\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{x^2+1}}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x^2+1}-x}\cdot\dfrac{x-\sqrt{x^2+1}}{\sqrt{x^2+1}}=-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x^2+1}}$. Multiplying by $\sqrt{x^2+1}$: $(x^2+1)\dfrac{dy}{dx}+xy=-1$, i.e. $(x^2+1)\dfrac{dy}{dx}+xy+1=0$.

questions.text: Find the differential of $x^{\cot x} + \dfrac{2x^2 - 3}{2x^2 - x + 2}$ with respect to $x$.

answer.text: Let $u=x^{\cot x}$ and $v=\dfrac{2x^2-3}{2x^2-x+2}$. $\log u=\cot x\log x\Rightarrow\dfrac{du}{dx}=x^{\cot x}\!\left(\dfrac{\cot x}{x}-\csc^2 x\log x\right)$. $\dfrac{dv}{dx}=\dfrac{(2x^2-x+2)(4x)-(2x^2-3)(4x-1)}{(2x^2-x+2)^2}=\dfrac{-2x^2+20x-3}{(2x^2-x+2)^2}$. Hence the required derivative is $x^{\cot x}\!\left(\dfrac{\cot x}{x}-\csc^2 x\log x\right)+\dfrac{-2x^2+20x-3}{(2x^2-x+2)^2}$.

questions.text: If $f(x) = a(x - \cos x)$ is strictly decreasing in $\mathbb{R}$, then '$a$' belongs to :
Show that the function $f(x) = \dfrac{16 \sin x}{4 + \cos x} - x$ is strictly decreasing in $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \pi\right)$.

answer.text:
$f'(x)=\dfrac{16[(4+\cos x)\cos x+\sin^2 x]}{(4+\cos x)^2}-1=\dfrac{\cos x\,(56-\cos x)}{(4+\cos x)^2}$
In $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2},\pi\right)$, $\cos x<0\Rightarrow f'(x)<0$
$\therefore\ f(x)$ is strictly decreasing in $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2},\pi\right)$.

questions.text: A tank, formed using a combination of a cylinder and a cone, offers better drainage as compared to a flat bottomed tank. A tap is connected to such a tank whose conical part is full of water. Water is dripping out from a tap at the bottom at the uniform rate of $2\ \text{cm}^3/\text{s}$. The semi-vertical angle of the conical tank is $45°$. On the basis of given information, answer the following questions : (i) Find the volume of water in the tank in terms of its radius $r$. (ii) Find rate of change of radius at an instant when $r = 2\sqrt{2}$ cm. (iii)(a) Find the rate at which the wet surface of the conical tank is decreasing at an instant when radius $r = 2\sqrt{2}$ cm.  OR  (iii)(b) Find the rate of change of height '$h$' at an instant when slant height is 4 cm.

answer.text:
(i) $v=\dfrac13\pi r^2 h=\dfrac13\pi r^3$ \ [as $\theta=45^\circ$ gives $r=h$]
(ii) $\dfrac{dv}{dt}=\pi r^2\dfrac{dr}{dt}\Rightarrow \left(\dfrac{dr}{dt}\right)_{r=2\sqrt2}=-\dfrac{1}{4\pi}\ \text{cm/sec}$
(iii)(a) $C=\pi r l=\pi r\cdot\sqrt2\,r=\sqrt2\,\pi r^2$
$\dfrac{dC}{dt}=\sqrt2\,\pi\cdot 2r\dfrac{dr}{dt}$, \ $\left(\dfrac{dC}{dt}\right)_{r=2\sqrt2}=-2\ \text{cm}^2/\text{sec}$

questions.text: The equation of the path traced by a roller-coaster is given by the polynomial $f(x) = a(x + 9)(x + 1)(x - 3)$. If the roller-coaster crosses y-axis at a point $(0, -1)$, answer the following : (i) Find the value of '$a$'. (ii) Find $f''(x)$ at $x = 1$.
A particle moves along the curve $3y = ax^3 + 1$ such that at a point with x-coordinate 1, y-coordinate is changing twice as fast as x-coordinate. Find the value of $a$.

answer.text:
Differentiating $3y=ax^3+1$ with respect to $x$: $3\dfrac{dy}{dx}=3ax^2$
Taking $x=1$, $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=2$: $\ 3(2)=3a(1)^2\Rightarrow a=2$

questions.text: Engine displacement is the measure of the cylinder volume swept by all the pistons of a piston engine. The piston moves inside the cylinder bore. The cylinder bore in the form of circular cylinder open at the top is to be made from a metal sheet of area $75\pi\ \text{cm}^2$. Based on the above information, answer the following questions : (i) If the radius of cylinder is $r$ cm and height is $h$ cm, then write the volume $V$ of cylinder in terms of radius $r$. (ii) Find $\dfrac{dV}{dr}$. (iii)(a) Find the radius of cylinder when its volume is maximum.  OR  (iii)(b) For maximum volume, $h > r$. State true or false and justify.

answer.text:
(i) $\pi r^2+2\pi rh=75\pi\Rightarrow h=\dfrac{75-r^2}{2r}$, $\therefore V=\pi r^2 h=\dfrac{\pi}{2}(75r-r^3)$
(ii) $\dfrac{dV}{dr}=\dfrac{\pi}{2}(75-3r^2)$
(iii)(a) $\dfrac{dV}{dr}=0\Rightarrow r=5$, $\ \dfrac{d^2V}{dr^2}\Big]_{r=5}=\dfrac{\pi}{2}(-6r)<0$, $\therefore$ volume is maximum when $r=5$

questions.text: The use of electric vehicles will curb air pollution in the long run. The use of electric vehicles is increasing every year and estimated electric vehicles in use at any time $t$ is given by the function $V$ : $V(t) = \dfrac{1}{5}t^3 - \dfrac{5}{2}t^2 + 25t - 2$ where $t$ represents the time and $t = 1, 2, 3, \ldots$ corresponds to year 2001, 2002, 2003, $\ldots$ respectively. Based on the above information, answer the following questions : (i) Can the above function be used to estimate number of vehicles in the year 2000 ? Justify. (ii) Prove that the function $V(t)$ is an increasing function.

answer.text:
(i) For the year 2000, $t=0$ and $V(0)=-2$; the number of vehicles cannot be negative, $\therefore$ the given function $V(t)$ cannot be used.
(ii) $V'(t)=\dfrac35 t^2-5t+25=\dfrac35\left[\left(t-\dfrac{25}{6}\right)^2+\dfrac{875}{36}\right]>0$, $\therefore V(t)$ is an increasing function.

questions.text: If $f(x) = a(\tan x - \cot x)$, where $a > 0$, then find whether $f(x)$ is increasing or decreasing function in its domain.

answer.text:
$f'(x)=a(\sec^2 x+\csc^2 x)$
As $a>0$ and $\sec^2 x$, $\csc^2 x$ are squares, $f'(x)>0$
$\therefore f(x)$ is an increasing function in its domain.

questions.text: In order to set up a rain water harvesting system, a tank to collect rain water is to be dug. The tank should have a square base and a capacity of $250\ \text{m}^3$. The cost of land is Rs. 5,000 per square metre and cost of digging increases with depth and for the whole tank, it is Rs. $40{,}000\,h^2$, where $h$ is the depth of the tank in metres. $x$ is the side of the square base of the tank in metres. Based on the above information, answer the following questions : (i) Find the total cost $C$ of digging the tank in terms of $x$. (ii) Find $\dfrac{dC}{dx}$. (iii)(a) Find the value of $x$ for which cost $C$ is minimum.  OR  (iii)(b) Check whether the cost function $C(x)$ expressed in terms of $x$ is increasing or not, where $x > 0$.

answer.text:
(i) $C=40000h^2+5000x^2$; as $x^2 h=250$, $\Rightarrow C=\dfrac{40000(250)^2}{x^4}+5000x^2$
(ii) $\dfrac{dC}{dx}=\dfrac{-160000(250)^2}{x^5}+10000x$
(iii)(a) For minimum cost $\dfrac{dC}{dx}=0\Rightarrow 10000x^6=250\times250\times160000\Rightarrow x=10$; showing $\dfrac{d^2C}{dx^2}>0$ at $x=10$, $\therefore$ cost is minimum when $x=10$

questions.text: A volleyball player serves the ball which takes a parabolic path given by the equation $h(t) = -\dfrac{7}{2}t^2 + \dfrac{13}{2}t + 1$, where $h(t)$ is the height of ball at any time $t$ (in seconds), $(t \geq 0)$. Based on the above information, answer the following questions : (i) Is $h(t)$ a continuous function ? Justify. (ii) Find the time at which the height of the ball is maximum.

answer.text:
(i) $h(t)=-\dfrac72 t^2+\dfrac{13}{2}t+1$. Clearly $h(t)$ is a polynomial function, hence continuous. Hence $h(t)$ is a continuous function.
(ii) For maximum height, $\dfrac{dh}{dt}=0\Rightarrow-7t+\dfrac{13}{2}=0\Rightarrow t=\dfrac{13}{14}$; $\ \dfrac{d^2h}{dt^2}=-7<0$, $\therefore$ height is maximum at $t=\dfrac{13}{14}$

questions.text: Find the maximum and minimum values of the function given by $f(x) = 5 + \sin 2x$.

answer.text:
We know that $-1\leq\sin2x\leq1$
$\Rightarrow4\leq\sin2x+5\leq1+5\Rightarrow4\leq\sin2x+5\leq6$
So, maximum value is $6$ and minimum value is $4$.

questions.text: Sooraj's father wants to construct a rectangular garden using a brick wall on one side of the garden and wire fencing for the other three sides as shown in the figure. He has 200 metres of fencing wire. Based on the above information, answer the following questions : (i) Let '$x$' metres denote the length of the side of the garden perpendicular to the brick wall and '$y$' metres denote the length of the side parallel to the brick wall. Determine the relation representing the total length of fencing wire and also write $A(x)$, the area of the garden. (ii) Determine the maximum value of $A(x)$.

answer.text:
(i)(a) $2x+y=200$
(b) $A(x)=xy=x(200-2x)$
(ii) $A(x)=200x-2x^2$; for max/min $\dfrac{dA}{dx}=0$, i.e. $200-4x=0\Rightarrow x=50$
$\dfrac{d^2A}{dx^2}=-4$, $\left(\dfrac{d^2A}{dx^2}\right)_{x=50}<0$, hence $A(x)$ is maximum at $x=50$.
Thus, Max $A(x)=200(50)-2(50)^2=10000-5000=5000\ \text{m}^2$.

questions.text: The interval in which the function $f(x) = 2x^3 + 9x^2 + 12x - 1$ is decreasing, is :
The median of an equilateral triangle is increasing at the rate of $2\sqrt{3}$ cm/s. Find the rate at which its side is increasing.

answer.text:
In an equilateral triangle, the median is same as the altitude. Let $h$ denote the length of the median (altitude) and $x$ be the side of $\triangle ABC$.
Then $h=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}x$ \ or \ $x=\dfrac{2h}{\sqrt3}$ \ ...(i)
It is given that $\dfrac{dh}{dt}=2\sqrt3$. So, by (i) we have
$\dfrac{dx}{dt}=\dfrac{2}{\sqrt3}\dfrac{dh}{dt}\Rightarrow\dfrac{dx}{dt}=4$
Thus, the side of $\triangle ABC$ is increasing at the rate of $4\ \text{cm/sec}$.

questions.text: Sum of two numbers is 5. If the sum of the cubes of these numbers is least, then find the sum of the squares of these numbers.

answer.text:
Let the two numbers be $x$ and $y$. Then $x+y=5$ or $y=5-x$.
Let $S$ denote the sum of the cubes of these numbers. Then $S=x^3+y^3=x^3+(5-x)^3$
$\dfrac{dS}{dx}=3x^2-3(5-x)^2=15(2x-5)$
Now $\dfrac{dS}{dx}=0$ gives $x=\dfrac52$. Showing $S$ is minimum at $x=\dfrac52$.
So, the two numbers are $\dfrac52$ and $\dfrac52$.
$\Rightarrow\ x^2+y^2=\dfrac{25}{4}+\dfrac{25}{4}=\dfrac{25}{2}$

questions.text: Let $f(x)$ be a continuous function on $[a, b]$ and differentiable on $(a, b)$. Then, this function $f(x)$ is strictly increasing in $(a, b)$ if :

answer.text: $f'(x) > 0, \forall\, x \in (a, b)$

questions.text: Show that the function $f(x) = 4x^3 - 18x^2 + 27x - 7$ has neither maxima nor minima.

answer.text:
$f'(x)=12x^2-36x+27=3(2x-3)^2\ge0$ for all $x\in\mathbb{R}$.
$\therefore\ f$ is increasing on $\mathbb{R}$.
Hence $f(x)$ does not have maxima or minima.

questions.text: The traffic police has installed Over Speed Violation Detection (OSVD) system at various locations in a city. These cameras can capture a speeding vehicle from a distance of 300 m and even function in the dark. A camera is installed on a pole at the height of 5 m. It detects a car travelling away from the pole at the speed of 20 m/s, $x$ m away from the base of the pole. Let $\theta$ be the angle of elevation of the speed camera from the car C. On the basis of the above information, answer the following questions : (i) Express $\theta$ in terms of height of the camera installed on the pole and $x$. (ii) Find $\dfrac{d\theta}{dx}$. (iii)(a) Find the rate of change of angle of elevation with respect to time at an instant when the car is 50 m away from the pole.  OR  (iii)(b) If the rate of change of angle of elevation with respect to time of another car at a distance of 50 m from the base of the pole is $\dfrac{3}{101}$ rad/s, then find the speed of the car.

answer.text:
(i) $\tan\theta=\dfrac{5}{x}\Rightarrow\theta=\tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{5}{x}\right)$
(ii) $\dfrac{d\theta}{dx}=\dfrac{-5}{5^2+x^2}$
(iii)(a) $\dfrac{d\theta}{dt}=\dfrac{d\theta}{dx}\times\dfrac{dx}{dt}=\left[\dfrac{-5}{5^2+x^2}\times20\right]_{x=50}=\dfrac{-100}{2525}$ or $\dfrac{-4}{101}\ \text{rad/s}$
