questions.text: If M and m denote the local maximum and local minimum values of the function $f(x) = x + \dfrac{1}{x}$ $(x \neq 0)$ respectively, find the value of $(M - m)$.

answer.text:
$f'(x)=1-\dfrac{1}{x^2}=\dfrac{x^2-1}{x^2}=\dfrac{(x+1)(x-1)}{x^2}$
$f'(x)=0\Rightarrow x=-1,\ 1$
$f''(x)=\dfrac{2}{x^3}\Rightarrow f''(-1)=-2<0$, so $-1$ is a point of local maximum.
Local maximum value $=f(-1)=-2=M$
$f''(1)=2>0$, so $1$ is a point of local minimum. Local minimum value $=f(1)=2=m$
$\therefore\ M-m=-4$

questions.text: Show that $f(x) = e^x - e^{-x} + x - \tan^{-1}x$ is strictly increasing in its domain.

answer.text:
$f'(x)=e^x+e^{-x}+1-\dfrac{1}{1+x^2}=e^x+\dfrac{1}{e^x}+\dfrac{x^2}{1+x^2}>0$ for all $x\in\mathbb{R}$
$\therefore\ f$ is strictly increasing over its domain $\mathbb{R}$.

questions.text: Overspeeding increases fuel consumption and decreases fuel economy as a result of tyre rolling friction and air resistance. While vehicles reach optimal fuel economy at different speeds, fuel mileage usually decreases rapidly at speeds above 80 km/h. The relation between fuel consumption $F$ ($\ell$/100 km) and speed $V$ (km/h) under some constraints is given as $F = \dfrac{V^2}{500} - \dfrac{V}{4} + 14$. On the basis of the above information, answer the following questions : (i) Find $F$, when $V = 40$ km/h. (ii) Find $\dfrac{dF}{dV}$. (iii)(a) Find the speed $V$ for which fuel consumption $F$ is minimum.  OR  (iii)(b) Find the quantity of fuel required to travel 600 km at the speed $V$ at which $\dfrac{dF}{dV} = -0{\cdot}01$.

answer.text:
(i) When $V=40\ \text{km/h}$, $F=\dfrac{36}{5}\ \ell/100\text{km}$
(ii) $\dfrac{dF}{dV}=\dfrac{V}{250}-\dfrac14$
(iii)(a) $\dfrac{dF}{dV}=0\Rightarrow V=62{\cdot}5\ \text{km/h}$
$\dfrac{d^2F}{dV^2}=\dfrac{1}{250}>0$ at $V=62{\cdot}5\ \text{km/h}$
Hence, $F$ is minimum when $V=62{\cdot}5\ \text{km/h}$.

questions.text: If the sides of a square are decreasing at the rate of $1{\cdot}5$ cm/s, the rate of decrease of its perimeter is :

answer.text: $6$ cm/s

questions.text: Find the intervals in which the function $f(x) = \dfrac{\log x}{x}$ is strictly increasing or strictly decreasing.

answer.text:
$f(x)=\dfrac{\log x}{x}\Rightarrow f'(x)=\dfrac{1-\log x}{x^2}$; \ $(x>0)$
For strictly increasing/decreasing, put $f'(x)=0\Rightarrow x=e$
$f$ is strictly increasing for $x\in(0,e)$ and strictly decreasing for $x\in(e,\infty)$.

questions.text: Find the absolute maximum and absolute minimum values of the function $f$ given by $f(x) = \dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{2}{x}$, on the interval $[1, 2]$.

answer.text:
$f(x)=\dfrac{x}{2}+\dfrac{2}{x}$; \ $x\in[1,2]$
$\Rightarrow f'(x)=\dfrac12-\dfrac{2}{x^2}$; put $f'(x)=0\Rightarrow x^2=4\Rightarrow x=2$
Now $f(1)=\dfrac52$ and $f(2)=2$
$\therefore$ absolute maximum value $=\dfrac52$ and absolute minimum value $=2$.

questions.text: It is given that function $f(x) = x^4 - 62x^2 + ax + 9$ attains local maximum value at $x = 1$. Find the value of '$a$', hence obtain all other points where the given function $f(x)$ attains local maximum or local minimum values.

answer.text:
$f(x)=x^4-62x^2+ax+9\Rightarrow f'(x)=4x^3-124x+a$
As at $x=1$, $f$ attains local maximum value, $f'(1)=0\Rightarrow a=120$
Now, $f'(x)=4x^3-124x+120=4(x-1)(x^2+x-30)=4(x-1)(x-5)(x+6)$
Critical points are $x=-6,\ 1,\ 5$; \ $f''(x)=12x^2-124$
$f''(-6)>0,\ f''(1)<0,\ f''(5)>0$
So $f$ attains local maximum value at $x=1$ and local minimum value at $x=-6,\ 5$.

questions.text: The perimeter of a rectangular metallic sheet is 300 cm. It is rolled along one of its sides to form a cylinder. Find the dimensions of the rectangular sheet so that volume of cylinder so formed is maximum.

answer.text:
Let length of rectangle be $x\ \text{cm}$ and breadth be $(150-x)\ \text{cm}$.
Let $r$ be the radius of cylinder $\Rightarrow2\pi r=x\Rightarrow r=\dfrac{x}{2\pi}$
$V=\pi r^2 h=\pi\left(\dfrac{x^2}{4\pi^2}\right)(150-x)=\dfrac{75x^2}{2\pi}-\dfrac{x^3}{4\pi}$
$\dfrac{dV}{dx}=\dfrac{150x}{2\pi}-\dfrac{3x^2}{4\pi}$; \ $\dfrac{dV}{dx}=0\Rightarrow x=100\ \text{cm}$
$\dfrac{d^2V}{dx^2}\Big|_{x=100}=-\dfrac{75}{\pi}<0\Rightarrow V$ is maximum when $x=100\ \text{cm}$.
Length of rectangle is $100\ \text{cm}$ and breadth of rectangle is $50\ \text{cm}$.

questions.text: The function $f(x) = kx - \sin x$ is strictly increasing for :
Find the interval in which the function $f(x) = x^4 - 4x^3 + 10$ is strictly decreasing.

answer.text:
$f'(x)=4x^3-12x^2=4x^2(x-3)$
$\Rightarrow4x^2(x-3)<0$ for $x<3,\ x\neq0\Rightarrow f'(x)<0$ for $x<3,\ x\neq0$
Thus, $f(x)=x^4-4x^3+10$ is strictly decreasing on $(-\infty,0)\cup(0,3)$ (or $(-\infty,0]\cup[0,3]$).

questions.text: The volume of a cube is increasing at the rate of $6\ \text{cm}^3/\text{s}$. How fast is the surface area of cube increasing, when the length of an edge is 8 cm ?

answer.text:
Given, $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=6\ \text{cm}^3/\text{sec}$. Since $V=x^3$:
$\dfrac{dV}{dt}=3x^2\dfrac{dx}{dt}\Rightarrow6=3x^2\dfrac{dx}{dt}\Rightarrow\dfrac{dx}{dt}=\dfrac{2}{x^2}\ \text{cm}/\text{sec}$
Now, Surface Area $=S=6x^2\Rightarrow\dfrac{dS}{dt}=12x\dfrac{dx}{dt}=\dfrac{24}{x}$; at $x=8$, $\dfrac{dS}{dt}=3\ \text{cm}^2/\text{sec}$

questions.text: A store has been selling calculators at Rs. 350 each. A market survey indicates that a reduction in price ($p$) of calculator increases the number of units ($x$) sold. The relation between the price and quantity sold is given by the demand function $p = 450 - \dfrac{1}{2}x$. Based on the above information, answer the following questions : (i) Determine the number of units ($x$) that should be sold to maximise the revenue $R(x) = x\,p(x)$. Also, verify the result. (ii) What rebate in price of calculator should the store give to maximise the revenue ?

answer.text:
(i) Revenue by selling $x$ items $=R(x)=x\cdot p(x)=450x-\dfrac{x^2}{2}$
$\dfrac{dR}{dx}=450-x$; for maxima/minima, $\dfrac{dR}{dx}=0\Rightarrow x=450$
$\dfrac{d^2R}{dx^2}=-1<0$, so revenue is maximum when $x=450$ units are sold.
(ii) At $x=450$, $p=450-\dfrac{450}{2}=225$. So rebate $=350-225=$ ₹$125$ per calculator.

questions.text: The function $f(x) = \dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{2}{x}$ has a local minima at $x$ equal to :
Given a curve $y = 7x - x^3$ and $x$ increases at the rate of 2 units per second. The rate at which the slope of the curve is changing, when $x = 5$ is :

answer.text: $-60$ units/sec

questions.text: The area of the circle is increasing at a uniform rate of $2\ \text{cm}^2/\text{sec}$. How fast is the circumference of the circle increasing when the radius $r = 5$ cm ?

answer.text:
Let $C=2\pi r$ be the circumference of the circle.
$\dfrac{d(\pi r^2)}{dt}=2\Rightarrow\dfrac{dr}{dt}=\dfrac{1}{\pi r}\ \text{cm/sec}$
$\dfrac{dC}{dt}=2\pi\dfrac{dr}{dt}=\dfrac{2}{r}=\dfrac25\ \text{cm/sec}$ at $r=5\ \text{cm}$

questions.text: A rectangular visiting card is to contain 24 sq.cm of printed matter. The margins at the top and bottom of the card are to be 1 cm and the margins on the left and right are to be $1\frac{1}{2}$ cm as shown in the figure below. On the basis of the above information, answer the following questions : (i) Write the expression for the area of the visiting card in terms of $x$. (ii) Obtain the dimensions of the card of minimum area.

answer.text:
(i) Let $A(x)$ be the area of the visiting card. As $xy=24$:
$A(x)=(x+3)(y+2)=2x+3y+xy+6=2x+\dfrac{72}{x}+30$
(ii) $A'(x)=2-\dfrac{72}{x^2}$ and $A''(x)=\dfrac{144}{x^3}$
Solving $A'(x)=0\Rightarrow x=6$ is the critical point.
$A''(6)=\dfrac{144}{6}>0$, $\therefore$ area of the card is minimum at $x=6,\ y=4$.
The dimensions of the card with minimum area are Length $=9\ \text{cm}$, Breadth $=6\ \text{cm}$.

questions.text: The absolute maximum value of function $f(x) = x^3 - 3x + 2$ in $[0, 2]$ is :
Find the intervals in which function $f(x) = 5x^{3/2} - 3x^{5/2}$ is (i) increasing (ii) decreasing.

answer.text:
$f(x)=5x^{3/2}-3x^{5/2}\Rightarrow f'(x)=\dfrac{15}{2}\sqrt x\,(1-x)$
For increasing/decreasing, put $f'(x)=0\Rightarrow x=0,1$
(i) When $x\in[0,1]$, $f'(x)\ge0$, so $f$ is increasing when $x\in[0,1]$.
(ii) When $x\in[1,\infty)$, $f'(x)\le0$, so $f$ is decreasing when $x\in[1,\infty)$.

questions.text: Each side of an equilateral triangle is increasing at the rate of 3 cm/s. At what rate is area increasing when the side of the triangle is 15 cm ?

answer.text:
Let $a$ be the side of the triangle, so $\dfrac{da}{dt}=3\ \text{cm/s}$.
Area of an equilateral triangle, $A=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{4}a^2$
$\Rightarrow\dfrac{dA}{dt}=\dfrac{\sqrt3\,a}{2}\times\dfrac{da}{dt}$
$\therefore\dfrac{dA}{dt}\bigg|_{a=15\,\text{cm}}=\dfrac{\sqrt3\times15}{2}\times3=\dfrac{45\sqrt3}{2}\ \text{cm}^2/\text{s}$

questions.text: Find the absolute maximum and absolute minimum of function $f(x) = 2x^3 - 15x^2 + 36x + 1$ on $[1, 5]$.

answer.text:
$f(x)=2x^3-15x^2+36x+1\Rightarrow f'(x)=6(x^2-5x+6)=6(x-2)(x-3)$
$f'(x)=0\Rightarrow x=2,3\in[1,5]$
Now $f(1)=24,\ f(2)=29,\ f(3)=28,\ f(5)=56$
Hence, the absolute maximum value is $56$ and the absolute minimum value is $24$.

questions.text: A technical company is designing a rectangular solar panel installation on a roof using 300 metres of boundary material. The design includes a partition running parallel to one of the sides dividing the area (roof) into two sections. Let the length of the side perpendicular to the partition be $x$ metres and with parallel to the partition be $y$ metres. On the basis of the above information, answer the following questions : (i) Write the equation for the total boundary material used in the boundary and parallel to the partition in terms of $x$ and $y$. (ii) Write the area of the solar panel as a function of $x$. (iii)(a) Find the critical points of the area function. Use second derivative test to determine critical points at the maximum area. Also, find the maximum area.  OR  (iii)(b) Using first derivative test, calculate the maximum area the company can enclose with the 300 metres of boundary material, considering the parallel partition.

answer.text:
(i) $2x+3y=300$
(ii) $A=xy=\dfrac{x}{3}(300-2x)$
(iii)(a) $A=\dfrac{x}{3}(300-2x)=\dfrac13(300x-2x^2)\Rightarrow\dfrac{dA}{dx}=\dfrac13(300-4x)$
For critical points, put $\dfrac{dA}{dx}=0\Rightarrow x=75$
$\dfrac{d^2A}{dx^2}=-\dfrac43<0$, so $A$ is maximum at $x=75$; maximum area $=\dfrac{75}{3}(300-150)=3750\ \text{m}^2$

questions.text: The function $f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 6$ is increasing in the interval :

answer.text: $[2, \infty)$

questions.text: A cylindrical tank of radius 10 cm is being filled with sugar at the rate of $100\pi\ \text{cm}^3/\text{s}$. The rate, at which the height of the sugar inside the tank is increasing, is :

answer.text: $1$ cm/s

questions.text: Find the values of '$a$' for which $f(x) = \sin x - ax + b$ is increasing on $\mathbb{R}$.

answer.text:
$f'(x)=\cos x-a$
For $f(x)$ to be increasing, $f'(x)\ge0$, i.e. $\cos x\ge a$
Since $-1\le\cos x\le1\Rightarrow a\le-1$
Hence, $a\in(-\infty,-1]$. (Also accept $a\in(-\infty,-1)$.)

questions.text: A small town is analyzing the pattern of a new street light installation. The lights are set up in such a way that the intensity of light at any point $x$ metres from the start of the street can be modelled by $f(x) = e^x\sin x$, where $x$ is in metres. Based on the above, answer the following : (i) Find the intervals on which the $f(x)$ is increasing or decreasing, $x \in [0, \pi]$. (ii) Verify, whether each critical point when $x \in [0, \pi]$ is a point of local maximum or local minimum or a point of inflexion.

answer.text:
(i) $f'(x)=e^x(\cos x+\sin x)$
For critical points, $f'(x)=0\Rightarrow\cos x+\sin x=0\Rightarrow\cos x=-\sin x$
For $x$ to be a critical point $x\in(0,\pi)$, hence $x=\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$
For all $x\in\left[0,\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\right],\ f'(x)\ge0$. Hence, $f$ is increasing in $\left[0,\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\right]$.
For all $x\in\left[\dfrac{3\pi}{4},\pi\right],\ f'(x)\le0$. Hence, $f$ is decreasing in $\left[\dfrac{3\pi}{4},\pi\right]$.
(ii) $x=\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$ is a critical point. $f''(x)=e^x(\cos x-\sin x)+e^x(\cos x+\sin x)=2e^x\cos x$
$f''\!\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\right)=-\text{ve}$. Hence, $\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$ is a point of local maximum.

questions.text: The values of $\lambda$, so that $f(x) = \sin x - \cos x - \lambda x + C$ decreases for all real values of $x$ are :

answer.text: $\lambda \geq \sqrt{2}$

questions.text: If $f(x) = 2x + \cos x$, then $f(x)$ :

answer.text: is an increasing function

questions.text: Find the least value of '$a$' so that $f(x) = 2x^2 - ax + 3$ is an increasing function on $[2, 4]$.

answer.text:
$f(x)=2x^2-ax+3\Rightarrow f'(x)=4x-a$
Now $2\le x\le4\Rightarrow8-a\le4x-a\le16-a$
For $f$ to be an increasing function, $f'(x)\ge0\Rightarrow8-a\ge0\Rightarrow a\le8$
$\therefore$ Least value of $a$ does not exist.

questions.text: If $f(x) = x + \dfrac{1}{x}$, $x \geq 1$, show that $f$ is an increasing function.

answer.text:
$f(x)=x+\dfrac1x\Rightarrow f'(x)=1-\dfrac{1}{x^2}=\dfrac{x^2-1}{x^2}$
Now $\dfrac{x^2-1}{x^2}\ge0$ for all $x\ge1$
$\Rightarrow f'(x)\ge0\Rightarrow f$ is an increasing function.

questions.text: For the curve $y = 5x - 2x^3$, if $x$ increases at the rate of 2 units/s, then how fast is the slope of the curve changing when $x = 2$ ?

answer.text:
$y=5x-2x^3$. Given $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=2$ units/s.
Slope of the curve $=\dfrac{dy}{dx}=5-6x^2=m$
$\dfrac{dm}{dt}=-12x\dfrac{dx}{dt}=-12x(2)=-24x$
At $x=2,\ \dfrac{dm}{dt}=-24(2)=-48$
Hence, the slope of the curve is decreasing at the rate of $48$.

questions.text: The relation between the height of the plant ($y$ cm) with respect to exposure to sunlight is governed by the equation $y = 4x - \dfrac{1}{2}x^2$, where $x$ is the number of days exposed to sunlight. (i) Find the rate of growth of the plant with respect to sunlight. (ii) In how many days will the plant attain its maximum height ? What is the maximum height ?

answer.text:
(i) $y=4x-\dfrac12x^2\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{dx}=(4-x)\ \text{cm/day}$
(ii) For maximum height, $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=0\Rightarrow x=4$ days.
As $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}<0$, number of days $=4$.
Now, Maximum height $=y(4)=16-\dfrac12(16)=8\ \text{cm}$

questions.text: The slope of the curve $y = -x^3 + 3x^2 + 8x - 20$ is maximum at :

Surface area of a balloon (spherical), when air is blown into it, increases at a rate of $5\ \text{mm}^2/\text{s}$. When the radius of the balloon is 8 mm, find the rate at which the volume of the balloon is increasing.

answer.text:
$\dfrac{dS}{dt}=5\ \text{mm}^2/\text{s},\ \left(\dfrac{dV}{dt}\right)_{r=8}=?$
$S=4\pi r^2\Rightarrow\dfrac{dS}{dt}=8\pi r\dfrac{dr}{dt}\Rightarrow\dfrac{dr}{dt}=\dfrac{5}{8\pi r}$
$V=\dfrac43\pi r^3\Rightarrow\dfrac{dV}{dt}=4\pi r^2\dfrac{dr}{dt}\Rightarrow\dfrac{dV}{dt}=\dfrac52 r$
$\Rightarrow\left(\dfrac{dV}{dt}\right)_{r=8}=20\ \text{mm}^3/\text{s}$

questions.text: Find the value of '$a$' for which $f(x) = \sqrt{3}\sin x - \cos x - 2ax + 6$ is decreasing in $\mathbb{R}$.

answer.text:
Since $f(x)$ is a decreasing function $\Rightarrow f'(x)\le0$
$\Rightarrow\sqrt3\cos x+\sin x-2a\le0\Rightarrow2\left(\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\cos x+\dfrac12\sin x\right)-2a\le0$
$\Rightarrow\cos\left(x-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\le a$
Since $-1\le\cos\left(x-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\le1\Rightarrow a\ge1$, i.e. $a\in[1,\infty)$ or $(1,\infty)$

questions.text: A carpenter needs to make a wooden cuboidal box, closed from all sides, which has a square base and fixed volume. Since he is short of the paint required to paint the box on completion, he wants the surface area to be minimum. On the basis of the above information, answer the following questions : (i) Taking length = breadth = $x$ m and height = $y$ m, express the surface area (S) of the box in terms of $x$ and its volume (V), which is constant. (ii) Find $\dfrac{dS}{dx}$. (iii)(a) Find a relation between $x$ and $y$ such that the surface area (S) is minimum.  OR  (iii)(b) If surface area (S) is constant, the volume $(V) = \dfrac{1}{4}(Sx - 2x^3)$, $x$ being the edge of base. Show that volume (V) is maximum for $x = \sqrt{\dfrac{S}{6}}$.

answer.text:
(i) $V=x^2y\Rightarrow y=\dfrac{V}{x^2}\quad\ldots(i)$. Hence, $S=2x^2+4xy=2x^2+\dfrac{4V}{x}$
(ii) $\dfrac{dS}{dx}=4\left(x-\dfrac{V}{x^2}\right)$
(iii)(a) $\dfrac{dS}{dx}=0\Rightarrow V=x^3\Rightarrow x^2y=x^3\Rightarrow y=x$
$\dfrac{d^2S}{dx^2}=4\left(1+\dfrac{2V}{x^3}\right)>0\Rightarrow S$ is minimum if $y=x$.

questions.text: Determine the values of $x$ for which $f(x) = \dfrac{x - 4}{x + 1}$, $x \neq -1$ is an increasing or a decreasing function.

answer.text:
$f'(x)=\dfrac{(x+1)-(x-4)}{(x+1)^2}=\dfrac{5}{(x+1)^2}>0$
Hence $f$ is increasing in its domain.

questions.text: A ladder of fixed length '$h$' is to be placed along the wall such that it is free to move along the height of the wall. Based upon the above information, answer the following questions : (i) Express the distance ($y$) between the wall and foot of the ladder in terms of '$h$' and height ($x$) on the wall at a certain instant. Also, write an expression in terms of $h$ and $x$ for the area (A) of the right triangle, as seen from the side by an observer. (ii) Find the derivative of the area (A) with respect to the height on the wall ($x$), and find its critical point. (iii)(a) Show that the area (A) of the right triangle is maximum at the critical point.  OR  (iii)(b) If the foot of the ladder whose length is 5 m, is being pulled towards the wall such that the rate of decrease of distance ($y$) is 2 m/s, then at what rate is the height on the wall ($x$) increasing, when the foot of the ladder is 3 m away from the wall ?

answer.text:
(i) $y^2=h^2-x^2$; $A=\dfrac12xy=\dfrac12x\sqrt{h^2-x^2}$
(ii) $\dfrac{dA}{dx}=\dfrac12\sqrt{h^2-x^2}+\dfrac12x\cdot\dfrac{-x}{\sqrt{h^2-x^2}}$; $\dfrac{dA}{dx}=0$ gives $x=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt2}$
(iii)(a) $A''=\dfrac12\cdot\dfrac{-4x\sqrt{h^2-x^2}-(h^2-2x^2)\frac{-x}{\sqrt{h^2-x^2}}}{h^2-x^2}$ is $<0$ at $x=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt2}$. Hence $A$ is maximum at the critical point.

questions.text: A spherical ball has a variable diameter $\dfrac{5}{2}(3x + 1)$. The rate of change of its volume w.r.t. $x$, when $x = 1$, is :
If $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is defined as $f(x) = 3x - \sin x$, then $f$ is :

answer.text: an increasing function

questions.text: Amongst all pairs of positive integers with product as 289, find which of the two numbers add up to the least.

answer.text:
Let the numbers be $x$ and $y$ such that $xy=289\Rightarrow y=\dfrac{289}{x}$. Let $S$ be their sum, then $S=x+y=x+\dfrac{289}{x}$
$\dfrac{dS}{dx}=1-\dfrac{289}{x^2},\ \dfrac{dS}{dx}=0\Rightarrow x=17$, a positive integer.
$\dfrac{d^2S}{dx^2}\bigg|_{x=17}=289\left(\dfrac{2}{x^3}\right)\bigg|_{x=17}>0$, $\therefore S$ is minimum when $x=17,\ y=17$.

questions.text: The least value of $f(x) = x^3 - 12x$, $x \in [0, 3]$ is :

A room freshner bottle in the shape of an inverted cone sprays the perfume at regular intervals such that volume of the perfume in the bottle decreases at the steady rate of $1\ \text{mm}^3/\text{min}$. Find the rate at which level of perfume is dropping at an instant when level of perfume in the bottle is 10 mm, if the semi-vertical angle of conical bottle is $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

answer.text: Let $v$, $r$, $h$ be respectively the volume, radius and height of perfume at time $t$. Given $\dfrac{dv}{dt}=-1\ \text{mm}^3/\text{min}$. Since $\dfrac{r}{h}=\tan\dfrac{\pi}{6}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$, we get $r=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{3}}$. Then $v=\dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h=\dfrac{1}{3}\pi\dfrac{h^3}{3}=\dfrac{\pi h^3}{9}$. Differentiating: $\dfrac{dv}{dt}=\dfrac{\pi}{9}\cdot 3h^2\dfrac{dh}{dt}=\dfrac{\pi h^2}{3}\dfrac{dh}{dt}$. At $h=10$: $-1=\dfrac{\pi(100)}{3}\dfrac{dh}{dt}$, so $\dfrac{dh}{dt}=-\dfrac{3}{100\pi}\ \text{mm/min}$. Hence the level of perfume is dropping at the rate $\dfrac{3}{100\pi}\ \text{mm/min}$.

questions.text: An online delivery company running in a city has 5000 subscribers and collects annual subscription fees of Rs. 300 per subscriber for unlimited free deliveries. The company wishes to increase the annual subscription fee. It is predicted that, for every increase of Rs. 1, ten subscribers will discontinue. Assume that the company increased the annual fee by Rs. $x$. Based on the given information, answer the following questions : (i) How many subscribers will discontinue after an increase of Rs. $x$ in annual fee ? (ii) If $R(x)$ denotes the total revenue collected after the increase of Rs. $x$ in subscription fee, express $R(x)$ as a function of $x$. (iii)(a) Find the value of $x$ for which $R(x)$ is maximum.  OR  (iii)(b) Find the sub-intervals of $(0, 5000)$ in which $R(x)$ is increasing and decreasing.

answer.text: $5000$ subscribers pay ₹$300$ each; for every ₹$1$ rise in fee, $10$ subscribers discontinue, and the fee is raised by ₹$x$. (i) Subscribers who discontinue $=10x$. (ii) Revenue $R(x)=(5000-10x)(300+x)$. (iii)(a) $R'(x)=2000-20x=0\Rightarrow x=100$; $R''(x)=-20<0$ at $x=100$, so $R(x)$ is maximum at $x=100$. OR (iii)(b) $R'(x)=2000-20x$, and $R'(x)=0\Rightarrow x=100$. On $(0,100)$, $R'(x)>0$, so $R(x)$ is increasing on $(0,100]$; on $(100,5000)$, $R'(x)<0$, so $R(x)$ is decreasing on $[100,5000)$.

questions.text: For $f(x) = x + \dfrac{1}{x}$ $(x \neq 0)$
options: local minimum value $<$ local maximum value

answer.text: local maximum value is $-2$

questions.text: Find the absolute maximum value of $f(x) = \cos x + \sin^2 x$, $x \in [0, \pi]$.

answer.text: $f(x)=\cos x+\sin^2 x$ on $[0,\pi]$. $f'(x)=-\sin x+2\sin x\cos x=\sin x\,(2\cos x-1)=0\Rightarrow\sin x=0$ or $\cos x=\dfrac{1}{2}\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$. Now $f(0)=1$, $f\!\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)=\dfrac{5}{4}$, $f(\pi)=-1$. Absolute maximum value $=\dfrac{5}{4}$.

questions.text: If the volume of a solid hemisphere increases at a uniform rate, prove that its surface area varies inversely as its radius.

answer.text: For a solid hemisphere, $V=\dfrac{2}{3}\pi r^3$ increases uniformly, so $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=2\pi r^2\dfrac{dr}{dt}=C$ (constant), giving $\dfrac{dr}{dt}=\dfrac{C}{2\pi r^2}$. The surface area $S=3\pi r^2\Rightarrow\dfrac{dS}{dt}=6\pi r\dfrac{dr}{dt}=6\pi r\cdot\dfrac{C}{2\pi r^2}=\dfrac{3C}{r}\propto\dfrac{1}{r}$. Hence $S$ varies inversely as the radius.

questions.text: Find the sub intervals in which $f(x) = \cot^{-1}(\sin x + \cos x)$, $x \in (0, \pi)$ is increasing and decreasing.

answer.text: $f(x)=\cot^{-1}(\sin x+\cos x)$, $x\in(0,\pi)$. $f'(x)=\dfrac{\sin x-\cos x}{1+(\sin x+\cos x)^2}$. $f'(x)=0\Rightarrow\sin x=\cos x\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$. On $\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$, $f'(x)<0$, so $f$ is decreasing; on $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4},\pi\right)$, $f'(x)>0$, so $f$ is increasing.

questions.text: A rectangle of perimeter 36 cm is revolved around one of its sides to sweep out a cylinder of maximum volume. Find the dimensions of the rectangle.

answer.text: Let the sides of the rectangle be $x$ and $(18-x)$. Revolving about the side of length $(18-x)$ makes $x$ the radius of the cylinder: $V=\pi x^2(18-x)=\pi(18x^2-x^3)$. $\dfrac{dV}{dx}=\pi(36x-3x^2)=0\Rightarrow x=12$ (as $x\neq 0$); $\dfrac{d^2V}{dx^2}=\pi(36-6x)=-36\pi<0$ at $x=12$, so $V$ is maximum. Hence the dimensions of the rectangle are $12\ \text{cm}$ and $6\ \text{cm}$.

questions.text: The rate of change of volume of a sphere with respect to its diameter, when its radius is 5 cm, is :

answer.text: $50\pi\ \text{cm}^3/\text{cm}$

questions.text: Find the sub-interval(s) of $\left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ in which $f(x) = \tan x - 4x$ is increasing.

answer.text: $f(x)=\tan x-4x$ on $\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$. $f'(x)=\sec^2 x-4=0\Rightarrow\sec^2 x=4\Rightarrow\cos x=\dfrac{1}{2}\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$. For $x>\dfrac{\pi}{3}$, $f'(x)>0$, so $f$ is increasing on $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$.

questions.text: As shown in the figure below, two vertical electric poles of heights 22 m and 16 m stand facing each other on either side of a 20 m wide road. From a point R on the road, which is at a distance of $x$ m from the shorter pole, two ladders $l_1$ and $l_2$ of certain lengths are placed reaching the tops of the poles. Based on the above information, answer the following questions : (i) Express $p(x) = l_1 + l_2$ in terms of $x$. (ii) Find $p'(x)$. (iii)(a) Find the value of $x$ for which $l_1^2 + l_2^2$ is minimum.  OR  (iii)(b) If the 22 m long pole is also replaced by a 16 m long pole, at what distance from either pole should the ladders be kept so that the sum of squares of lengths of ladders needed to reach the top of the pole is minimum ?

answer.text: Two poles of heights $22$ m and $16$ m stand on opposite sides of a $20$ m wide road; ladders of lengths $l_1$ and $l_2$ are placed from a common point $R$ at distance $x$ m from the smaller pole. (i) $p(x)=l_1+l_2=\sqrt{22^2+(20-x)^2}+\sqrt{16^2+x^2}=\sqrt{x^2-40x+884}+\sqrt{x^2+256}$. (ii) $p'(x)=\dfrac{x-20}{\sqrt{x^2-40x+884}}+\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{x^2+256}}$. (iii)(a) Let $q(x)=l_1^2+l_2^2=2x^2-40x+1140$; $q'(x)=4x-40=0\Rightarrow x=10$, and $q''(x)=4>0$, so $q$ is minimum at $x=10$. OR (iii)(b) If both poles are $16$ m, $r(y)=(16^2+y^2)+[16^2+(20-y)^2]=2y^2-40y+912$; $r'(y)=4y-40=0\Rightarrow y=10$, $r''(y)=4>0$, so the ladders should be kept $10$ m from each pole.

questions.text: The surface area of a sphere when its volume changes at the same rate as its radius is :

answer.text: $1$ sq. unit

questions.text: Find the values of $x$ for which $f(x) = x^x$, $x > 0$ is increasing.

answer.text: $f(x)=x^x$, $x>0$. $f'(x)=x^x(1+\log x)$. Since $x^x>0$, $f'(x)=0\Rightarrow 1+\log x=0\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{1}{e}$. For $x>\dfrac{1}{e}$, $f'(x)>0$, so $f$ is increasing on $\left(\dfrac{1}{e},\infty\right)$.

questions.text: At a birthday party, children are being served orange juice in conical cups, as shown in the figure. Each cup is 15 cm deep and has a radius 5 cm. The juice is being poured into this cup at a rate of $0\cdot1\ \text{cm}^3/\text{s}$. On the basis of the above information, answer the following questions : (i) Establish a relation between the height $h$ of the juice in the cup and radius $r$ of the surface of the juice in the cup, if the semi-vertical angle of the cone is $\alpha$. (ii) At what rate is the juice level in the cup rising when the juice is 6 cm deep ? (iii)(a) When the juice is 6 cm deep, then find at what rate is the upper surface area of juice increasing ?  OR  (iii)(b) When the juice is 6 cm deep, then find the rate at which the wetted surface area of the cup is increasing.

answer.text: A conical cup has $R=5\ \text{cm}$, $H=15\ \text{cm}$; juice is poured at $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=0{\cdot}1\ \text{cm}^3/\text{s}$. (i) $\tan\alpha=\dfrac{r}{h}=\dfrac{5}{15}=\dfrac{1}{3}\Rightarrow r=\dfrac{h}{3}$. (ii) $V=\dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h=\dfrac{1}{27}\pi h^3\Rightarrow\dfrac{dV}{dt}=\dfrac{1}{9}\pi h^2\dfrac{dh}{dt}$; at $h=6$, $\dfrac{dh}{dt}=\dfrac{1}{40\pi}\ \text{cm/s}$. (iii)(a) Upper surface area $A=\pi r^2=\dfrac{\pi h^2}{9}\Rightarrow\dfrac{dA}{dt}=\dfrac{2\pi h}{9}\dfrac{dh}{dt}=\dfrac{1}{30}\ \text{cm}^2/\text{s}$ at $h=6$. OR (iii)(b) Wetted surface area $S=\pi r l=\dfrac{\sqrt{10}\,\pi h^2}{9}\Rightarrow\dfrac{dS}{dt}=\dfrac{2\sqrt{10}\,\pi h}{9}\dfrac{dh}{dt}=\dfrac{\sqrt{10}}{30}\ \text{cm}^2/\text{s}$ at $h=6$.

questions.text: Absolute minimum value of $f(x) = (x - 2)^2 + 5$ in the interval $[-3, 2]$ is :
Determine the values of $x$ for which $f(x) = \dfrac{x - 3}{x + 1}$, $x \neq -1$ is an increasing function.

answer.text: $f(x)=\dfrac{x-3}{x+1}$, $x\neq -1$. $f'(x)=\dfrac{(x+1)-(x-3)}{(x+1)^2}=\dfrac{4}{(x+1)^2}>0$ for all $x\neq -1$. Hence $f$ is increasing on $\mathbb{R}-\{-1\}$.

questions.text: A spherical balloon loses its volume due to escape of air from it in such a way that decrease of volume at any instant is proportional to its surface area. Show that the radius is decreasing at a constant rate.

answer.text: $V=\dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3$; the rate of change of volume is proportional to the surface area, so $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=-k(4\pi r^2)$, $k>0$. But $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=4\pi r^2\dfrac{dr}{dt}$, so $4\pi r^2\dfrac{dr}{dt}=-4k\pi r^2\Rightarrow\dfrac{dr}{dt}=-k$, a constant. Hence the radius decreases at a constant rate.

questions.text: A company produces cylindrical tumblers, open from the top. Since they want uniformity in the product, they fix the surface area of the tumblers produced. Based on the above information, answer the following questions : If for a tumbler, V is its volume, $h$ the height and $r$ the radius of the circular base, then : (i) Differentiate its volume with respect to radius of the base, where the surface area is constant. (ii) If the company wants to maximize the volume of each tumbler, then establish a relation between its height and the radius of the base.

answer.text: An open-top cylindrical tumbler has fixed surface area $S=2\pi rh+\pi r^2$. (i) $V=\pi r^2 h=\pi r^2\cdot\dfrac{S-\pi r^2}{2\pi r}=\dfrac{Sr-\pi r^3}{2}\Rightarrow\dfrac{dV}{dr}=\dfrac{S-3\pi r^2}{2}$. (ii) For maximum volume, $\dfrac{dV}{dr}=0\Rightarrow S=3\pi r^2$; $\dfrac{d^2V}{dr^2}=-3\pi r<0$ confirms a maximum. Then $h=\dfrac{S-\pi r^2}{2\pi r}=\dfrac{3\pi r^2-\pi r^2}{2\pi r}=r$, i.e. $h=r$.

questions.text: If $\dfrac{d}{dx}(f(x)) = \log x$, then $f(x)$ equals :
questions.topic: Integration as an Inverse Process of Differentiation

answer.text: $x(\log x - 1) + C$

questions.text: $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\pi/6} \sec^2\left(x - \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) dx$ is equal to :

answer.text: $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

questions.text: Evaluate : $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\pi/2} [\log(\sin x) - \log(2\cos x)]\, dx$

answer.text:
Let $I=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}[\log\sin x-\log(2\cos x)]\,dx=\int_0^{\pi/2}\log\!\left(\dfrac{\tan x}{2}\right)dx$
Using the property $\displaystyle\int_0^a f(x)\,dx=\int_0^a f(a-x)\,dx$, we get
$I=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}\log\!\left(\dfrac{\cot x}{2}\right)dx$
$\therefore\ 2I=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}\log\!\left(\dfrac{\tan x}{2}\cdot\dfrac{\cot x}{2}\right)dx=\int_0^{\pi/2}\log\!\left(\dfrac14\right)dx$
$2I=\log\!\left(\dfrac14\right)\big[x\big]_0^{\pi/2}=\dfrac{\pi}{2}\log\dfrac14$
$I=\dfrac{\pi}{4}\log\dfrac14$ or $-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\log 2$

questions.text: Find : $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}\,(\sqrt{x} + 1)(\sqrt{x} + 2)}\, dx$

answer.text:
Let $I=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt x\,(\sqrt x+1)(\sqrt x+2)}$
Let $\sqrt x=t$, $\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt x}\,dx=dt$
$\therefore\ I=2\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dt}{(t+1)(t+2)}=2\int\left(\dfrac{1}{t+1}-\dfrac{1}{t+2}\right)dt$
$=2[\log|t+1|-\log|t+2|]+C=2[\log(\sqrt x+1)-\log(\sqrt x+2)]+C$
or $2\log\!\left(\dfrac{\sqrt x+1}{\sqrt x+2}\right)+C$

questions.text: Evaluate : $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\pi/2} e^x \sin x\, dx$

answer.text:
Let $I=\displaystyle\int e^{x}\sin x\,dx=e^{x}\sin x-\displaystyle\int\cos x\,e^{x}\,dx$
$=e^{x}\sin x-\cos x\,e^{x}-I$
$\therefore\ I=\dfrac12 e^{x}(\sin x-\cos x)$
$\therefore\ \displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}e^{x}\sin x\,dx=\dfrac12 e^{\pi/2}+\dfrac12$ or $\dfrac12\left(e^{\pi/2}+1\right)$

questions.text: Find : $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{1}{\cos(x-a)\,\cos(x-b)}\, dx$

answer.text:
Let $I=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{1}{\cos(x-a)\cos(x-b)}\,dx=\dfrac{1}{\sin(a-b)}\displaystyle\int\dfrac{\sin[(x-b)-(x-a)]}{\cos(x-a)\cos(x-b)}\,dx$
$=\dfrac{1}{\sin(a-b)}\displaystyle\int[\tan(x-b)-\tan(x-a)]\,dx$
$=\dfrac{1}{\sin(a-b)}\big[\log|\sec(x-b)|-\log|\sec(x-a)|\big]+C$

questions.text: If $\dfrac{d}{dx}[f(x)] = ax + b$ and $f(0) = 0$, then $f(x)$ is equal to :
questions.topic: Integration as an Inverse Process of Differentiation

answer.text: $\dfrac{ax^2}{2} + bx$

questions.text: Anti-derivative of $\dfrac{\tan x - 1}{\tan x + 1}$ with respect to $x$ is :
questions.topic: Integration as an Inverse Process of Differentiation

answer.text: $\log\left|\sec\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} - x\right)\right| + c$

questions.text: Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\pi/4} \log(1 + \tan x)\, dx$.

answer.text:
Let $I=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/4}\log(1+\tan x)\,dx$ \ ...(i)
$\Rightarrow I=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/4}\log\!\left(1+\tan\!\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}-x\right)\right)dx=\int_0^{\pi/4}\log\!\left(\dfrac{2}{1+\tan x}\right)dx$ \ ...(ii)
Add (i) and (ii): $2I=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/4}\log 2\,dx=\log 2\cdot[x]_0^{\pi/4}=\dfrac{\pi}{4}\log 2$
$\Rightarrow I=\dfrac{\pi}{8}\log 2$

questions.text: Find $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{\sin^3 x \cos(x - \alpha)}}$.

answer.text:
Let $I=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{\sin^3 x\,\cos(x-\alpha)}}=\int\dfrac{\csc^2 x}{\sqrt{\sin\alpha+\cos\alpha\cot x}}\,dx$
Put $\sin\alpha+\cos\alpha\cot x=t\Rightarrow \csc^2 x\,dx=-\dfrac{1}{\cos\alpha}\,dt$
$\therefore I=-\displaystyle\int\dfrac{1}{\cos\alpha\,\sqrt t}\,dt=-\dfrac{2\sqrt t}{\cos\alpha}+c\Rightarrow I=-\dfrac{2}{\cos\alpha}\sqrt{\sin\alpha+\cos\alpha\cot x}+c$

questions.text: Find $\displaystyle\int e^{\cot^{-1}x}\left(\dfrac{1 - x + x^2}{1 + x^2}\right) dx$.

answer.text:
Put $\cot^{-1}x=t\therefore x=\cot t$ and $\dfrac{1}{1+x^2}\,dx=-dt$
$\therefore \displaystyle\int e^{\cot^{-1}x}\left(\dfrac{1-x+x^2}{1+x^2}\right)dx=-\int e^{t}(1-\cot t+\cot^2 t)\,dt=\int e^{t}(\cot t-\csc^2 t)\,dt$
$=e^{t}\cot t+c=x\,e^{\cot^{-1}x}+c$

questions.text: Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_{\log\sqrt{2}}^{\log\sqrt{3}} \dfrac{1}{(e^x + e^{-x})(e^x - e^{-x})}\, dx$.

answer.text:
Let $I=\displaystyle\int_{\log\sqrt2}^{\log\sqrt3}\dfrac{1}{(e^{x}+e^{-x})(e^{x}-e^{-x})}\,dx=\int_{\log\sqrt2}^{\log\sqrt3}\dfrac{e^{2x}}{(e^{2x})^2-1}\,dx$
Put $e^{2x}=t\Rightarrow e^{2x}\,dx=\dfrac12\,dt$; \ Upper limit $=3$, Lower limit $=2$
$\therefore I=\dfrac12\displaystyle\int_2^3\dfrac{1}{t^2-1}\,dt=\dfrac14\log\left|\dfrac{t-1}{t+1}\right|\ \Big]_2^3$
$\Rightarrow I=\dfrac14\left[\log\dfrac24-\log\dfrac13\right]=\dfrac14\log\dfrac32$

questions.text: $\displaystyle\int 2^{x+2}\,dx$ is equal to :
$\displaystyle\int \dfrac{2\cos 2x - 1}{1 + 2\sin x}\,dx$ is equal to :

answer.text: $x + 2\cos x + C$

questions.text: Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_{1}^{3} \dfrac{\sqrt{4 - x}}{\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{4 - x}}\,dx$.

answer.text:
Let $I=\displaystyle\int_1^3\dfrac{\sqrt{4-x}}{\sqrt x+\sqrt{4-x}}\,dx$
$I=\displaystyle\int_1^3\dfrac{\sqrt{4-(4-x)}}{\sqrt{4-x}+\sqrt{4-(4-x)}}\,dx$
$2I=\displaystyle\int_1^3\dfrac{\sqrt{4-x}+\sqrt x}{\sqrt{4-x}+\sqrt x}\,dx=\int_1^3 1\,dx$
$2I=[x]_1^3=2\Rightarrow I=1$

questions.text: Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_{1}^{e} \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{4x^2 - (x\log x)^2}}\,dx$.

answer.text:
Let $I=\displaystyle\int_1^{e}\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{4x^2-(x\log x)^2}}\,dx=\int_1^{e}\dfrac{1}{x\sqrt{4-(\log x)^2}}\,dx$ \ [Let $\log x=t\Rightarrow\dfrac1x\,dx=dt$]
$=\displaystyle\int_0^1\dfrac{dt}{\sqrt{4-t^2}}=\sin^{-1}\dfrac{t}{2}\ \Big]_0^1=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$

questions.text: Find $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{\cos x}{\sin 3x}\,dx$.

answer.text:
$I=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{\cos x}{3\sin x-4\sin^3 x}\,dx$; \ Let $\sin x=t\Rightarrow\cos x\,dx=dt$
$I=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dt}{3t-4t^3}=\int\dfrac{1}{t^3\left(\frac{3}{t^2}-4\right)}\,dt$
Let $\dfrac{3}{t^2}-4=z\Rightarrow-\dfrac{6}{t^3}\,dt=dz$
$I=-\dfrac16\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dz}{z}=-\dfrac16\log|z|+C=-\dfrac16\log\left|3\csc^2 x-4\right|+C$

questions.text: Find $\displaystyle\int x^2 \log(x^2 + 1)\,dx$.

answer.text:
Let $I=\displaystyle\int x^2\log(x^2+1)\,dx=\log(x^2+1)\cdot\dfrac{x^3}{3}-\int\dfrac{2x}{x^2+1}\cdot\dfrac{x^3}{3}\,dx$
$=\dfrac{x^3}{3}\log(x^2+1)-\dfrac23\displaystyle\int\dfrac{x^4}{x^2+1}\,dx=\dfrac{x^3}{3}\log(x^2+1)-\dfrac23\int\left(x^2-1+\dfrac{1}{x^2+1}\right)dx$
$=\dfrac{x^3}{3}\log(x^2+1)-\dfrac23\left[\dfrac{x^3}{3}-x+\tan^{-1}x\right]+C$

questions.text: $\displaystyle\int e^{5\log x}\,dx$ is equal to :
If $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{a} 3x^2\,dx = 8$, then the value of '$a$' is :
Find : $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{x^2 + x + 1}{(x + 1)^2(x + 2)}\,dx$

answer.text:
Let $I=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{x^2+x+1}{(x+1)^2(x+2)}\,dx$
Here $\dfrac{x^2+x+1}{(x+1)^2(x+2)}=\dfrac{A}{x+1}+\dfrac{B}{(x+1)^2}+\dfrac{C}{x+2}$
$\Rightarrow x^2+x+1=A(x+1)(x+2)+B(x+2)+C(x+1)^2$
On comparing, we get $A=-2$, $B=1$ and $C=3$.
$\therefore I=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{-2\,dx}{x+1}+\int\dfrac{dx}{(x+1)^2}+3\int\dfrac{dx}{x+2}=-2\log|x+1|-\dfrac{1}{x+1}+3\log|x+2|+C$

questions.text: Evaluate : $\displaystyle\int_{\pi/4}^{\pi/2} e^{2x}\left(\dfrac{1 - \sin 2x}{1 - \cos 2x}\right) dx$

answer.text:
$I=\displaystyle\int_{\pi/4}^{\pi/2}e^{2x}\left(\dfrac{1-\sin2x}{1-\cos2x}\right)dx$
Put $2x=t$ so that $2\,dx=dt$. When $x=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, $t=\pi$; $\ x=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$, $t=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$
Thus $I=\displaystyle\int_{\pi/2}^{\pi}e^{t}\left(\dfrac{1-\sin t}{1-\cos t}\right)\dfrac{dt}{2}=\dfrac12\int_{\pi/2}^{\pi}e^{t}\left(\dfrac12\csc^2\dfrac t2-\cot\dfrac t2\right)dt$
$=-\dfrac12\left|e^{t}\cot\dfrac t2\right|_{\pi/2}^{\pi}=\dfrac12 e^{\pi/2}$

questions.text: Evaluate : $\displaystyle\int_{-2}^{2} \dfrac{x^2}{1 + 5^x}\,dx$

answer.text:
$I=\displaystyle\int_{-2}^{2}\dfrac{x^2}{1+5^x}\,dx$ \ ...(1)
Replacing $x$ by $-2+2-x$: $\ I=\displaystyle\int_{-2}^{2}\dfrac{x^2\,5^x}{1+5^x}\,dx$ \ ...(2)
Adding (1) and (2): $2I=\displaystyle\int_{-2}^{2}\dfrac{x^2(1+5^x)}{1+5^x}\,dx=\int_{-2}^{2}x^2\,dx=\dfrac{x^3}{3}\Big]_{-2}^{2}=\dfrac83+\dfrac83=\dfrac{16}{3}$
$\Rightarrow I=\dfrac{16}{6}$ or $\dfrac83$

questions.text: Find : $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{e^x}{\sqrt{5 - 4e^x - e^{2x}}}\,dx$

answer.text: Let $e^{x}=t$, so that $e^{x}\,dx=dt$. Then $I=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dt}{\sqrt{5-4t-t^2}}=\int\dfrac{dt}{\sqrt{3^2-(t+2)^2}}=\sin^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{t+2}{3}\right)+C=\sin^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{e^{x}+2}{3}\right)+C$

questions.text: Evaluate : $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \sqrt{\sin x}\,\cos^5 x\,dx$

answer.text:
$I=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}\sqrt{\sin x}\,\cos^5 x\,dx=\int_0^{\pi/2}\sqrt{\sin x}\,(1-\sin^2 x)^2\cos x\,dx$
Put $\sin x=t\Rightarrow\cos x\,dx=dt$: $\ =\displaystyle\int_0^1\sqrt t\,(1-t^2)^2\,dt=\int_0^1\left(\sqrt t+t^{9/2}-2t^{5/2}\right)dt$
$=\dfrac{2t^{3/2}}{3}+\dfrac{2t^{11/2}}{11}-\dfrac{4t^{7/2}}{7}\ \Big]_0^1=\dfrac23+\dfrac{2}{11}-\dfrac47=\dfrac{64}{231}$

questions.text: $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{\sec x}{\sec x - \tan x}\,dx$ equals :

answer.text: $\sec x + \tan x + c$

questions.text: $\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{1} \dfrac{|x - 2|}{x - 2}\,dx$, $x \neq 2$ is equal to :
In the following question, a statement of Assertion (A) is followed by a statement of Reason (R). Choose the correct answer.
questions.assertion: $\displaystyle\int_{2}^{8} \dfrac{\sqrt{10 - x}}{\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{10 - x}}\,dx = 3$.

Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.text: Evaluate : $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{2\pi} \dfrac{1}{1 + e^{\sin x}}\,dx$

answer.text:
Let $I=\displaystyle\int_0^{2\pi}\dfrac{1}{1+e^{\sin x}}\,dx=\int_0^{2\pi}\dfrac{1}{1+e^{\sin(2\pi-x)}}\,dx=\int_0^{2\pi}\dfrac{e^{\sin x}}{e^{\sin x}+1}\,dx$
$\Rightarrow\ 2I=\displaystyle\int_0^{2\pi}\dfrac{e^{\sin x}+1}{e^{\sin x}+1}\,dx=\int_0^{2\pi}1\,dx=2\pi$
$\therefore\ I=\pi$

questions.text: Find : $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{x^4}{(x - 1)(x^2 + 1)}\,dx$

answer.text:
$I=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{x^4}{(x-1)(x^2+1)}\,dx=\int\left[x+1+\dfrac{1}{(x-1)(x^2+1)}\right]dx$
$=\dfrac{x^2}{2}+x+\displaystyle\int\left[\dfrac{1}{2(x-1)}-\dfrac12\cdot\dfrac{(x+1)}{(x^2+1)}\right]dx$ \ (using partial fractions)
$=\dfrac{x^2}{2}+x+\dfrac12\log|x-1|-\dfrac14\log|x^2+1|-\dfrac12\tan^{-1}x+C$

questions.text: Evaluate : $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \sin 2x \tan^{-1}(\sin x)\,dx$

answer.text:
Let $I=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin 2x\,\tan^{-1}(\sin x)\,dx=\int_0^{\pi/2}2\sin x\cos x\,\tan^{-1}(\sin x)\,dx$
Put $\sin x=t$ so that $\cos x\,dx=dt$. Thus, $I=2\displaystyle\int_0^{1}t\,\tan^{-1}t\,dt$
$=2\left[\left|\dfrac{t^2}{2}\tan^{-1}t\right|_0^{1}-\displaystyle\int_0^{1}\dfrac{1}{1+t^2}\cdot\dfrac{t^2}{2}\,dt\right]=2\cdot\dfrac12\cdot\dfrac{\pi}{4}-\displaystyle\int_0^{1}\dfrac{t^2}{1+t^2}\,dt$
$=\dfrac{\pi}{4}-\displaystyle\int_0^{1}\left[1-\dfrac{1}{1+t^2}\right]dt=\dfrac{\pi}{4}-\big|t\big|_0^{1}+\big|\tan^{-1}t\big|_0^{1}=\dfrac{\pi}{4}-1+\dfrac{\pi}{4}=\dfrac{\pi}{2}-1$

questions.text: $\displaystyle\int_{a}^{b} f(x)\,dx$ is equal to :

answer.text: $\displaystyle\int_{a}^{b} f(a + b - x)\,dx$

questions.text: Find : $\displaystyle\int x\sqrt{1 + 2x}\,dx$

answer.text:
$1+2x=t^2$, \ $2\,dx=2t\,dt$
$\dfrac12\displaystyle\int(t^4-t^2)\,dt=\dfrac12\left[\dfrac{t^5}{5}-\dfrac{t^3}{3}\right]+C$
$=\dfrac{(1+2x)^{5/2}}{10}-\dfrac{(1+2x)^{3/2}}{6}+C$

questions.text: Evaluate : $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\pi^2/4} \dfrac{\sin\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{x}}\,dx$

answer.text:
$\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi^2/4}\dfrac{\sin\sqrt x}{\sqrt x}\,dx$; \ Put $\sqrt x=t\Rightarrow dx=2t\,dt$
$=2\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin t\,dt=2\big[-\cos t\big]_0^{\pi/2}=2$

questions.text: Find : $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{x^2}{(x^2 + 4)(x^2 + 9)}\,dx$

answer.text:
Let $I=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{x^2}{(x^2+4)(x^2+9)}\,dx$; \ Put $x^2=t$
$\dfrac{t}{(t+4)(t+9)}=\dfrac{A}{t+4}+\dfrac{B}{t+9}\Rightarrow A=\dfrac{-4}{5},\ B=\dfrac{9}{5}$
$I=\dfrac{-4}{5}\displaystyle\int\dfrac{1}{2^2+x^2}\,dx+\dfrac{9}{5}\int\dfrac{1}{3^2+x^2}\,dx$
$=\dfrac{-2}{5}\tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)+\dfrac{3}{5}\tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)+C$

questions.text: Evaluate : $\displaystyle\int_{1}^{3} \left(|x - 1| + |x - 2| + |x - 3|\right) dx$

answer.text:
$\displaystyle\int_1^3(|x-1|+|x-2|+|x-3|)\,dx$
$=\displaystyle\int_1^3(x-1)\,dx+\int_1^2-(x-2)\,dx+\int_2^3(x-2)\,dx-\int_1^3(x-3)\,dx$
$=\displaystyle\int_1^3 2\,dx+\int_1^2(2-x)\,dx+\int_2^3(x-2)\,dx$
$=\big[2x\big]_1^3+\left[\dfrac{(2-x)^2}{-2}\right]_1^2+\left[\dfrac{(x-2)^2}{2}\right]_2^3=4+\dfrac12+\dfrac12=5$

questions.text: Evaluate : $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\pi/4} \dfrac{\sin x + \cos x}{9 + 16\sin 2x}\,dx$

answer.text:
Let $I=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/4}\dfrac{\sin x+\cos x}{9+16\sin2x}\,dx$
Put $\sin x-\cos x=t$, so that $(\cos x+\sin x)\,dx=dt$; \ $\sin^2 x+\cos^2 x-\sin2x=t^2\Rightarrow\sin2x=1-t^2$
$I=\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{0}\dfrac{dt}{25-16t^2}=\dfrac{1}{16}\int_{-1}^{0}\dfrac{dt}{\left(\dfrac54\right)^2-t^2}$
$=\dfrac{1}{40}\left[\log\left|\dfrac{5+4t}{5-4t}\right|\right]_{-1}^{0}=\dfrac{1}{40}\left[\log1-\log\!\left(\dfrac19\right)\right]=\dfrac{1}{40}\log9$ or $\dfrac{1}{20}\log3$

questions.text: Evaluate : $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \sin 2x \tan^{-1}(\sin x)\,dx$

answer.text:
Let $I=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin2x\,\tan^{-1}(\sin x)\,dx$; \ Put $\sin x=t$ so that $\cos x\,dx=dt$
$I=2\displaystyle\int_0^{1}t\,\tan^{-1}t\,dt=2\left[\tan^{-1}t\left(\dfrac{t^2}{2}\right)-\dfrac12\int\dfrac{t^2}{1+t^2}\,dt\right]_0^{1}$
$=2\left[\left(\dfrac{t^2}{2}\right)\tan^{-1}t-\dfrac12 t+\dfrac12\tan^{-1}t\right]_0^{1}=2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}-\dfrac12\right)=\dfrac{\pi}{2}-1$

questions.text: $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \dfrac{\sin x - \cos x}{1 + \sin x \cos x}\,dx$ is equal to :

answer.text: Zero $(0)$

questions.text: Find : $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{e^{4x} - 1}{e^{4x} + 1}\,dx$

answer.text:
Given integral $=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{e^{4x}-1}{e^{4x}+1}\,dx=\int\dfrac{e^{2x}-e^{-2x}}{e^{2x}+e^{-2x}}\,dx$
$=\dfrac12\displaystyle\int\dfrac{2(e^{2x}-e^{-2x})}{e^{2x}+e^{-2x}}\,dx=\dfrac12\log|e^{2x}+e^{-2x}|+C$

questions.text: Evaluate : $\displaystyle\int_{-2}^{2} \sqrt{\dfrac{2 - x}{2 + x}}\,dx$

answer.text:
$\displaystyle\int_{-2}^{2}\sqrt{\dfrac{2-x}{2+x}}\,dx=\int_{-2}^{2}\dfrac{2-x}{\sqrt{4-x^2}}\,dx=\int_{-2}^{2}\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{4-x^2}}\,dx-\int_{-2}^{2}\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{4-x^2}}\,dx$
$=2\displaystyle\int_{0}^{2}\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{4-x^2}}\,dx-0$ \ $\left[\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{4-x^2}}\text{ is even},\ \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{4-x^2}}\text{ is odd}\right]$
$=4\displaystyle\int_{0}^{2}\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{4-x^2}}\,dx=4\left[\sin^{-1}\dfrac{x}{2}\right]_0^{2}=2\pi$

questions.text: Find : $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{1}{x[(\log x)^2 - 3\log x - 4]}\,dx$

answer.text:
Let $\log x=t\Rightarrow\dfrac1x\,dx=dt$
The given integral becomes $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{1}{t^2-3t-4}\,dt=\int\dfrac{1}{\left(t-\dfrac32\right)^2-\left(\dfrac52\right)^2}\,dt$
$=\dfrac15\log\left|\dfrac{t-4}{t+1}\right|+C=\dfrac15\log\left|\dfrac{\log x-4}{\log x+1}\right|+C$

questions.text: Find : $\displaystyle\int x^2 \cdot \sin^{-1}\left(x^{3/2}\right) dx$

answer.text:
Let $x^{3/2}=t\Rightarrow\dfrac32 x^{1/2}\,dx=dt$
The given integral becomes $\dfrac23\displaystyle\int t\,\sin^{-1}t\,dt=\dfrac23\left[\sin^{-1}t\times\dfrac{t^2}{2}-\int\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-t^2}}\times\dfrac{t^2}{2}\,dt\right]$
$=\dfrac13\left[t^2\sin^{-1}t+\displaystyle\int\dfrac{1-t^2-1}{\sqrt{1-t^2}}\,dt\right]=\dfrac13\left[t^2\sin^{-1}t+\int\sqrt{1-t^2}\,dt-\int\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-t^2}}\,dt\right]$
$=\dfrac13\left[t^2\sin^{-1}t+\dfrac{t}{2}\sqrt{1-t^2}-\dfrac12\sin^{-1}t\right]+C$
$=\dfrac13\left[x^3\sin^{-1}\!\left(x^{3/2}\right)+\dfrac{x^{3/2}}{2}\sqrt{1-x^3}-\dfrac12\sin^{-1}\!\left(x^{3/2}\right)\right]+C$

questions.text: $\displaystyle\int_{-a}^{a} f(x)\,dx = 0$, if :
Evaluate : $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \sin 2x \cos 3x\,dx$

answer.text:
$I=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin2x\cos3x\,dx=\dfrac12\int_0^{\pi/2}(\sin5x-\sin x)\,dx$
$=\dfrac12\left[-\dfrac15\cos5x+\cos x\right]_0^{\pi/2}=-\dfrac25$

questions.text: Given $\dfrac{d}{dx}F(x) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2x - x^2}}$ and $F(1) = 0$, find $F(x)$.

answer.text:
$F(x)=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2x-x^2}}\,dx=\int\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-(x-1)^2}}\,dx=\sin^{-1}(x-1)+c$
When $x=1,\ y=0$ gives $c=0$
$\therefore\ F(x)=\sin^{-1}(x-1)$

questions.text: Find : $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{x^2 + 1}{(x^2 + 2)(x^2 + 4)}\,dx$

answer.text:
$I = \displaystyle\int \dfrac{x^2 + 1}{\left(x^2 + 2\right)\left(x^2 + 4\right)}\,dx$
Let $x^2 = y$, then $\dfrac{x^2 + 1}{\left(x^2 + 2\right)\left(x^2 + 4\right)} = \dfrac{y + 1}{(y + 2)(y + 4)}$
Let $\dfrac{y + 1}{(y + 2)(y + 4)} = \dfrac{A}{y + 2} + \dfrac{B}{y + 4}$
this gives $A = -\dfrac{1}{2},\ B = \dfrac{3}{2}$
$\therefore\ I = -\dfrac{1}{2}\displaystyle\int \dfrac{1}{x^2 + 2}\,dx + \dfrac{3}{2}\displaystyle\int \dfrac{1}{x^2 + 4}\,dx$
$\Rightarrow I = -\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{2}}\right) + \dfrac{3}{4}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) + c$

questions.text: Find : $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{2 + \sin 2x}{1 + \cos 2x}\,e^x\,dx$

answer.text:
$I=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{2+\sin2x}{1+\cos2x}e^x\,dx=\int\dfrac{2+2\sin x\cos x}{2\cos^2 x}e^x\,dx$
$=\displaystyle\int(\sec^2 x+\tan x)e^x\,dx=e^x\tan x+c$

questions.text: Evaluate : $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\pi/4} \dfrac{1}{\sin x + \cos x}\,dx$

answer.text:
$I=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/4}\dfrac{1}{\sin x+\cos x}\,dx=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\int_0^{\pi/4}\dfrac{1}{\cos\frac{\pi}{4}\sin x+\sin\frac{\pi}{4}\cos x}\,dx$
$=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/4}\dfrac{1}{\sin\!\left(x+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)}\,dx=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\int_0^{\pi/4}\csc\!\left(x+\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)dx$
$=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\left[\log\left|\csc\!\left(x+\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)-\cot\!\left(x+\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\right|\right]_0^{\pi/4}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\log\left(\sqrt2+1\right)$ or $-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\log\left(\sqrt2-1\right)$

questions.text: The value of $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{3} \dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{9 - x^2}}$ is :

answer.text: $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$

questions.text: Find : $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{1}{x(x^2 - 1)}\,dx$

answer.text:
$I=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{x(x^2-1)}=\int\dfrac{dx}{x^3\left(1-\frac{1}{x^2}\right)}=\dfrac12\int\dfrac{\left(\frac{2}{x^3}\right)dx}{\left(1-\frac{1}{x^2}\right)}$
Put $\left(1-\dfrac{1}{x^2}\right)=t\Rightarrow\left(\dfrac{2}{x^3}\right)dx=dt$
$I=\dfrac12\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dt}{t}=\dfrac12\log\left|1-\dfrac{1}{x^2}\right|+c$ or $\dfrac12\log\left|\dfrac{x^2-1}{x^2}\right|+c$

questions.text: Evaluate : $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \dfrac{x\,dx}{1 + \cos 2x + \sin 2x}$

answer.text:
$I=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/4}\dfrac{x}{1+\cos2x+\sin2x}\,dx$ \ ...(1)
On applying $\displaystyle\int_0^a f(x)\,dx=\int_0^a f(a-x)\,dx$, we get $I=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/4}\dfrac{\frac{\pi}{4}-x}{1+\cos2x+\sin2x}\,dx$ \ ...(2)
Adding (1) and (2): $2I=\dfrac{\pi}{4}\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/4}\dfrac{1}{1+\cos2x+\sin2x}\,dx$
$I=\dfrac{\pi}{16}\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/4}\dfrac{1}{\cos^2 x+\sin x\cos x}\,dx=\dfrac{\pi}{16}\int_0^{\pi/4}\dfrac{\sec^2 x\,dx}{1+\tan x}$
$I=\dfrac{\pi}{16}\big(\log|1+\tan x|\big)_0^{\pi/4}=\dfrac{\pi}{16}\log2$

questions.text: Find : $\displaystyle\int e^x\left[\dfrac{1}{(1 + x^2)^{3/2}} + \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1 + x^2}}\right] dx$

answer.text:
$I=\displaystyle\int e^x\left[\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1+x^2}}+\dfrac{1}{(1+x^2)^{3/2}}\right]dx$
Let $f(x)=\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1+x^2}}$, then $f'(x)=\dfrac{\sqrt{1+x^2}-x\cdot\frac{x}{\sqrt{1+x^2}}}{1+x^2}=\dfrac{1}{(1+x^2)^{3/2}}$
On applying $\displaystyle\int e^x(f(x)+f'(x))\,dx=e^x f(x)+c$:
$I=e^x\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1+x^2}}+c$

questions.text: Find : $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{3x + 5}{\sqrt{x^2 + 2x + 4}}\,dx$

answer.text:
$I=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{3x+5}{\sqrt{x^2+2x+4}}\,dx=\dfrac32\int\dfrac{2x+2}{\sqrt{x^2+2x+4}}\,dx+2\int\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x^2+2x+4}}\,dx$
$I=\dfrac32\left(2\sqrt{x^2+2x+4}\right)+2\displaystyle\int\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{(x+1)^2+\left(\sqrt3\right)^2}}\,dx$
$I=3\sqrt{x^2+2x+4}+2\log\left|(x+1)+\sqrt{x^2+2x+4}\right|+c$

questions.text: $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{1}{x(\log x)^2}\,dx$ is equal to :

answer.text: $-\dfrac{1}{\log x} + c$

questions.text: The value of $\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{1} x\,|x|\,dx$ is :
Find : $\displaystyle\int \cos^3 x\,e^{\log\sin x}\,dx$

answer.text:
$\displaystyle\int\cos^3 x\,e^{\log\sin x}\,dx=\int\cos^3 x\cdot\sin x\,dx$ (assuming $\cos x=t$, $\sin x\,dx=-dt$)
$=-\displaystyle\int t^3\,dt=-\dfrac{t^4}{4}+C=-\dfrac{\cos^4 x}{4}+C$

questions.text: Find : $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{1}{5 + 4x - x^2}\,dx$

answer.text: $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{1}{5+4x-x^2}\,dx=\int\dfrac{1}{3^2-(x-2)^2}\,dx=\dfrac16\log\left|\dfrac{1+x}{5-x}\right|+C$

questions.text: Evaluate : $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\pi} \dfrac{e^{\cos x}}{e^{\cos x} + e^{-\cos x}}\,dx$

answer.text:
Let $I=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi}\dfrac{e^{\cos x}}{e^{\cos x}+e^{-\cos x}}\,dx$ \ ...(i)
$\Rightarrow I=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi}\dfrac{e^{\cos(\pi-x)}}{e^{\cos(\pi-x)}+e^{-\cos(\pi-x)}}\,dx=\int_0^{\pi}\dfrac{e^{-\cos x}}{e^{-\cos x}+e^{\cos x}}\,dx$ \ ...(ii)
Adding (i) and (ii): $2I=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi}dx=[x]_0^{\pi}=\pi\Rightarrow I=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$

questions.text: Find : $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{2x + 1}{(x + 1)^2(x - 1)}\,dx$

answer.text:
$\displaystyle\int\dfrac{2x+1}{(x+1)^2(x-1)}\,dx=-\dfrac34\int\dfrac{1}{x+1}\,dx+\dfrac12\int\dfrac{1}{(x+1)^2}\,dx+\dfrac34\int\dfrac{1}{x-1}\,dx$
$=-\dfrac34\log|x+1|-\dfrac{1}{2(x+1)}+\dfrac34\log|x-1|+C$
or $\dfrac34\log\left|\dfrac{x-1}{x+1}\right|-\dfrac{1}{2(x+1)}+C$

questions.text: $\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{1} \dfrac{|x|}{x}\,dx$, $x \neq 0$ is equal to :
If $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{2^{1/x}}{x^2}\,dx = k \cdot 2^{1/x} + C$, then $k$ is equal to :

answer.text: $\dfrac{-1}{\log 2}$

questions.text: Find : $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{x + \sin x}{1 + \cos x}\,dx$

answer.text:
$\displaystyle\int\dfrac{x+\sin x}{1+\cos x}\,dx=\int\dfrac{x+2\sin\frac{x}{2}\cos\frac{x}{2}}{2\cos^2\frac{x}{2}}\,dx=\int x\left(\dfrac12\sec^2\dfrac{x}{2}\right)dx+\int\tan\dfrac{x}{2}\,dx$
$=x\tan\dfrac{x}{2}-\displaystyle\int\tan\dfrac{x}{2}\,dx+\int\tan\dfrac{x}{2}\,dx=x\tan\dfrac{x}{2}+C$

questions.text: Evaluate : $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\pi/4} \dfrac{dx}{\cos^3 x\sqrt{2\sin 2x}}$

answer.text:
$\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/4}\dfrac{dx}{\cos^3 x\sqrt{2\sin2x}}=\dfrac12\int_0^{\pi/4}\dfrac{dx}{\cos^4 x\sqrt{\tan x}}=\dfrac12\int_0^{\pi/4}\dfrac{(1+\tan^2 x)\sec^2 x}{\sqrt{\tan x}}\,dx$
Put $\tan x=t\Rightarrow\sec^2 x\,dx=dt$; $\therefore I=\dfrac12\displaystyle\int_0^{1}\dfrac{1+t^2}{\sqrt t}\,dt=\dfrac12\int_0^{1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt t}+t^{3/2}\right)dt$
$=\dfrac12\left[2\sqrt t+\dfrac25 t^{5/2}\right]_0^{1}=\dfrac65$

questions.text: If $f(2a - x) = f(x)$, then $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{2a} f(x)\,dx$ is :

answer.text: $2\displaystyle\int_{0}^{a} f(x)\,dx$

questions.text: Evaluate : $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \sqrt{1 + \sin 2x}\,dx$

answer.text:
Given definite integral $=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/4}\sqrt{(\sin x+\cos x)^2}\,dx=\int_0^{\pi/4}(\sin x+\cos x)\,dx$
$=[-\cos x+\sin x]_0^{\pi/4}=1$

questions.text: Find : $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{1}{x}\sqrt{\dfrac{x + a}{x - a}}\,dx$

answer.text:
$I=\displaystyle\int\dfrac1x\dfrac{x+a}{\sqrt{x^2-a^2}}\,dx=\int\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x^2-a^2}}\,dx+a\int\dfrac{1}{x\sqrt{x^2-a^2}}\,dx$
$=\log\left|x+\sqrt{x^2-a^2}\right|+\sec^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right)+C$

questions.text: Find : $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{x^2 + x + 9}{(x^2 + 9)(x + 1)}\,dx$

answer.text:
$\dfrac{x^2+x+1}{(x+2)(x^2+1)}=\dfrac{A}{x+2}+\dfrac{Bx+C}{x^2+1}$
Getting $A=\dfrac35,\ B=\dfrac25,\ C=\dfrac15$
Given integral $=\dfrac35\displaystyle\int\dfrac{1}{x+2}\,dx+\dfrac15\int\dfrac{2x}{x^2+1}\,dx+\dfrac15\int\dfrac{1}{x^2+1}\,dx$
$=\dfrac35\log|x+2|+\dfrac15\log(x^2+1)+\dfrac15\tan^{-1}x+C$

questions.text: $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{\cos 2x - \cos 2\alpha}{\cos x - \cos \alpha}\,dx$ is equal to :

answer.text: $2(\sin x + x\cos\alpha) + C$

questions.text: The value of $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{1} \dfrac{dx}{e^x + e^{-x}}$ is :

answer.text: $\tan^{-1}e - \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

questions.text: Evaluate : $\displaystyle\int_{\pi/2}^{\pi} e^x\left(\dfrac{1 - \sin x}{1 - \cos x}\right) dx$

answer.text:
$I=\displaystyle\int_{\pi/2}^{\pi}e^x\left(\dfrac{1-\sin x}{1-\cos x}\right)dx=\int_{\pi/2}^{\pi}e^x\left(\dfrac{1-2\sin\frac{x}{2}\cos\frac{x}{2}}{2\sin^2\frac{x}{2}}\right)dx$
$=\displaystyle\int_{\pi/2}^{\pi}e^x\left(\dfrac12\csc^2\dfrac{x}{2}-\cot\dfrac{x}{2}\right)dx$
$\therefore I=-\left[e^x\cot\dfrac{x}{2}\right]_{\pi/2}^{\pi}=-\left[e^\pi\cot\dfrac{\pi}{2}-e^{\pi/2}\cot\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right]=e^{\pi/2}$

questions.text: Find : $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{\cos x}{(4 + \sin^2 x)(5 - 4\cos^2 x)}\,dx$

answer.text:
$I=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{\cos x}{(4+\sin^2 x)(5-4\cos^2 x)}\,dx=\int\dfrac{\cos x}{(4+\sin^2 x)(1+4\sin^2 x)}\,dx$
$\sin x=t$ gives $I=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dt}{(4+t^2)(1+4t^2)}$
$=-\dfrac{1}{15}\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dt}{4+t^2}+\dfrac{4}{15}\int\dfrac{dt}{1+4t^2}\qquad(\text{using partial fractions})$
$=-\dfrac{1}{30}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{t}{2}\right)+\dfrac{2}{15}\tan^{-1}(2t)+C$
$=-\dfrac{1}{30}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sin x}{2}\right)+\dfrac{2}{15}\tan^{-1}(2\sin x)+C$

questions.text: Evaluate : $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \dfrac{dx}{a^2\cos^2 x + b^2\sin^2 x}$

answer.text:
$I=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi}\dfrac{dx}{a^2\cos^2 x+b^2\sin^2 x}=2\int_0^{\pi/2}\dfrac{dx}{a^2\cos^2 x+b^2\sin^2 x}=2\int_0^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\sec^2 x}{a^2+b^2\tan^2 x}\,dx$
$\tan x=t$ gives $I=2\displaystyle\int_0^{\infty}\dfrac{dt}{a^2+b^2t^2}=\dfrac{2}{b^2}\cdot\dfrac{b}{a}\left[\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{bt}{a}\right)\right]_0^{\infty}=\dfrac{\pi}{ab}$

questions.text: $\displaystyle\int \sqrt{1 + \sin x}\,dx$ is equal to :

answer.text: $2\left(\sin\dfrac{x}{2} - \cos\dfrac{x}{2}\right) + C$

questions.text: $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \cos x\,e^{\sin x}\,dx$ is equal to :
Find : $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{2x}{(x^2 + 3)(x^2 - 5)}\,dx$

answer.text:
Let $I=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{2x}{(x^2+3)(x^2-5)}\,dx$. Put $x^2=t\Rightarrow2x\,dx=dt$
$\Rightarrow I=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dt}{(t+3)(t-5)}=\int\left(-\dfrac{1}{8(t+3)}+\dfrac{1}{8(t-5)}\right)dt$
$=\dfrac18\left[\log|t-5|-\log|t+3|\right]+c=\dfrac18\log\left|\dfrac{x^2-5}{x^2+3}\right|+c$

questions.text: Evaluate : $\displaystyle\int_{1}^{4} \left(|x - 2| + |x - 4|\right) dx$

answer.text:
$\displaystyle\int_1^4(|x-2|+|x-4|)\,dx=\int_1^2(2-x)\,dx+\int_2^4(x-2)\,dx-\int_1^4(x-4)\,dx$
$=\left[\dfrac{(2-x)^2}{-2}\right]_1^2+\left[\dfrac{(x-2)^2}{2}\right]_2^4-\left[\dfrac{(x-4)^2}{2}\right]_1^4=\dfrac12+2+\dfrac92=7$

questions.topic: Integration as an Inverse Process of Differentiation

questions.text: $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{x + 5}{(x + 6)^2}\,e^x\,dx$ is equal to :

answer.text: $\dfrac{e^x}{x + 6} + C$

questions.text: Find : $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{x^2 + 1}{(x - 1)^2(x + 3)}\,dx$
Evaluate : $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \dfrac{x}{\sin x + \cos x}\,dx$

answer.text:
Let $I=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}\dfrac{x}{\sin x+\cos x}\,dx=\int_0^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\frac{\pi}{2}-x}{\cos x+\sin x}\,dx\quad(\text{using property})$
$2I=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\frac{\pi}{2}}{\sin x+\cos x}\,dx=\dfrac{\pi}{2}\cdot\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\int_0^{\pi/2}\dfrac{1}{\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4}+x\right)}\,dx$
$2I=\dfrac{\pi}{2\sqrt2}\left[\log\left|\csc\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}+x\right)-\cot\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}+x\right)\right|\right]_0^{\pi/2}$
$\Rightarrow I=\dfrac{\pi}{4\sqrt2}\log\dfrac{\sqrt2+1}{\sqrt2-1}$

questions.text: $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{e^{9\log x} - e^{8\log x}}{e^{6\log x} - e^{5\log x}}\,dx$ is equal to :
For a function $f(x)$, which of the following holds true ?
options: $\displaystyle\int_{-a}^{a} f(x)\,dx = 0$, if $f$ is an even function
$\displaystyle\int_{-a}^{a} f(x)\,dx = 2\int_{0}^{a} f(x)\,dx$, if $f$ is an odd function

answer.text: $\displaystyle\int_{a}^{b} f(x)\,dx = \int_{a}^{b} f(a + b - x)\,dx$

questions.text: $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{e^x}{\sqrt{4 - e^{2x}}}\,dx$ is equal to :

answer.text: $\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{e^x}{2}\right) + C$

questions.text: Find : $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{x^2 + 1}{(x^2 + 2)(2x^2 + 1)}\,dx$

answer.text:
$\displaystyle\int\dfrac{x^2+1}{(x^2+2)(2x^2+1)}\,dx=\dfrac13\int\dfrac{1}{x^2+2}\,dx+\dfrac13\int\dfrac{1}{2x^2+1}\,dx\qquad(\text{using partial fractions})$
$=\dfrac13\cdot\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{\sqrt2}\right)+\dfrac13\cdot\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\tan^{-1}(\sqrt2 x)+C$
or $=\dfrac{1}{3\sqrt2}\left(\tan^{-1}\dfrac{x}{\sqrt2}+\tan^{-1}\sqrt2 x\right)+C$

questions.text: Evaluate : $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\pi} \dfrac{x\tan x}{\sec x + \tan x}\,dx$

answer.text:
Let $I=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi}\dfrac{x\tan x}{\sec x+\tan x}\,dx\quad\ldots(i)\Rightarrow I=\int_0^{\pi}\dfrac{(\pi-x)\tan x}{\sec x+\tan x}\,dx\quad\ldots(ii)$
Adding (i) and (ii): $2I=\pi\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi}\dfrac{\tan x}{\sec x+\tan x}\,dx=\pi\int_0^{\pi}\dfrac{\tan x(\sec x-\tan x)}{\sec^2 x-\tan^2 x}\,dx$
$=\pi\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi}(\sec x\tan x-\sec^2 x+1)\,dx=\pi\left[\sec x-\tan x+x\right]_0^{\pi}=\pi(-1+\pi-1)=\pi(\pi-2)$
$\therefore I=\dfrac{\pi}{2}(\pi-2)$ or $\pi\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}-1\right)$

questions.text: If $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{3ax}{b^2 + c^2x^2}\,dx = A\log|b^2 + c^2x^2| + K$, then the value of A is :
The value of $\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{1} \dfrac{x^3}{x^2 + 2|x| + 1}\,dx$ is :
Evaluate : $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{1} x\tan^{-1}x\,dx$

answer.text: $\displaystyle\int_0^1 x\tan^{-1}x\,dx=\left[\tan^{-1}x\cdot\dfrac{x^2}{2}\right]_0^1-\int_0^1\dfrac{x^2}{2(1+x^2)}\,dx=\dfrac{\pi}{8}-\dfrac{1}{2}\int_0^1\left(1-\dfrac{1}{1+x^2}\right)dx=\dfrac{\pi}{8}-\dfrac{1}{2}\big[x-\tan^{-1}x\big]_0^1=\dfrac{\pi}{8}-\dfrac{1}{2}\left(1-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)=\dfrac{\pi}{4}-\dfrac{1}{2}$.

questions.text: Find : $\displaystyle\int \sqrt{\dfrac{x + 4}{x - 2}}\,dx$

answer.text: $\displaystyle\int\sqrt{\dfrac{x+2}{x-2}}\,dx=\int\dfrac{x+2}{\sqrt{x^2-4}}\,dx=\dfrac{1}{2}\int\dfrac{2x}{\sqrt{x^2-4}}\,dx+2\int\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{x^2-4}}=\sqrt{x^2-4}+2\log\left|x+\sqrt{x^2-4}\right|+C$.

questions.text: Find : $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{x^2}{(x^2 + 9)(x^2 + 16)}\,dx$

answer.text: $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{x^2}{(x^2+9)(x^2+16)}\,dx$: putting $x^2=t$, partial fractions give $\dfrac{t}{(t+9)(t+16)}=\dfrac{-9/7}{t+9}+\dfrac{16/7}{t+16}$, so the integral $=-\dfrac{9}{7}\int\dfrac{dx}{x^2+9}+\dfrac{16}{7}\int\dfrac{dx}{x^2+16}=-\dfrac{3}{7}\tan^{-1}\dfrac{x}{3}+\dfrac{4}{7}\tan^{-1}\dfrac{x}{4}+C$.

questions.text: If $I_1 = \displaystyle\int_{-\pi/4}^{\pi/4} \dfrac{dx}{1 + \cos 2x}$ and $I_2 = \int_{-1/2}^{1/2} |x|\,dx$, then show that $I_1 - 4I_2 = 0$.

answer.text: $I_1=\displaystyle\int_{-\pi/4}^{\pi/4}\dfrac{dx}{1+\cos 2x}=2\int_0^{\pi/4}\dfrac{dx}{2\cos^2 x}=\int_0^{\pi/4}\sec^2 x\,dx=\big[\tan x\big]_0^{\pi/4}=1$ (even integrand). $I_2=\displaystyle\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}|x|\,dx=2\int_0^{1/2}x\,dx=\big[x^2\big]_0^{1/2}=\dfrac{1}{4}$. Hence $I_1-4I_2=1-4\cdot\dfrac{1}{4}=0$.

questions.text: If $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{2a} \dfrac{1}{1 + 4x^2}\,dx = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$, then the value of $a$ is :

answer.text: $\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4}$

questions.text: Find : $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{x + 2}{\sqrt{9x - x^2}}\,dx$

answer.text: $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{x+2}{\sqrt{9x-x^2}}\,dx$: write $x+2=A(9-2x)+B\Rightarrow A=-\dfrac{1}{2}$, $B=\dfrac{13}{2}$. Then $I=-\dfrac{1}{2}\int\dfrac{9-2x}{\sqrt{9x-x^2}}\,dx+\dfrac{13}{2}\int\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{\left(\frac{9}{2}\right)^2-\left(x-\frac{9}{2}\right)^2}}=-\sqrt{9x-x^2}+\dfrac{13}{2}\sin^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{2x-9}{9}\right)+C$.

questions.text: Evaluate : $\displaystyle\int_{\pi/12}^{5\pi/12} \dfrac{dx}{1 + \sqrt{\cot x}}$

answer.text: $I=\displaystyle\int_{\pi/12}^{5\pi/12}\dfrac{dx}{1+\sqrt{\cot x}}=\int_{\pi/12}^{5\pi/12}\dfrac{\sqrt{\sin x}}{\sqrt{\sin x}+\sqrt{\cos x}}\,dx$. Using $\int_a^b f(x)\,dx=\int_a^b f(a+b-x)\,dx$: $I=\displaystyle\int_{\pi/12}^{5\pi/12}\dfrac{\sqrt{\cos x}}{\sqrt{\cos x}+\sqrt{\sin x}}\,dx$. Adding, $2I=\displaystyle\int_{\pi/12}^{5\pi/12}dx=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$, so $I=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

questions.text: Evaluate : $\displaystyle\int_{-\pi/6}^{\pi/2} (\sin|x| + \cos|x|)\,dx$

answer.text: $\displaystyle\int_{-\pi/6}^{\pi/2}(\sin|x|+\cos|x|)\,dx=\int_{-\pi/6}^{0}(-\sin x+\cos x)\,dx+\int_{0}^{\pi/2}(\sin x+\cos x)\,dx=\big[\cos x+\sin x\big]_{-\pi/6}^{0}+\big[-\cos x+\sin x\big]_{0}^{\pi/2}=\left(\dfrac{3}{2}-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)+2=\dfrac{1}{2}\,(7-\sqrt{3})$.

questions.text: If $\dfrac{d}{dx}(F(x)) = \dfrac{1}{e^x + 1}$, then find $F(x)$ given that $F(0) = \log\dfrac{1}{2}$.
questions.topic: Integration as an Inverse Process of Differentiation

answer.text: $\dfrac{d}{dx}F(x)=\dfrac{1}{e^x+1}\Rightarrow F(x)=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{e^x+1}=\int\dfrac{e^{-x}}{1+e^{-x}}\,dx=-\log(1+e^{-x})+C$. $F(0)=-\log 2+C=\log\dfrac{1}{2}\Rightarrow C=0$. Hence $F(x)=-\log(1+e^{-x})$ (equivalently $x-\log(e^x+1)$).

questions.text: $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{dx}{2^x + 2^{-x}}$ is equal to :
$\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{1} (1 - |x|)\,dx$ is equal to :

answer.text: $2\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{0} (1 + x)\,dx$

questions.text: Find : $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{dx}{x^{1/2} + x^{1/3}}$

answer.text: $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{x^{1/2}+x^{1/3}}$: put $x=t^6\Rightarrow dx=6t^5\,dt$. Then $I=6\displaystyle\int\dfrac{t^3}{t+1}\,dt=6\int\left(t^2-t+1-\dfrac{1}{t+1}\right)dt=6\left(\dfrac{t^3}{3}-\dfrac{t^2}{2}+t-\log|t+1|\right)=2x^{1/2}-3x^{1/3}+6x^{1/6}-6\log\!\left|x^{1/6}+1\right|+c$.

questions.text: Find : $\displaystyle\int \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1 - x}{1 + x}\right)\,dx$

answer.text: $\displaystyle\int\tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{1-x}{1+x}\right)dx=\int\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}-\tan^{-1}x\right)dx=\dfrac{\pi x}{4}-\left[x\tan^{-1}x-\int\dfrac{x}{1+x^2}\,dx\right]=\dfrac{\pi x}{4}-x\tan^{-1}x+\dfrac{1}{2}\log(1+x^2)+c$.

questions.text: Evaluate : $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\pi} \dfrac{\sin^{2026}x}{\sin^{2026}x + \cos^{2026}x}\,dx$

answer.text: $I=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi}\dfrac{\sin^{2026}x}{\sin^{2026}x+\cos^{2026}x}\,dx=2\int_0^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\sin^{2026}x}{\sin^{2026}x+\cos^{2026}x}\,dx$. Using $\int_0^a f(x)\,dx=\int_0^a f(a-x)\,dx$, $I=2\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\cos^{2026}x}{\sin^{2026}x+\cos^{2026}x}\,dx$. Adding the two, $2I=2\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}dx=\pi$, so $I=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

questions.text: Find : $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{\cos x}{(2 + \sin x)(4 + \sin x)}\,dx$

answer.text: $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{\cos x}{(2+\sin x)(4+\sin x)}\,dx$: put $\sin x=t\Rightarrow\cos x\,dx=dt$. Then $I=\int\dfrac{dt}{(2+t)(4+t)}=\dfrac{1}{2}\int\left(\dfrac{1}{2+t}-\dfrac{1}{4+t}\right)dt=\dfrac{1}{2}\log\left|\dfrac{2+t}{4+t}\right|=\dfrac{1}{2}\log\left|\dfrac{2+\sin x}{4+\sin x}\right|+c$.

questions.text: Find : $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{x + 3}{\sqrt{x^2 + 4x + 5}}\,dx$

answer.text: $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{x+3}{x^2+4x+5}\,dx=\dfrac{1}{2}\int\dfrac{2x+4}{x^2+4x+5}\,dx+\int\dfrac{dx}{(x+2)^2+1}=\dfrac{1}{2}\log\left|x^2+4x+5\right|+\tan^{-1}(x+2)+c$.

questions.text: $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{25 - 16x^2}}$ is equal to :
If $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{1} \dfrac{dx}{e^x + e^{-x}} = \tan^{-1}e + k$, then the value of $k$ is :

answer.text: $-\dfrac{\pi}{4}$

questions.text: Find : $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{x}{(x - 1)(x^2 + 4)}\,dx$

answer.text: $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{x}{(x-1)(x^2+4)}\,dx$. Partial fractions give $\dfrac{x}{(x-1)(x^2+4)}=\dfrac{1/5}{x-1}+\dfrac{-\frac{1}{5}x+\frac{4}{5}}{x^2+4}$. Then $I=\dfrac{1}{5}\int\dfrac{dx}{x-1}-\dfrac{1}{10}\int\dfrac{2x}{x^2+4}\,dx+\dfrac{4}{5}\int\dfrac{dx}{x^2+4}=\dfrac{1}{5}\log|x-1|-\dfrac{1}{10}\log(x^2+4)+\dfrac{2}{5}\tan^{-1}\dfrac{x}{2}+c$.

questions.text: Evaluate : $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{1} \dfrac{x\tan^{-1}x}{(1 + x^2)^{3/2}}\,dx$

answer.text: $\displaystyle\int_0^1\dfrac{x\tan^{-1}x}{(1+x^2)^{3/2}}\,dx$. Put $x=\tan t\Rightarrow dx=\sec^2 t\,dt$; the integral becomes $\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/4}t\sin t\,dt=\big[-t\cos t+\sin t\big]_0^{\pi/4}=-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\cdot\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\dfrac{4-\pi}{4\sqrt{2}}$.

questions.text: $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 + \cos 2x}}\,dx$ is equal to :

answer.text: $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\log|\sec x + \tan x| + C$

questions.text: The value of $\displaystyle\int_{-5}^{-1} \dfrac{1}{x}\,dx$ is equal to :
Find : $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{x - \sin x}{1 - \cos x}\,dx$

answer.text: $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{x-\sin x}{1-\cos x}\,dx=\int\dfrac{x}{2\sin^2\frac{x}{2}}\,dx-\int\dfrac{\sin x}{1-\cos x}\,dx=\int\dfrac{x}{2}\csc^2\dfrac{x}{2}\,dx-\int\cot\dfrac{x}{2}\,dx=-x\cot\dfrac{x}{2}+C$ (the $\int\cot\frac{x}{2}\,dx$ terms cancel).

questions.text: Evaluate : $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{2} \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x^2 + 2x + 3}}\,dx$

answer.text: $\displaystyle\int_0^2\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{x^2+2x+3}}=\int_0^2\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{(x+1)^2+2}}=\Big[\log\big|x+1+\sqrt{x^2+2x+3}\big|\Big]_0^2=\log(3+\sqrt{11})-\log(1+\sqrt{3})=\log\dfrac{3+\sqrt{11}}{1+\sqrt{3}}$.

topic_order: Integration as an Inverse Process of Differentiation

questions.text: Find the area of the region bounded by the curves $x^2 = y$, $y = x + 2$ and x-axis, using integration.

answer.text:
The $x$-coordinates of the points of intersection are $-1$ and $2$.
Required area $=\displaystyle\int_{-2}^{-1}(x+2)\,dx+\int_{-1}^{0}x^2\,dx$
$=\left[\dfrac{(x+2)^2}{2}\right]_{-2}^{-1}+\left[\dfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_{-1}^{0}=\dfrac12+\dfrac13=\dfrac56$

questions.text: Using integration, find the area of region bounded by line $y = \sqrt{3}\,x$, the curve $y = \sqrt{4 - x^2}$ and y-axis in first quadrant.

answer.text:
Point of intersection at $x=1$.
$\text{ar}(OAB)=\displaystyle\int_0^{1}\sqrt{4-x^2}\,dx-\int_0^{1}\sqrt3\,x\,dx$
$=\left[\dfrac{x\sqrt{4-x^2}}{2}+2\sin^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)\right]_0^{1}-\left[\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}x^2\right]_0^{1}$
$=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}+2\cdot\dfrac{\pi}{6}-\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$

questions.text: The area of the region bounded by the line $y = mx$ $(m > 0)$, the curve $x^2 + y^2 = 4$ in the first quadrant is $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ units. Using integration, find the value of $m$.

answer.text:
$x^2+y^2=4$ and $y=mx\Rightarrow x^2+m^2x^2=4\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{1+m^2}}$
x-coordinate of the required point of intersection is $\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{1+m^2}}$.
According to the question, $\displaystyle\int_0^{2/\sqrt{1+m^2}}mx\,dx+\int_{2/\sqrt{1+m^2}}^{2}\sqrt{4-x^2}\,dx=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$
$\Rightarrow m\dfrac{x^2}{2}\Big]_0^{2/\sqrt{1+m^2}}+\left[\dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{4-x^2}+2\sin^{-1}\dfrac{x}{2}\right]_{2/\sqrt{1+m^2}}^{2}=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$
$\Rightarrow\dfrac{2m}{1+m^2}+\pi-\dfrac{2m}{1+m^2}-2\sin^{-1}\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1+m^2}}=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$
$\Rightarrow\dfrac{\pi}{4}=\sin^{-1}\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1+m^2}}\Rightarrow\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1+m^2}}\Rightarrow m^2+1=2\Rightarrow m=1$ (as $m>0$)

questions.text: Using integration, find the area of the region bounded by the parabola $y^2 = 4ax$ and its latus rectum.

answer.text:
Draw the parabola $y^2=4ax$ and its latus rectum $x=a$; the required region is bounded by the curve and the line $x=a$, and is symmetrical about the $x$-axis.
Required area $=2\displaystyle\int_0^a 2\sqrt{ax}\,dx$
$=4\sqrt{a}\displaystyle\int_0^a \sqrt{x}\,dx$
$=4\sqrt{a}\left[\dfrac{2x^{3/2}}{3}\right]_0^a$
$=\dfrac{8}{3}\,a\sqrt{a}\,\sqrt{a}=\dfrac{8}{3}a^2\ \text{sq units}$

questions.text: Sketch the region bounded by the lines $2x + y = 8$, $y = 2$, $y = 4$ and the y-axis. Hence, obtain its area using integration.

answer.text: Required area $=\displaystyle\int_2^4\dfrac12(8-y)\,dy=\dfrac12\left[8y-\dfrac{y^2}{2}\right]_2^4=5$ (square units).

questions.text: Find the area of the following region using integration : $\{(x, y) : y^2 \leq 2x \text{ and } y \geq x - 4\}$.

answer.text:
Solving $y^2=2x$ and $y=x-4$, we get $y=4$ or $y=-2$.
Required area $=\displaystyle\int_{-2}^{4}\left[(y+4)-\dfrac{y^2}{2}\right]dy=\left|\dfrac{y^2}{2}+4y-\dfrac16 y^3\right|_{-2}^{4}=18$ (square units).

questions.text: Using integration, find the area of the ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{16} + \dfrac{y^2}{4} = 1$, included between the lines $x = -2$ and $x = 2$.

answer.text:
Area $=4\displaystyle\int_0^{2}y\,dx=4\left[\dfrac12\int_0^{2}\sqrt{4^2-x^2}\,dx\right]$
$=2\left[\dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{4^2-x^2}+8\sin^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{x}{4}\right)\right]_0^{2}$
$=2\left[\sqrt{12}+\dfrac{8\pi}{6}\right]=4\sqrt3+\dfrac{8\pi}{3}$ (square units).

questions.text: If $A_1$ denotes the area of region bounded by $y^2 = 4x$, $x = 1$ and x-axis in the first quadrant and $A_2$ denotes the area of region bounded by $y^2 = 4x$, $x = 4$, find $A_1 : A_2$.

answer.text:
$A_1=$ Area (region $OABO$) $=\displaystyle\int_0^{1}2\sqrt x\,dx=2\left[\dfrac{x^{3/2}}{3/2}\right]_0^{1}=\dfrac43$
$A_2=$ Area (region $ODEO$) $=2\displaystyle\int_0^{4}2\sqrt x\,dx=4\times\dfrac23\left[2^3\right]=\dfrac{64}{3}$
$A_1:A_2=\dfrac43:\dfrac{64}{3}=1:16$

questions.text: Using integration, find the area of the region enclosed between the circle $x^2 + y^2 = 16$ and the lines $x = -2$ and $x = 2$.

answer.text: Required area $=4\displaystyle\int_0^{2}\sqrt{16-x^2}\,dx=4\left[\dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{16-x^2}+8\sin^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{x}{4}\right)\right]_0^{2}=8\sqrt3+\dfrac{16\pi}{3}$ (square units).

questions.text: Sketch the graph of $y = x\,|x|$ and hence find the area bounded by this curve, X-axis and the ordinates $x = -2$ and $x = 2$, using integration.

answer.text:
$y=x|x|=\begin{cases}-x^2,&x<0\\x^2,&x\ge0\end{cases}$
Area of the shaded region $=\displaystyle\int_{-2}^{2}y\,dx=2\int_0^{2}y\,dx=2\int_0^{2}x^2\,dx=2\left(\dfrac{x^3}{3}\right)_0^{2}=2\left(\dfrac83\right)=\dfrac{16}{3}$ (square units).

questions.text: Using integration, find the area bounded by the ellipse $9x^2 + 25y^2 = 225$, the lines $x = -2$, $x = 2$, and the X-axis.

answer.text:
As $9x^2+25y^2=225\Rightarrow y=\pm\dfrac35\sqrt{5^2-x^2}$
Required Area $=\displaystyle\int_{-2}^{2}\dfrac35\sqrt{5^2-x^2}\,dx=\dfrac65\int_0^{2}\sqrt{5^2-x^2}\,dx$
$=\dfrac65\left[\dfrac{x\sqrt{5^2-x^2}}{2}+\dfrac{25}{2}\sin^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{x}{5}\right)\right]_0^{2}=\dfrac65\left(\dfrac{2\sqrt{21}}{2}+\dfrac{25}{2}\sin^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac25\right)\right)$
$=\dfrac{6\sqrt{21}}{5}+15\sin^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac25\right)$ (square units).

questions.text: Area of the region bounded by curve $y^2 = 4x$ and the X-axis between $x = 0$ and $x = 1$ is :
Find the area of the region bounded by the curve $4x^2 + y^2 = 36$ using integration.

answer.text:
The given equation can be written as $\dfrac{x^2}{9}+\dfrac{y^2}{36}=1$, which is an ellipse.
Area of the region $=4\times\dfrac63\displaystyle\int_0^{3}\sqrt{9-x^2}\,dx=8\left[\dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{9-x^2}+\dfrac92\sin^{-1}\dfrac{x}{3}\right]_0^{3}=18\pi$ (square units).

questions.text: The area of the shaded region bounded by the curves $y^2 = x$, $x = 4$ and the x-axis is given by :

answer.text: $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{4} \sqrt{x}\,dx$

questions.text: Sketch the graph of $y = |x + 3|$ and find the area of the region enclosed by the curve, x-axis, between $x = -6$ and $x = 0$, using integration.

answer.text: Required Area $=\displaystyle\int_{-6}^{0}y\,dx=2\int_{-3}^{0}(x+3)\,dx=2\left[\dfrac{(x+3)^2}{2}\right]_{-3}^{0}=9$ (square units).

questions.text: The area of the shaded region (figure) represented by the curves $y = x^2$, $0 \leq x \leq 2$ and y-axis is given by :

answer.text: $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{4} \sqrt{y}\,dy$

questions.text: Using integration, find the area of the region bounded by the line $y = 5x + 2$, the x-axis and the ordinates $x = -2$ and $x = 2$.

answer.text:
The required area
$=\left|\displaystyle\int_{-2}^{-2/5}(5x+2)\,dx\right|+\int_{-2/5}^{2}(5x+2)\,dx$
$=\left|\left[\dfrac{(5x+2)^2}{10}\right]_{-2}^{-2/5}\right|+\left[\dfrac{(5x+2)^2}{10}\right]_{-2/5}^{2}$
$=\dfrac{64}{10}+\dfrac{144}{10}=\dfrac{104}{5}$ (square units).

questions.text: The area of the region enclosed by the curve $y = \sqrt{x}$ and the lines $x = 0$ and $x = 4$ and x-axis is :

answer.text: $\dfrac{16}{3}$ sq. units

questions.text: Calculate the area of the region bounded by the curve $\dfrac{x^2}{9} + \dfrac{y^2}{4} = 1$ and the x-axis using integration.

answer.text:
$A=2\times\dfrac23\displaystyle\int_0^3\sqrt{9-x^2}\,dx=\dfrac43\left[\dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{9-x^2}+\dfrac92\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)\right]_0^3$
$=\dfrac43\left[\left(0+\dfrac92\sin^{-1}1\right)-0\right]=3\pi$ (square units).

questions.text: The area of the region enclosed by the curve $y = x\,|x|$, x-axis, $x = -2$ and $x = 2$ is :
Sketch a graph of $y = x^2$. Using integration, find the area of the region bounded by $y = 9$, $x = 0$ and $y = x^2$.

answer.text: Required area $=\displaystyle\int_0^9\sqrt y\,dy=\dfrac23\left[y^{3/2}\right]_0^9=18$ (square units).

questions.text: The area of the region bounded by the curve $y^2 = x$ and $x = 0$ and $x = 1$ is :

answer.text: $\dfrac{4}{3}$ sq units

questions.text: Draw a rough sketch for the curve $y = 2 + |x + 1|$. Using integration, find the area of the region bounded by the curve $y = 2 + |x + 1|$, $x = -4$, $x = 3$ and $y = 0$.

A woman discovered a scratch along a straight line on a circular table top of radius 8 cm. She divided the table top into 4 equal quadrants and discovered the scratch passing through the origin inclined at an angle $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ anticlockwise along the positive direction of x-axis. Find the area of the region enclosed by the x-axis, the scratch and the circular table top in the first quadrant, using integration.

answer.text:
Equation of the circular table top: $x^2+y^2=64$; equation of line (scratch): $x=y$. The line and circle intersect at $x=4\sqrt2$.
Area of the shaded region $=\displaystyle\int_0^{4\sqrt2}x\,dx+\int_{4\sqrt2}^{8}\sqrt{64-x^2}\,dx$
$=\left[\dfrac{x^2}{2}\right]_0^{4\sqrt2}+\left[\dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{64-x^2}+32\sin^{-1}\dfrac{x}{8}\right]_{4\sqrt2}^{8}$
$=\dfrac{32}{2}+32\sin^{-1}1-2\sqrt2\cdot4\sqrt2-32\sin^{-1}\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}=16+16\pi-16-8\pi=8\pi\ \text{cm}^2$

questions.text: The area bounded by the curve $y = x\,|x|$, x-axis and the ordinates $x = -1$ and $x = 1$ is given by :

Roundabouts are often made on busy roads to ease the traffic and avoid red lights. One such round-about is made such that equation representing its boundary is given by $C_1 : x^2 + y^2 = 64$. There is a circular pond with a fountain in the middle of the roundabout whose equation is given by $C_2 : x^2 + y^2 = 4$. Based on the given information, answer the following questions : (i) Represent the given equations $C_1$ and $C_2$ with the help of a diagram. (ii) Express $y$ as a function of $x$, $(y = f(x))$, for both $C_1$ and $C_2$. (iii)(a) Using integration find the area of region covered by the roundabout.  OR  (iii)(b) Using integration, find the area of region covered by circular pond.

answer.text: The roundabout boundary is $C_1:x^2+y^2=64$ (radius $8$) and the circular pond is $C_2:x^2+y^2=4$ (radius $2$). (i) $C_1$ and $C_2$ are concentric circles centred at the origin (see figure). (ii) $C_1:y=\sqrt{64-x^2}$ or $y=-\sqrt{64-x^2}$; $C_2:y=\sqrt{4-x^2}$ or $y=-\sqrt{4-x^2}$. (iii)(a) Area of the roundabout $=4\displaystyle\int_0^8\sqrt{64-x^2}\,dx=2\left[x\sqrt{64-x^2}+64\sin^{-1}\dfrac{x}{8}\right]_0^8=64\pi$. OR (iii)(b) Area of the pond $=4\displaystyle\int_0^2\sqrt{4-x^2}\,dx=2\left[x\sqrt{4-x^2}+4\sin^{-1}\dfrac{x}{2}\right]_0^2=4\pi$.

questions.text: Which of the following expressions will give the area of region bounded by the curve $y = x^2$ and line $y = 16$ ?

answer.text: $2\displaystyle\int_{0}^{16} \sqrt{y}\,dy$

questions.text: A racing track is build around an elliptical ground whose equation is given by $9x^2 + 16y^2 = 144$. The width of the track is 3 m as shown below. Based on given information, answer the following questions : (i) Express $y$ as a function of $x$ from the given equation of ellipse. (ii) Integrate the function obtained in (i) with respect to $x$. (iii)(a) Find the area of the region enclosed within the elliptical ground excluding the track using integration.  OR  (iii)(b) Write the co-ordinates of the points P and Q where the outer edge of the track cuts $x$ axis and $y$ axis in first quadrant and find the area of the triangle formed by points P, O, Q using integration.

answer.text: The elliptical ground is $9x^2+16y^2=144$, i.e. $a=4$, $b=3$. (i) $y=\dfrac{3}{4}\sqrt{16-x^2}$. (ii) $\displaystyle\int y\,dx=\dfrac{3}{4}\int\sqrt{16-x^2}\,dx=\dfrac{3}{4}\left[\dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{16-x^2}+8\sin^{-1}\dfrac{x}{4}\right]+C$. (iii)(a) Area of the region enclosed within the elliptical ground $=4\displaystyle\int_0^4\dfrac{3}{4}\sqrt{16-x^2}\,dx=3\left[\dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{16-x^2}+8\sin^{-1}\dfrac{x}{4}\right]_0^4=3\left(8\cdot\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)=12\pi$. OR (iii)(b) The outer edge meets the axes at $P(7,0)$ and $Q(0,6)$; line $PQ$ is $\dfrac{x}{7}+\dfrac{y}{6}=1$, i.e. $y=\dfrac{6}{7}(7-x)$. Area of $\triangle POQ=\displaystyle\int_0^7\dfrac{6}{7}(7-x)\,dx=\dfrac{6}{7}\left[\dfrac{(7-x)^2}{-2}\right]_0^7=21$.

questions.text: The area of the shaded region of the circle given below is equal to :

answer.text: $2\displaystyle\int_{1}^{3} \sqrt{9 - y^2}\,dy$

questions.text: There is a triangular park in the society. The park is divided into two sections as shown in the figure. In region OAC, children are allowed to play games like cricket and football, while running games are not allowed in region AOB. The vertices of the triangular park ABC are $A(0, 4)$, $B(-2, 0)$ and $C(3, 0)$. Based on the above information, answer the following questions : (i) Write the equation of boundary line AB of the park. (ii) Write the equation of boundary line AC of the park. (iii)(a) Using integration, find the area of region OAC, in which playing cricket and football is allowed.  OR  (iii)(b) Using integration, find the area of region AOB.

answer.text: The triangular park has vertices $A(0,4)$, $B(-2,0)$, $C(3,0)$. (i) Boundary line $AB$: $2x-y+4=0$. (ii) Boundary line $AC$: $4x+3y=12$. (iii)(a) Area of region $OAC=\displaystyle\int_0^3\dfrac{12-4x}{3}\,dx=\dfrac{1}{3}\big[12x-2x^2\big]_0^3=6$ square units. OR (iii)(b) Area of region $AOB=\displaystyle\int_{-2}^{0}(2x+4)\,dx=\big[x^2+4x\big]_{-2}^{0}=4$ square units.

Integrating factor $=e^{\int \sec^2 x\,dx}=e^{\tan x}$
Solution is $y\,e^{\tan x}=\displaystyle\int \tan x\,\sec^2 x\,e^{\tan x}\,dx+C$
Let $\tan x=t$, $\sec^2 x\,dx=dt$
$\therefore\ \displaystyle\int e^{\tan x}\tan x\,\sec^2 x\,dx=\int e^t\,t\,dt=e^t(t-1)$
$\therefore\ y\,e^{\tan x}=e^{\tan x}(\tan x-1)+C$
$y(0)=0$ gives $C=1$
Particular solution is $y\,e^{\tan x}=e^{\tan x}(\tan x-1)+1$ or $y=\tan x-1+e^{-\tan x}$

questions.text: Solve the differential equation given by $x\,dy - y\,dx - \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}\,dx = 0$.
