answer.text:
Given differential equation can be written as $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{y}{x}+\sqrt{1+\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)^2}$ \ \ ...(i)
Let $y=vx\Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{dx}=v+x\dfrac{dv}{dx}$; substituting in (i)
We get $v+x\dfrac{dv}{dx}=v+\sqrt{1+v^2}$
$\Rightarrow\ \dfrac{dv}{\sqrt{1+v^2}}=\dfrac{dx}{x}$
Integrating both sides, we get $\log\left|\sqrt{1+v^2}+v\right|=\log|x|+\log C$
$y+\sqrt{x^2+y^2}=Cx^2$

questions.text: Find the general solution of the differential equation $(xy - x^2)\,dy = y^2\,dx$.

answer.text:
Given differential equation can be written as $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{y^2}{xy-x^2}=\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)^2}{\dfrac{y}{x}-1}$
Put $y=ux$, $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=u+x\dfrac{du}{dx}$
$\therefore u+x\dfrac{du}{dx}=\dfrac{u^2}{u-1}\Rightarrow x\dfrac{du}{dx}=\dfrac{u}{u-1}$
Separating the variables and integrating: $\displaystyle\int\left(1-\dfrac1u\right)du=\int\dfrac{dx}{x}$
$\Rightarrow u-\log u=\log|x|+c\Rightarrow \dfrac{y}{x}-\log\dfrac{y}{x}=\log|x|+c$

questions.text: Find the general solution of the differential equation $(x^2 + 1)\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2xy = \sqrt{x^2 + 4}$.

Integrating factor $=e^{\int\frac{2x}{1+x^2}\,dx}=e^{\log(1+x^2)}=1+x^2$
$\therefore$ solution is $y(1+x^2)=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{\sqrt{x^2+4}}{1+x^2}\cdot(1+x^2)\,dx+c=\int\sqrt{x^2+4}\,dx+c$
$\therefore y(1+x^2)=\dfrac{x\sqrt{x^2+4}}{2}+2\log\left|x+\sqrt{x^2+4}\right|+c$

questions.text: An equation involving derivatives of the dependent variable with respect to the independent variables is called a differential equation. A differential equation of the form $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = F(x, y)$ is said to be homogeneous if $F(x, y)$ is a homogeneous function of degree zero, whereas a function $F(x, y)$ is a homogeneous function of degree $n$ if $F(\lambda x, \lambda y) = \lambda^n F(x, y)$. To solve a homogeneous differential equation of the type $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = F(x, y) = g\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)$, we make the substitution $y = vx$ and then separate the variables. Based on the above, answer the following questions : (I) Show that $(x^2 - y^2)\,dx + 2xy\,dy = 0$ is a differential equation of the type $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = g\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)$. (II) Solve the above equation to find its general solution.
questions.topic: Methods of Solving First Order, First Degree Differential Equations

answer.text:
(I) $(x^2-y^2)\,dx+2xy\,dy=0$
$\Rightarrow\ \dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{y^2-x^2}{2xy}=\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)^2-1}{2\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)}=g\!\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)$, so it is homogeneous.
(II) $y=vx\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{dx}=v+x\dfrac{dv}{dx}$
$v+x\dfrac{dv}{dx}=\dfrac{v^2-1}{2v}\Rightarrow x\dfrac{dv}{dx}=\dfrac{v^2-1}{2v}-v=\dfrac{-1-v^2}{2v}$
$\Rightarrow\ \displaystyle\int\dfrac{2v}{1+v^2}\,dv=-\int\dfrac{dx}{x}$
$\Rightarrow\ \log|1+v^2|+\log|x|=\log C$
$\Rightarrow\ x\left(1+\dfrac{y^2}{x^2}\right)=C$ \ or \ $x^2+y^2=Cx$

$\Rightarrow\dfrac12\log\left|\dfrac{v}{v+2}\right|=\log\left|\dfrac{C}{x}\right|$

questions.text: During a heavy gaming session, the temperature of a student's laptop processor increases significantly. After the session, the processor begins to cool down, and the rate of cooling is proportional to the difference between the processor's temperature and the room temperature $(25°C)$. Initially the processor's temperature is $85°C$. The rate of cooling is defined by the equation $\dfrac{d}{dt}(T(t)) = -k(T(t) - 25)$, where $T(t)$ represents the temperature of the processor at time $t$ (in minutes) and $k$ is a constant. Based on the above information, answer the following questions : (i) Find the expression for temperature of processor, $T(t)$ given that $T(0) = 85°C$. (ii) How long will it take for the processor's temperature to reach $40°C$ ? Given that $k = 0{\cdot}03$, $\log_e 4 = 1{\cdot}3863$.

answer.text:
(i) $\dfrac{dT}{dt}=-k(T-25)\Rightarrow\dfrac{dT}{T-25}=-k\,dt$
$\Rightarrow\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dT}{T-25}=-k\int dt\Rightarrow\log|T-25|=-kt+C$
When $t=0,\ T=85\Rightarrow\log 60=C$
$\therefore\log|T-25|=-kt+\log 60$
(ii) When $k=0{\cdot}03,\ \log\left|\dfrac{T-25}{60}\right|=-0{\cdot}03t\Rightarrow T-25=60\,e^{-0{\cdot}03t}$
When $T=40,\ t=t_1:\ \dfrac{15}{60}=e^{-0{\cdot}03t_1}\Rightarrow e^{-0{\cdot}03t_1}=\dfrac14\Rightarrow-0{\cdot}03t_1=-\log 4$
$\Rightarrow t_1=\dfrac{\log 4}{0{\cdot}03}=\dfrac{1{\cdot}3863}{0{\cdot}03}=46{\cdot}21$ minutes.

answer.text:
The given differential equation can be written as $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{yx^2}{x^3+y^3}$

$\Rightarrow\left(\dfrac{1}{v^4}+\dfrac1v\right)dv=\dfrac{-dx}{x}$
Integrating: $\dfrac{-1}{3v^3}+\log|v|=-\log|x|+C\Rightarrow\dfrac{-x^3}{3y^3}+\log|y|=C$

questions.text: Solve the differential equation $(1 + x^2)\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2xy - 4x^2 = 0$ subject to initial condition $y(0) = 0$.
questions.topic: Methods of Solving First Order, First Degree Differential Equations

answer.text:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac{2x}{1+x^2}y=\dfrac{4x^2}{1+x^2}$
Integrating factor $=e^{\int\frac{2x}{1+x^2}dx}=e^{\log(1+x^2)}=(1+x^2)$
Solution is $y(1+x^2)=\displaystyle\int4x^2\,dx+C\Rightarrow y(1+x^2)=\dfrac{4x^3}{3}+C$
$y(0)=0$ gives $C=0$, hence solution is $y(1+x^2)=\dfrac{4x^3}{3}$

questions.text: Solve the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \cos x - 2y$.
questions.topic: Methods of Solving First Order, First Degree Differential Equations

answer.text:
The given differential equation can be written as $\dfrac{dy}{dx}+2y=\cos x$, taking $P=2,\ Q=\cos x$
Integrating factor is $I=e^{\int2\,dx}=e^{2x}$
$\therefore$ The solution is $y\cdot e^{2x}=\displaystyle\int e^{2x}\cos x\,dx$
Let $I_1=\displaystyle\int\cos x\cdot e^{2x}\,dx=\cos x\dfrac{e^{2x}}{2}-\int(-\sin x)\dfrac{e^{2x}}{2}\,dx=\dfrac{e^{2x}\cos x}{2}+\dfrac12\left[\sin x\cdot\dfrac{e^{2x}}{2}-\int\cos x\cdot\dfrac{e^{2x}}{2}\,dx\right]$
$\Rightarrow I_1=\dfrac{e^{2x}\cos x}{2}+\dfrac{e^{2x}\sin x}{4}-\dfrac14 I_1\Rightarrow I_1=\dfrac{e^{2x}}{5}(2\cos x+\sin x)$
$\therefore y\cdot e^{2x}=\dfrac{e^{2x}}{5}(2\cos x+\sin x)+C\Rightarrow y=\dfrac15(2\cos x+\sin x)+Ce^{-2x}$

questions.text: Camphor is a waxy, colourless solid with strong aroma that evaporates through the process of sublimation, if left in the open at room temperature. A cylindrical camphor tablet whose height is equal to its radius ($r$) evaporates when exposed to air such that the rate of reduction of its volume is proportional to its total surface area. Thus, $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = kS$ is the differential equation, where V is the volume, S is the surface area and $t$ is the time in hours. Based upon the above information, answer the following questions : (i) Write the order and degree of the given differential equation. (ii) Substituting $V = \pi r^3$ and $S = 2\pi r^2$, we get the differential equation $\dfrac{dr}{dt} = \dfrac{2}{3}k$. Solve it, given that $r(0) = 5$ mm. (iii)(a) If it is given that $r = 3$ mm when $t = 1$ hour, find the value of $k$. Hence, find $t$ for $r = 0$ mm.  OR  (iii)(b) If it is given that $r = 1$ mm when $t = 1$ hour, find the value of $k$. Hence, find $t$ for $r = 0$ mm.
questions.topic: General and Particular Solutions of a Differential Equation

answer.text:
(i) Order $=1$, Degree $=1$
(ii) Separating the variables and integrating: $\displaystyle\int dr=\dfrac{2k}{3}\int dt\Rightarrow r=\dfrac{2}{3}kt+C$. Putting $t=0,\ r=5$, we get $C=5$; $\therefore r=\dfrac23 kt+5$
(iii)(a) Putting $r=3,\ t=1$: $3=\dfrac23 k(1)+5\Rightarrow k=-3$. $\therefore r=-2t+5$; for $r=0,\ t=\dfrac52$ hours or $2{\cdot}5$ hours.

questions.text: Find the general solution of the following differential equation : $x^2\dfrac{dy}{dx} = x^2 + xy + y^2$.

answer.text: $x^2\dfrac{dy}{dx}=x^2+xy+y^2\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{dx}=1+\dfrac{y}{x}+\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)^2$. Put $y=vx\Rightarrow v+x\dfrac{dv}{dx}=1+v+v^2\Rightarrow x\dfrac{dv}{dx}=1+v^2\Rightarrow\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dv}{1+v^2}=\int\dfrac{dx}{x}\Rightarrow\tan^{-1}v=\log|x|+C\Rightarrow\tan^{-1}\dfrac{y}{x}=\log|x|+C$.

questions.text: Find the particular solution of the differential equation $xy\dfrac{dy}{dx} = (x + 2)(y + 2)$, given that $y(1) = -1$.
questions.topic: Methods of Solving First Order, First Degree Differential Equations

answer.text: $xy\dfrac{dy}{dx}=(x+2)(y+2)$, $y(1)=-1$. Separating: $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{y}{y+2}\,dy=\int\dfrac{x+2}{x}\,dx\Rightarrow\int\left(1-\dfrac{2}{y+2}\right)dy=\int\left(1+\dfrac{2}{x}\right)dx\Rightarrow y-2\log|y+2|=x+2\log|x|+C$. Using $y(1)=-1$ gives $C=-2$. Particular solution: $y-2\log|y+2|=x+2\log|x|-2$.

questions.text: Solve the following differential equation : $x\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y - x\sin^2\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)$, given that $y(1) = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

answer.text: $x\dfrac{dy}{dx}=y-x\sin^2\!\dfrac{y}{x}\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{y}{x}-\sin^2\!\dfrac{y}{x}$. Put $\dfrac{y}{x}=v\Rightarrow v+x\dfrac{dv}{dx}=v-\sin^2 v\Rightarrow x\dfrac{dv}{dx}=-\sin^2 v\Rightarrow-\displaystyle\int\csc^2 v\,dv=\int\dfrac{dx}{x}\Rightarrow\cot v=\log|x|+C\Rightarrow\cot\!\dfrac{y}{x}=\log|x|+C$. Using $y(1)=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ gives $C=\sqrt{3}$. Solution: $\cot\!\dfrac{y}{x}=\log|x|+\sqrt{3}$.

questions.text: Find the general solution of the differential equation : $y\log y\dfrac{dx}{dy} + x = \dfrac{2}{y}$.
questions.topic: Methods of Solving First Order, First Degree Differential Equations

answer.text: $y\log y\,\dfrac{dx}{dy}+x=\dfrac{2}{y}\Rightarrow\dfrac{dx}{dy}+\dfrac{x}{y\log y}=\dfrac{2}{y^2\log y}$. $\text{I.F.}=e^{\int\frac{dy}{y\log y}}=\log y$. Solution: $x\log y=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{2}{y^2\log y}\cdot\log y\,dy=\int\dfrac{2}{y^2}\,dy=-\dfrac{2}{y}+C$, i.e. $x\log y=-\dfrac{2}{y}+C$.

answer.text: $2x^2\dfrac{dy}{dx}=y^2+2xy\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)^2+\dfrac{y}{x}$. Put $y=vx\Rightarrow v+x\dfrac{dv}{dx}=\dfrac{1}{2}v^2+v\Rightarrow\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dv}{v^2}=\int\dfrac{dx}{2x}\Rightarrow-\dfrac{1}{v}=\dfrac{1}{2}\log x+c\Rightarrow-\dfrac{x}{y}=\dfrac{1}{2}\log x+c$.

questions.text: Find a particular solution of the differential equation $(x + 1)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2e^{-y} - 1$, given that $y = 0$ when $x = 0$.

answer.text: $(x+1)\dfrac{dy}{dx}=2e^{-y}-1\Rightarrow\displaystyle\int\dfrac{e^y}{2-e^y}\,dy=\int\dfrac{dx}{x+1}$. Put $2-e^y=t\Rightarrow-\int\dfrac{dt}{t}=\log|x+1|\Rightarrow-\log|t|=\log|x+1|-\log|c|\Rightarrow(x+1)(2-e^y)=c$. Using $y=0$ at $x=0$ gives $c=1$. Particular solution: $(x+1)(2-e^y)=1$.

questions.text: Solve the differential equation $y\,e^y\,dx = (y^3 + 2x\,e^y)\,dy$, when $y(0) = 1$.
questions.topic: Methods of Solving First Order, First Degree Differential Equations

answer.text: $ye^y\,dx=(y^3+2xe^y)\,dy\Rightarrow\dfrac{dx}{dy}-\dfrac{2}{y}x=y^2e^{-y}$. $\text{I.F.}=e^{\int(-2/y)\,dy}=\dfrac{1}{y^2}$. Solution: $x\cdot\dfrac{1}{y^2}=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{1}{y^2}\cdot y^2e^{-y}\,dy=-e^{-y}+c\Rightarrow x=y^2(-e^{-y}+c)$. Using $x=0$ at $y=1$: $0=-e^{-1}+c\Rightarrow c=e^{-1}$. Particular solution: $x=y^2\left(e^{-1}-e^{-y}\right)$.

questions.text: Find the general solution of the differential equation $(x^3 - 3xy^2)\,dx = (y^3 - 3x^2y)\,dy$.

answer.text: $(x^3-3xy^2)\,dx=(y^3-3x^2y)\,dy\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{x^3-3xy^2}{y^3-3x^2y}$. This is homogeneous; put $y=vx$ to get $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{3v-v^3}{v^4-1}\,dv=\int\dfrac{dx}{x}\Rightarrow\dfrac{3}{4}\log\left|\dfrac{v^2-1}{v^2+1}\right|-\dfrac{1}{4}\log|v^4-1|=\log x+c$. Substituting $v=\dfrac{y}{x}$: $\dfrac{3}{4}\log\left|\dfrac{y^2-x^2}{y^2+x^2}\right|-\dfrac{1}{4}\log\left|\dfrac{y^4-x^4}{x^4}\right|=\log x+c$.

answer.text:
Let $ABCD$ be the parallelogram with diagonals $\overrightarrow{AB}=\vec a$ and $\overrightarrow{BD}=\vec b$.
$\therefore\overrightarrow{AB}=\dfrac12(\vec a-\vec b)$ and $\overrightarrow{AD}=\dfrac12(\vec a+\vec b)$
Area of $ABCD=\left|\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AD}\right|=\left|\dfrac12(\vec a-\vec b)\times\dfrac12(\vec a+\vec b)\right|=\dfrac14\left|\vec a\times\vec a+\vec a\times\vec b-\vec b\times\vec a-\vec b\times\vec b\right|$
$=\dfrac14\left|2(\vec a\times\vec b)\right|=\dfrac12\left|\vec a\times\vec b\right|\qquad(\because\vec a\times\vec a=\vec0)$
Given $\vec a=2\hat i-\hat j+\hat k,\ \vec b=\hat i+3\hat j-\hat k$
$\vec a\times\vec b=\begin{vmatrix}\hat i&\hat j&\hat k\\2&-1&1\\1&3&-1\end{vmatrix}=-2\hat i+3\hat j+7\hat k$
$|\vec a\times\vec b|=\sqrt{62}$; $\therefore$ Area of parallelogram $=\dfrac12\sqrt{62}$

questions.text: Let $\vec{a}$, $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ be three vectors such that $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} = \vec{a} \cdot \vec{c}$ and $\vec{a} \times \vec{b} = \vec{a} \times \vec{c}$, $\vec{a} \neq \vec{0}$. Show that $\vec{b} = \vec{c}$.

answer.text:
$\vec a\cdot\vec b=\vec a\cdot\vec c\Rightarrow\vec a\cdot(\vec b-\vec c)=0\Rightarrow$ either $\vec b=\vec c$ or $\vec a\perp(\vec b-\vec c)$, since $\vec a\neq\vec0$.
Also, $\vec a\times\vec b=\vec a\times\vec c\Rightarrow\vec a\times(\vec b-\vec c)=0\Rightarrow$ either $\vec b=\vec c$ or $\vec a\parallel(\vec b-\vec c)$, since $\vec a\neq\vec0$.
Since vectors $\vec a$ and $(\vec b-\vec c)$ cannot be parallel and perpendicular simultaneously, hence $\vec b=\vec c$.

answer.text: $|\vec{a}|=|\vec{b}|=1$. $|\vec{a}+2\vec{b}|=|2\vec{a}-\vec{b}|\Rightarrow|\vec{a}|^2+4|\vec{b}|^2+4\,\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=4|\vec{a}|^2+|\vec{b}|^2-4\,\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}\Rightarrow 8\,\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=0\Rightarrow\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=0$. Hence the angle between $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ is $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

questions.text: If the position vectors of three points A, B and C are $3\hat{i} + \hat{j}$, $5\hat{i} + 6\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}$ and $4\hat{j}$ respectively, then show that they form an isosceles triangle.

answer.text: With position vectors $A=3\hat{i}+\hat{j}$, $B=5\hat{i}+6\hat{j}-3\hat{k}$, $C=4\hat{j}$: $\vec{AB}=2\hat{i}+5\hat{j}-3\hat{k}$, $\vec{BC}=-5\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$, $\vec{CA}=3\hat{i}-3\hat{j}$. Then $|\vec{AB}|=|\vec{BC}|=\sqrt{38}$ and $|\vec{CA}|=\sqrt{18}$. Since two sides are equal, the points form an isosceles triangle.

questions.text: Let two rods placed on the ground be represented by vectors $4\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$ and $-2\hat{i} + \hat{j} - 2\hat{k}$. Find a vector representing a flag-post of height 5 m that has to be erected perpendicular to both the rods.

answer.text: With $\vec{a}=4\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}=-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}$: $\vec{a}\times\vec{b}=-\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$, $|\vec{a}\times\vec{b}|=3$. The flag-post of length $5$ m perpendicular to both is $5\cdot\dfrac{\vec{a}\times\vec{b}}{|\vec{a}\times\vec{b}|}=\pm\left(-\dfrac{5}{3}\hat{i}+\dfrac{10}{3}\hat{j}+\dfrac{10}{3}\hat{k}\right)$.

questions.text: A unit vector $\vec{a}$ is such that it makes an angle $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ with x-axis, $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ with y-axis and an acute angle $\theta$ with z-axis. Find $\theta$ and the components of $\vec{a}$.

answer.text: A unit vector $\vec{a}$ makes $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ with the $x$-axis, $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ with the $y$-axis and an acute angle $\theta$ with the $z$-axis. Then $\cos^2\dfrac{\pi}{4}+\cos^2\dfrac{\pi}{3}+\cos^2\theta=1\Rightarrow\dfrac{1}{2}+\dfrac{1}{4}+\cos^2\theta=1\Rightarrow\cos\theta=\dfrac{1}{2}$ ($\theta$ acute) $\Rightarrow\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$. The components of $\vec{a}$ are $\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}},\dfrac{1}{2},\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$.

questions.text: If A, B and C be three non-collinear points such that $\overrightarrow{AB} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - \hat{k}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC} = 2\hat{i} - 3\hat{j}$, then find the area of $\triangle ABC$.

answer.text: $\vec{AB}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$, $\vec{AC}=2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}$. Area of $\triangle ABC=\dfrac{1}{2}|\vec{AB}\times\vec{AC}|=\dfrac{1}{2}|-3\hat{i}-2\hat{j}-7\hat{k}|=\dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{9+4+49}=\dfrac{\sqrt{62}}{2}$ square units.

questions.text: If $\vec{a}$, $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ are unit vectors, then prove that $|\vec{a} - \vec{b}|^2 + |\vec{b} - \vec{c}|^2 + |\vec{c} - \vec{a}|^2 \leq 9$.

answer.text: $|\vec{a}|=|\vec{b}|=|\vec{c}|=1$. $|\vec{a}-\vec{b}|^2+|\vec{b}-\vec{c}|^2+|\vec{c}-\vec{a}|^2=2\big(|\vec{a}|^2+|\vec{b}|^2+|\vec{c}|^2\big)-2\big(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}+\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c}+\vec{c}\cdot\vec{a}\big)=3\big(|\vec{a}|^2+|\vec{b}|^2+|\vec{c}|^2\big)-|\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}|^2=9-|\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}|^2\le 9$. Hence proved.

questions.text: Three vectors $\vec{a}$, $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ satisfy the condition $\vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c} = \vec{0}$. Evaluate the quantity $\mu = \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} + \vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} + \vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}$, if $|\vec{a}| = 3$, $|\vec{b}| = 4$ and $|\vec{c}| = 2$.

questions.text: During a cricket match, the position of the bowler, the wicket keeper and the leg slip fielder are in a line given by $\vec{B} = 2\hat{i} + 8\hat{j}$, $\vec{W} = 6\hat{i} + 12\hat{j}$ and $\vec{F} = 12\hat{i} + 18\hat{j}$ respectively. Let the wicket keeper divide the line segment in ratio $k:1$: $\vec W=\dfrac{k\vec F+1\cdot\vec B}{k+1}$

Hence, the required ratio is $2:3$.

answer.text:
The two given lines are parallel, with $\vec{a_1}=2\hat i-\hat j+3\hat k,\ \vec{a_2}=\hat i+4\hat k$
Then $\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1}=-\hat i+\hat j+\hat k$ and the parallel vector is $\vec b=\hat i-2\hat j+3\hat k$
$\vec b\times(\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1})=\begin{vmatrix}\hat i&\hat j&\hat k\\1&-2&3\\-1&1&1\end{vmatrix}=-5\hat i-4\hat j-\hat k$
Shortest Distance $=\dfrac{|\vec b\times(\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1})|}{|\vec b|}=\dfrac{\sqrt{42}}{\sqrt{14}}=\sqrt3$

and Cartesian equation: $\dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac{y-2}{3}=\dfrac{z+4}{6}$

$\therefore\ d=\dfrac{\sqrt{293}}{7}$

$\Rightarrow\dfrac{2\lambda+1-4}{5}=\dfrac{3\lambda+2-1}{2}=4\lambda+3\Rightarrow\lambda=-1$
$\therefore$ point of intersection is $(-1,-1,-1)$

questions.text: Show that the following lines do not intersect each other : $\dfrac{x-1}{3} = \dfrac{y+1}{2} = \dfrac{z-1}{5}$; $\dfrac{x+2}{4} = \dfrac{y-1}{3} = \dfrac{z+1}{-2}$.

answer.text:
Shortest Distance $=\dfrac{\begin{vmatrix}-3&2&-2\\3&2&5\\4&3&-2\end{vmatrix}}{\sqrt{(2\times-2-5\times3)^2+(3\times-2-4\times5)^2+(3\times3-2\times4)^2}}$
$=\dfrac{-3(-19)-2(-26)-2(1)}{\sqrt{361+676+1}}=\dfrac{57+52-2}{\sqrt{1038}}=\dfrac{107}{\sqrt{1038}}\neq0$
So, the lines will not intersect each other.

questions.text: Find the angle between the lines $2x = 3y = -z$ and $6x = -y = -4z$.

answer.text:
The given lines are $\dfrac{x}{1/2}=\dfrac{y}{1/3}=\dfrac{z}{-1}$ and $\dfrac{x}{1/6}=\dfrac{y}{-1}=\dfrac{z}{-1/4}$, i.e. $\dfrac{x}{3}=\dfrac{y}{2}=\dfrac{z}{-6}$ and $\dfrac{x}{2}=\dfrac{y}{-12}=\dfrac{z}{-3}$
Let $\theta$ be the angle between the two lines, then
$\cos\theta=\left|\dfrac{(3\times2)+(2\times-12)+(-6)(-3)}{\sqrt{9+4+36}\,\sqrt{4+144+9}}\right|=\left|\dfrac{6-24+18}{7\times\sqrt{157}}\right|=0\Rightarrow\theta=90^\circ$

answer.text:
The given line $5x-25=14-7y=35z$ can be written as $\dfrac{x-5}{7}=\dfrac{y-2}{-5}=\dfrac{z}{1}$
$\therefore$ direction ratios of the given line are $\langle 7,-5,1\rangle$.
Vector equation of the required line through $A(1,2,-1)$:
$\vec r=(\hat i+2\hat j-\hat k)+\lambda(7\hat i-5\hat j+\hat k)$
Cartesian equation: $\dfrac{x-1}{7}=\dfrac{y-2}{-5}=\dfrac{z+1}{1}$

questions.text: Find the coordinates of the foot of the perpendicular drawn from the point $P(0, 2, 3)$ to the line $\dfrac{x + 3}{5} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = \dfrac{z + 4}{3}$.

answer.text:
General point on the given line is $M(5\lambda-3,\ 2\lambda+1,\ 3\lambda-4)$.
Direction ratios of $PM$ are $\langle 5\lambda-3,\ 2\lambda-1,\ 3\lambda-7\rangle$.
Since $PM$ is perpendicular to the line, $(5\lambda-3)5+(2\lambda-1)2+(3\lambda-7)3=0\Rightarrow\lambda=1$
$\therefore$ coordinates of the foot of perpendicular $M$ are $(2,3,-1)$.

questions.text: Find the distance between the lines : $\vec{r} = (\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 4\hat{k}) + \lambda(2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 6\hat{k})$; $\vec{r} = (3\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 5\hat{k}) + \mu(4\hat{i} + 6\hat{j} + 12\hat{k})$.

answer.text:
Here $\vec{a_1}=\hat i+2\hat j-4\hat k$, \ $\vec{b_1}=2\hat i+3\hat j+6\hat k$
$\vec{a_2}=3\hat i+3\hat j-5\hat k$, \ $\vec{b_2}=4\hat i+6\hat j+12\hat k$
Here $\vec{b_1}$ and $\vec{b_2}$ are parallel vectors, so $\vec b=2\hat i+3\hat j+6\hat k$.
$\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1}=2\hat i+\hat j-\hat k$
$(\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1})\times\vec b=\begin{vmatrix}\hat i&\hat j&\hat k\\2&1&-1\\2&3&6\end{vmatrix}=9\hat i-14\hat j+4\hat k$
Distance $=\dfrac{|(\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1})\times\vec b|}{|\vec b|}=\dfrac{\sqrt{81+196+16}}{\sqrt{4+9+36}}=\dfrac{\sqrt{293}}{7}$ units.

questions.text: Find the equation of the line passing through the point of intersection of the lines $\dfrac{x}{1} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = \dfrac{z - 2}{3}$ and $\dfrac{x - 1}{0} = \dfrac{y}{-3} = \dfrac{z - 7}{2}$ and perpendicular to these two lines.
questions.topic: Equation of a Line in Space

answer.text:
$l_1:\dfrac{x}{1}=\dfrac{y-1}{2}=\dfrac{z-2}{3}=\lambda$; \ $l_2:\dfrac{x-1}{0}=\dfrac{y}{-3}=\dfrac{z-7}{2}=\mu$
Any point on $l_1$ is $(\lambda,2\lambda+1,3\lambda+2)$ and any point on $l_2$ is $(1,-3\mu,2\mu+7)$.
If $l_1$ and $l_2$ intersect: $\lambda=1,\ 2\lambda+1=-3\mu$ and $3\lambda+2=2\mu+7\Rightarrow\lambda=1,\ \mu=-1$
Point of intersection of $l_1$ and $l_2$ is $(1,3,5)$.
Let d.r.'s of required line be $\langle a,b,c\rangle$. Then $a+2b+3c=0$ and $-3b+2c=0\Rightarrow\dfrac{a}{13}=\dfrac{b}{-2}=\dfrac{c}{-3}$
Required equation of line is $\dfrac{x-1}{13}=\dfrac{y-3}{-2}=\dfrac{z-5}{-3}$

questions.text: Two vertices of the parallelogram ABCD are given as $A(-1, 2, 1)$ and $B(1, -2, 5)$. If the line passing through C and D is $\dfrac{x - 4}{1} = \dfrac{y + 7}{-2} = \dfrac{z - 8}{2}$, then find the distance between sides AB and CD. Hence, find the area of parallelogram ABCD.
questions.topic: Equation of a Line in Space

answer.text:
Equation of $AB$ is $\dfrac{x+1}{1}=\dfrac{y-2}{-2}=\dfrac{z-1}{2}$; \ Equation of $CD$ is $\dfrac{x-4}{1}=\dfrac{y+7}{-2}=\dfrac{z-8}{2}$
Let $\vec{a_1}=-\hat i+2\hat j+\hat k,\ \vec{a_2}=4\hat i-7\hat j+8\hat k$ and $\vec b=\hat i-2\hat j+2\hat k$
$\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1}=5\hat i-9\hat j+7\hat k$; \ $(\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1})\times\vec b=\begin{vmatrix}\hat i&\hat j&\hat k\\5&-9&7\\1&-2&2\end{vmatrix}=-4\hat i-3\hat j-\hat k$
Distance between $AB$ and $CD$: $d=\dfrac{|(\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1})\times\vec b|}{|\vec b|}=\dfrac{\sqrt{16+9+1}}{\sqrt{1+4+4}}=\dfrac{\sqrt{26}}{3}$
$CD=\sqrt{2^2+(-4)^2+4^2}=6$; \ Area of parallelogram $ABCD=b\times h=6\times\dfrac{\sqrt{26}}{3}=2\sqrt{26}$

answer.text:
$L_1:\dfrac{x}{2}=\dfrac{y-3}{2}=\dfrac{z-1}{1}$; \ $L_2:\dfrac{x-4}{2}=\dfrac{y}{2}=\dfrac{z+5}{1}$ (parallel, through $(4,0,-5)$)
$L_1:\vec r=(0\hat i+3\hat j+\hat k)+\lambda(2\hat i+2\hat j+\hat k)$; \ $L_2:\vec r=(4\hat i+0\hat j-5\hat k)+\mu(2\hat i+2\hat j+\hat k)$
$\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1}=4\hat i-3\hat j-6\hat k$; \ $\vec b=2\hat i+2\hat j+\hat k$
$(\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1})\times\vec b=\begin{vmatrix}\hat i&\hat j&\hat k\\4&-3&-6\\2&2&1\end{vmatrix}=9\hat i-16\hat j+14\hat k$; \ $|\vec b|=\sqrt{4+4+1}=3$
$\text{S.D.}=\dfrac{|(\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1})\times\vec b|}{|\vec b|}=\dfrac{\sqrt{81+256+196}}{3}=\dfrac{\sqrt{533}}{3}$ units.

questions.text: If the lines $\dfrac{x - 1}{-3} = \dfrac{y - 2}{2k} = \dfrac{z - 3}{2}$ and $\dfrac{x - 1}{3k} = \dfrac{y - 1}{1} = \dfrac{z - 6}{-7}$ are perpendicular to each other, find the value of $k$ and hence write the vector equation of a line perpendicular to these two lines and passing through the point $(3, -4, 5)$.

answer.text:
$L_1:\dfrac{x-1}{-3}=\dfrac{y-2}{2k}=\dfrac{z-3}{2}$, d.r.'s $\langle-3,2k,2\rangle$; \ $L_2:\dfrac{x-1}{3k}=\dfrac{y-1}{1}=\dfrac{z-6}{-7}$, d.r.'s $\langle3k,1,-7\rangle$
Since $L_1\perp L_2$: $-9k+2k-14=0\Rightarrow k=-2$
d.r.'s of $L_1=\langle-3,-4,2\rangle$, d.r.'s of $L_2=\langle-6,1,-7\rangle$
Vector perpendicular to both: $\vec b=\begin{vmatrix}\hat i&\hat j&\hat k\\-3&-4&2\\-6&1&-7\end{vmatrix}=26\hat i-33\hat j-27\hat k$
Equation of the required line: $\vec r=(3\hat i-4\hat j+7\hat k)+\lambda(26\hat i-33\hat j-27\hat k)$

questions.text: Find the co-ordinates of the foot of the perpendicular drawn from the point $(2, 3, -8)$ to the line $\dfrac{4 - x}{2} = \dfrac{y}{6} = \dfrac{1 - z}{3}$. Also, find the perpendicular distance of the given point from the line.

answer.text:
The standard form of the line is $\dfrac{x-4}{-2}=\dfrac{y}{6}=\dfrac{z-1}{-3}$.
Let foot of perpendicular from $A(2,3,-8)$ be $B(-2\lambda+4,\ 6\lambda,\ -3\lambda+1)$.
D-ratios of $AB$: $-2\lambda+2,\ 6\lambda-3,\ -3\lambda+9$
As $AB$ is perpendicular to the line: $-2(-2\lambda+2)+6(6\lambda-3)-3(-3\lambda+9)=0\Rightarrow\lambda=1$
$\therefore$ Foot of the perpendicular is $B(2,6,-2)$; \ Perpendicular distance $=AB=3\sqrt5$

questions.text: Find the shortest distance between the lines $L_1$ and $L_2$ given below : $L_1$ : The line passing through $(2, -1, 1)$ and parallel to $\dfrac{x}{1} = \dfrac{y}{1} = \dfrac{z}{3}$. $L_2$ : $\vec{r} = \hat{i} + (2\mu + 1)\hat{j} - (\mu + 2)\hat{k}$.

answer.text:
$L_1:\vec r=2\hat i-\hat j+\hat k+\lambda(\hat i+\hat j+3\hat k)$; \ $L_2:\vec r=(\hat i+\hat j-2\hat k)+\mu(2\hat j-\hat k)$
$\vec{a_1}=2\hat i-\hat j+\hat k,\ \vec{b_1}=\hat i+\hat j+3\hat k$; \ $\vec{a_2}=\hat i+\hat j-2\hat k,\ \vec{b_2}=2\hat j-\hat k$
$\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1}=-\hat i+2\hat j-3\hat k$; \ $\vec{b_1}\times\vec{b_2}=-7\hat i+\hat j+2\hat k$
Shortest Distance $=\dfrac{|(\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1})\cdot(\vec{b_1}\times\vec{b_2})|}{|\vec{b_1}\times\vec{b_2}|}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt6}$

questions.text: Verify that lines $\vec{r} = (1 - \lambda)\hat{i} + (\lambda - 2)\hat{j} + (3 - 2\lambda)\hat{k}$ and $\vec{r} = (\mu + 1)\hat{i} + (2\mu - 1)\hat{j} - (2\mu + 1)\hat{k}$ are skew lines. Hence, find shortest distance between the lines.

answer.text:
Rewriting the lines: $\vec r=(\hat i-2\hat j+3\hat k)+\lambda(-\hat i+\hat j-2\hat k)$ and $\vec r=(\hat i-\hat j-\hat k)+\mu(\hat i+2\hat j-2\hat k)$
$\vec{a_1}=\hat i-2\hat j+3\hat k,\ \vec{a_2}=\hat i-\hat j-\hat k,\ \vec{b_1}=-\hat i+\hat j-2\hat k,\ \vec{b_2}=\hat i+2\hat j-2\hat k$
The d.r.'s are not proportional, so the lines are not parallel.
$\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1}=\hat j-4\hat k$, \ $\vec{b_1}\times\vec{b_2}=2\hat i-4\hat j-3\hat k$
$(\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1})\cdot(\vec{b_1}\times\vec{b_2})=(\hat j-4\hat k)\cdot(2\hat i-4\hat j-3\hat k)=8\neq0$, so the lines do not intersect; hence they are skew.
Shortest Distance $=\dfrac{|(\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1})\cdot(\vec{b_1}\times\vec{b_2})|}{|\vec{b_1}\times\vec{b_2}|}=\dfrac{8}{\sqrt{4+16+9}}=\dfrac{8}{\sqrt{29}}$

questions.text: Find the image of the point $A'$ of the point $A(1, 6, 3)$ in the line $\dfrac{x}{1} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = \dfrac{z - 2}{3}$. Also, find the equation of the line joining A and $A'$.

answer.text:
The equation of given line is $\dfrac{x}{1}=\dfrac{y-1}{2}=\dfrac{z-2}{3}=\lambda$
Any arbitrary point on the line is $M(\lambda,2\lambda+1,3\lambda+2)$; d.r.'s of $AM$ are $\langle\lambda-1,2\lambda-5,3\lambda-1\rangle$
$1(\lambda-1)+2(2\lambda-5)+3(3\lambda-1)=0\Rightarrow\lambda=1$; $\therefore M(1,3,5)$ is the foot of perpendicular.
Let image $A'(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$. Since $M$ is mid-point of $AA'$: $M\!\left(\dfrac{1+\alpha}{2},\dfrac{6+\beta}{2},\dfrac{3+\gamma}{2}\right)=M(1,3,5)\Rightarrow A'(1,0,7)$
Also, equation of $AA'$ is $\dfrac{x-1}{0}=\dfrac{y-6}{-3}=\dfrac{z-3}{2}$

questions.text: Find a point P on the line $\dfrac{x + 3}{1} = \dfrac{y + 1}{4} = \dfrac{z - 6}{-9}$ such that its distance from point $Q(2, 4, -1)$ is 7 units. Also, find the equation of line joining P and Q.

answer.text:

Any point on the line is $P(\lambda-5,4\lambda-3,-9\lambda+6)$.
Since $PQ=7\Rightarrow\sqrt{(\lambda-7)^2+(4\lambda-7)^2+(-9\lambda+7)^2}=7\Rightarrow98(\lambda^2-2\lambda+1)=0\Rightarrow\lambda=1$
Hence, the required point is $P(-4,1,-3)$.
The equation of line $PQ$ is $\dfrac{x+4}{6}=\dfrac{y-1}{3}=\dfrac{z+3}{2}$ or $\dfrac{x-2}{6}=\dfrac{y-4}{3}=\dfrac{z+1}{2}$

answer.text:
The vector equations of the lines are
$\vec r=-\hat i+\hat j+9\hat k+\lambda(2\hat i+\hat j-3\hat k)$ and $\vec r=3\hat i-15\hat j+9\hat k+\mu(2\hat i-7\hat j+5\hat k)$
$\vec{a_1}=-\hat i+\hat j+9\hat k,\ \vec{a_2}=3\hat i-15\hat j+9\hat k$
$\vec{b_1}=2\hat i+\hat j-3\hat k,\ \vec{b_2}=2\hat i-7\hat j+5\hat k$
$\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1}=4\hat i-16\hat j$
$\vec{b_1}\times\vec{b_2}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat i&\hat j&\hat k\\2&1&-3\\2&-7&5\end{vmatrix}=-16\hat i-16\hat j-16\hat k$
S.D. $=\dfrac{|(\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1})\cdot(\vec{b_1}\times\vec{b_2})|}{|\vec{b_1}\times\vec{b_2}|}=\dfrac{12}{\sqrt3}=4\sqrt3$

questions.text: Find the image $A'$ of the point $A(2, 1, 2)$ in the line $l : \vec{r} = 4\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k} + \lambda(\hat{i} - \hat{j} - \hat{k})$. Also, find the equation of line joining $AA'$. Find the foot of perpendicular from point A on the line $l$.

answer.text:
Let the image of $A$ in the line be $A'(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$.
The point $P$, the point of intersection of the lines $l$ and $AA'$, has coordinates $(\lambda+4,-\lambda+2,-\lambda+2)$ for some $\lambda$.
Drs of $AP$ are $\langle\lambda+2,-\lambda+1,-\lambda\rangle$.
$AP\perp l\Rightarrow(\lambda+2)-(-\lambda+1)-(-\lambda)=0\Rightarrow\lambda=-\dfrac13$
Therefore, the coordinates of $P$ (foot of perpendicular) are $\left(\dfrac{11}{3},\dfrac73,\dfrac73\right)$.
$P$ is the mid-point of $AA'$: $\dfrac{2+\alpha}{2}=\dfrac{11}{3},\ \dfrac{1+\beta}{2}=\dfrac73,\ \dfrac{2+\gamma}{2}=\dfrac73\Rightarrow\alpha=\dfrac{16}{3},\ \beta=\dfrac{11}{3},\ \gamma=\dfrac83$
The coordinates of the image are $\left(\dfrac{16}{3},\dfrac{11}{3},\dfrac83\right)$.
The equation of $AA'$ is $\dfrac{x-2}{10/3}=\dfrac{y-1}{8/3}=\dfrac{z-2}{2/3}$ or $\dfrac{3(x-2)}{5}=\dfrac{3(y-1)}{4}=\dfrac{3(z-2)}{1}$

questions.text: Find the distance of the point $(-1, -5, -10)$ from the point of intersection of the lines $\dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 2}{3} = \dfrac{z - 3}{4}$ and $\dfrac{x - 4}{5} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = z$.

answer.text:
$l_1:\dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac{y-2}{3}=\dfrac{z-3}{4}=\lambda$. Any point on $l_1$ is $(2\lambda+1,3\lambda+2,4\lambda+3)$.
$l_2:\dfrac{x-4}{5}=\dfrac{y-1}{2}=\dfrac{z-0}{1}=\mu$. Any point on $l_2$ is $(5\mu+4,2\mu+1,\mu)$.
For the point of intersection, $2\lambda+1=5\mu+4,\ 3\lambda+2=2\mu+1$
Solving, $\lambda=\mu=-1$. Since $\lambda=\mu=-1$ satisfy $4\lambda+3=\mu$,
$\therefore$ the point of intersection is $(-1,-1,-1)$.
Now the distance of $(-1,-5,-10)$ from $(-1,-1,-1)$ is $\sqrt{(-1+1)^2+(-1+5)^2+(-1+10)^2}=\sqrt{97}$ units.

questions.text: An engineer is designing a new metro rail network in a city. Initially, two metro lines, Line A and Line B, each consisting of multiple stations are designed. The track for Line A is represented by $l_1 : \dfrac{x - 2}{3} = \dfrac{y + 1}{-2} = \dfrac{z - 3}{4}$, while the track for Line B is represented by $l_2 : \dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 3}{1} = \dfrac{z + 2}{-3}$. Based on the above information, answer the following questions : (i) Find whether the two metro tracks are parallel. (ii) Solar panels are to be installed on the rooftop of the metro stations. Determine the equation of the line representing the placement of solar panels on the rooftop of Line A's stations, given that panels are to be positioned parallel to Line A's track ($l_1$) and pass through the point $(1, -2, -3)$. (iii)(a) To connect the stations, a pedestrian pathway perpendicular to the two metro lines is to be constructed which passes through point $(3, 2, 1)$. Determine the equation of the pedestrian walkway.  OR  (iii)(b) Find the shortest distance between Line A and Line B.

answer.text:
$l_1:\dfrac{x-2}{3}=\dfrac{y+1}{-2}=\dfrac{z-3}{4}$;\ $l_2:\dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac{y-3}{1}=\dfrac{z+2}{-3}$
(i) Drs of $l_1$ are $\langle3,-2,4\rangle$, drs of $l_2$ are $\langle2,1,-3\rangle$. As the drs are not proportional, $l_1$ is not parallel to $l_2$.
(ii) Equation of line parallel to $l_1$ and passing through $(1,-2,-3)$ is $\dfrac{x-1}{3}=\dfrac{y+2}{-2}=\dfrac{z+3}{4}$ or $\vec r=(\hat i-2\hat j-3\hat k)+\lambda(3\hat i-2\hat j+4\hat k)$
(iii)(a) The pathway is perpendicular to $l_1$ and $l_2$, $\therefore$ it is parallel to $\vec{b_1}\times\vec{b_2}$.
$\vec b=\vec{b_1}\times\vec{b_2}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat i&\hat j&\hat k\\3&-2&4\\2&1&-3\end{vmatrix}=2\hat i+17\hat j+7\hat k$
$\therefore$ Equation of pathway is $\vec r=(3\hat i+2\hat j+\hat k)+\lambda(2\hat i+17\hat j+7\hat k)$

questions.text: A man needs to hang two lanterns on a straight wire whose end points have coordinates $A(4, 1, -2)$ and $B(6, 2, -3)$. Find the coordinates of the points where he hangs the lanterns such that these points trisect the wire AB.
questions.topic: Equation of a Line in Space

answer.text:
Let $P$ and $Q$ trisect the wire $AB$.
$P$ divides $AB$ in the ratio $1:2$, so the coordinates of $P=\left(\dfrac{14}{3},\dfrac43,-\dfrac73\right)$
$Q$ divides $AB$ in the ratio $2:1$, so the coordinates of $Q=\left(\dfrac{16}{3},\dfrac53,-\dfrac83\right)$

questions.text: Find the foot of the perpendicular drawn from the point $(1, 1, 4)$ on the line $\dfrac{x + 2}{5} = \dfrac{y + 1}{2} = \dfrac{-z + 4}{-3}$.

answer.text:
Let $\dfrac{x+2}{5}=\dfrac{y+1}{2}=\dfrac{-z+4}{-3}=\lambda$. Coordinates of the general point on the line are $M(5\lambda-2,2\lambda-1,3\lambda+4)$.
Direction ratios of $PM$ are $\langle5\lambda-3,2\lambda-2,3\lambda\rangle$.
Since $PM\perp l\Rightarrow5(5\lambda-3)+2(2\lambda-2)+3(3\lambda)=0\Rightarrow\lambda=\dfrac12$
Hence, coordinates of $M$ (foot of perpendicular) are $\left(\dfrac12,0,\dfrac{11}{2}\right)$.

questions.text: Find the point on the line $\dfrac{x - 1}{3} = \dfrac{y + 1}{2} = \dfrac{z - 4}{3}$ at a distance of $2\sqrt{2}$ units from the point $(-1, -1, 2)$.

answer.text:
Equation of the given line: $\dfrac{x-1}{3}=\dfrac{y+1}{2}=\dfrac{z-4}{3}=\lambda$. Coordinates of any general point on the line are $P(3\lambda+1,2\lambda-1,3\lambda+4)$.
Let the distance of $P$ from $(-1,-1,2)$ be $2\sqrt2$.
$\Rightarrow\sqrt{(3\lambda+2)^2+(2\lambda)^2+(3\lambda+2)^2}=2\sqrt2\Rightarrow22\lambda^2+24\lambda=0\Rightarrow\lambda=0$ or $\lambda=-\dfrac{12}{11}$
Hence, coordinates of point $P$ are $(1,-1,4)$ or $\left(-\dfrac{25}{11},-\dfrac{35}{11},\dfrac{8}{11}\right)$

questions.text: Determine if the lines $\vec{r} = (\hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k}) + \lambda(3\hat{i} - \hat{j})$ and $\vec{r} = (4\hat{i} - \hat{k}) + \mu(2\hat{i} + 3\hat{k})$ intersect each other.
questions.topic: Equation of a Line in Space

answer.text:
$\vec{b_1}=3\hat i-\hat j,\ \vec{b_2}=2\hat i+3\hat k,\ \vec{a_1}=\hat i+\hat j-\hat k,\ \vec{a_2}=4\hat i-\hat k$
$(\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1})=3\hat i-\hat j$
$\vec{b_1}\times\vec{b_2}=-3\hat i-9\hat j+2\hat k$
$(\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1})\cdot(\vec{b_1}\times\vec{b_2})=(3\hat i-\hat j)\cdot(-3\hat i-9\hat j+2\hat k)=0$, hence the lines intersect.

questions.text: Find the distance of the point $P(2, 4, -1)$ from the line $\dfrac{x + 5}{1} = \dfrac{y + 3}{4} = \dfrac{z - 6}{-9}$.

answer.text:
Let $\vec{a_2}=2\hat i+4\hat j-\hat k,\ \vec{a_1}=-5\hat i-3\hat j+6\hat k$ and $\vec b=\hat i+4\hat j-9\hat k$
Distance between point and line is $d=\dfrac{|(\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1})\times\vec b|}{|\vec b|}$
Here $(\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1})=7\hat i+7\hat j-7\hat k$
$(\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1})\times\vec b=-35\hat i+56\hat j+21\hat k$
$d=\dfrac{49\sqrt2}{7\sqrt2}=7$

questions.text: Let the position vectors of the points A, B and C be $3\hat{i} - \hat{j} - 2\hat{k}$, $\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - \hat{k}$ and $\hat{i} + 5\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$ respectively. Find the vector and cartesian equations of the line passing through A and parallel to line BC.

answer.text:

Vector equation is $\vec r=3\hat i-\hat j-2\hat k+\mu(3\hat j+4\hat k)$
Cartesian equation is $\dfrac{x-3}{0}=\dfrac{y+1}{3}=\dfrac{z+2}{4}$

questions.text: Let the polished side of the mirror be along the line $\dfrac{x}{1} = \dfrac{1 - y}{-2} = \dfrac{2z - 4}{6}$. A point $P(1, 6, 3)$, some distance away from the mirror, has its image formed behind the mirror. Find the coordinates of the image point and the distance between the point P and its image.
questions.topic: Equation of a Line in Space

answer.text:
Equation of the given line is $\dfrac{x}{1}=\dfrac{y-1}{2}=\dfrac{z-2}{3}$. Let coordinates of a point on the line be $(\lambda,2\lambda+1,3\lambda+2)$ for some $\lambda$.
Direction ratios of the line perpendicular to the line along the mirror are $\langle\lambda-1,2\lambda-5,3\lambda-1\rangle$.
$(\lambda-1)\cdot1+(2\lambda-5)\cdot2+(3\lambda-1)\cdot3=0$ gives $\lambda=1$.
Coordinates of the foot of perpendicular are $(1,3,5)$.
For the image: $\dfrac{x+1}{2}=1,\ \dfrac{y+6}{2}=3,\ \dfrac{z+3}{2}=5$ gives the image as $(1,0,7)$.
Required distance $=\sqrt{0+36+16}=2\sqrt{13}$

questions.text: Find the point Q on the line $\dfrac{2x + 4}{6} = \dfrac{y + 1}{2} = \dfrac{-2z + 6}{-4}$ at a distance of $3\sqrt{2}$ from the point $P(1, 2, 3)$.

answer.text:
The general point on the line is $Q(3\lambda-2,2\lambda-1,2\lambda+3)$ for some $\lambda\in R$.
$PQ=3\sqrt2\Rightarrow(PQ)^2=18\Rightarrow(3\lambda-3)^2+(2\lambda-3)^2+(2\lambda)^2=18$
$17\lambda^2-30\lambda=0\Rightarrow\lambda=0$ or $\lambda=\dfrac{30}{17}$
Thus, the point is $Q(-2,-1,3)$ or $Q\left(\dfrac{56}{17},\dfrac{43}{17},\dfrac{111}{17}\right)$

questions.text: Find the image of the point $(-1, 5, 2)$ in the line $\dfrac{2x - 4}{2} = \dfrac{y}{2} = \dfrac{2 - z}{3}$. Find the length of the line segment joining the points (given point and the image point).

answer.text:
Let $A'(a,b,c)$ be the image of the point $A(-1,5,2)$ in the given line. Assume $M$ as the point of intersection of $AA'$ with the given line; then $M$ is the mid-point of $AA'$.
The line in standard form is $\dfrac{x-2}{1}=\dfrac{y}{2}=\dfrac{z-2}{-3}$, so $M$ is the point $(\lambda+2,2\lambda,-3\lambda+2)$ for some $\lambda\in R$.
Direction ratios of $AM$ are $\langle\lambda+3,2\lambda-5,-3\lambda\rangle$.
$AM\perp$ line $\Rightarrow1(\lambda+3)+2(2\lambda-5)-3(-3\lambda)=0\Rightarrow\lambda=\dfrac12$
$M\left(\dfrac52,1,\dfrac12\right)=M\left(\dfrac{a-1}{2},\dfrac{b+5}{2},\dfrac{c+2}{2}\right)\Rightarrow a=6,\ b=-3,\ c=-1$
$\therefore$ the image of $A$ in the line is $A'(6,-3,-1)$; and $AA'=\sqrt{49+64+9}=\sqrt{122}$

questions.text: Check whether the lines given by $\dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 2}{3} = \dfrac{z - 3}{4}$ and $\dfrac{x - 4}{5} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = z$ are parallel or not. If parallel, find the distance between them, otherwise find their point of intersection, if the lines are intersecting.
questions.topic: Equation of a Line in Space

answer.text: The direction ratios of the two lines are $\langle 2,3,4\rangle$ and $\langle 5,2,1\rangle$. Since these are not proportional, the lines are not parallel. A general point on the first line is $(2\lambda+1,\ 3\lambda+2,\ 4\lambda+3)$ and on the second is $(5\mu+4,\ 2\mu+1,\ \mu)$. For intersection: $2\lambda+1=5\mu+4$, $3\lambda+2=2\mu+1$, $4\lambda+3=\mu$. Solving the first two gives $\lambda=-1$, $\mu=-1$, which also satisfy the third equation. Hence the lines intersect, and the point of intersection is $(-1,-1,-1)$.

questions.text: Find the co-ordinates of the point on the line $\vec{r} = -\hat{j} + 3\hat{k} + \lambda(2\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + \hat{k})$ such that the sum of co-ordinates is 3.
questions.topic: Equation of a Line in Space

answer.text: $\vec{r}=-\hat{j}+3\hat{k}+\lambda(2\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\hat{k})=2\lambda\hat{i}+(-2\lambda-1)\hat{j}+(\lambda+3)\hat{k}$. The sum of the coordinates is $3$: $2\lambda+(-2\lambda-1)+(\lambda+3)=3\Rightarrow\lambda=1$. Required point: $(2,-3,4)$.

questions.text: A line passing through the points $A(1, 2, 3)$ and $B(5, 8, 11)$ intersects the line $\vec{r} = 4\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \lambda(5\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + \hat{k})$. Find the co-ordinates of the point of intersection. Hence, write the equation of a line passing through the point of intersection and perpendicular to both the lines.
questions.topic: Equation of a Line in Space

answer.text: The line through $A(1,2,3)$ and $B(5,8,11)$ is $l_1:\dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac{y-2}{3}=\dfrac{z-3}{4}=\mu$, and the given line is $l_2:\dfrac{x-4}{5}=\dfrac{y-1}{2}=\dfrac{z}{1}=\lambda$. A general point on $l_1$ is $P(2\mu+1,\,3\mu+2,\,4\mu+3)$ and on $l_2$ is $Q(5\lambda+4,\,2\lambda+1,\,\lambda)$. For intersection $P=Q$: $2\mu+1=5\lambda+4$, $3\mu+2=2\lambda+1$, $4\mu+3=\lambda$; solving gives $\mu=\lambda=-1$, so the point of intersection is $(-1,-1,-1)$. A line $l$ through $(-1,-1,-1)$ with direction ratios $\langle a,b,c\rangle$ perpendicular to both satisfies $2a+3b+4c=0$ and $5a+2b+c=0$, giving $\langle a,b,c\rangle\propto\langle -5,18,-11\rangle$. Hence $l:\dfrac{x+1}{-5}=\dfrac{y+1}{18}=\dfrac{z+1}{-11}$.

questions.text: If the lines $\dfrac{x - 3}{1} = \dfrac{1 - y}{1} = \dfrac{z + 2}{p}$ and $\dfrac{2 - x}{3} = \dfrac{y + 1}{5} = \dfrac{z + 56}{2p}$ are perpendicular to each other, then find the value(s) of $p$.
questions.topic: Equation of a Line in Space

answer.text: Line 1 has direction ratios $\langle 1,-1,p\rangle$; line 2, $\dfrac{2-x}{3}=\dfrac{y+1}{5}=\dfrac{z+56}{2p}$, has direction ratios $\langle -3,5,2p\rangle$. Perpendicularity $\Rightarrow 1(-3)+(-1)(5)+p(2p)=0\Rightarrow 2p^2=8\Rightarrow p=\pm 2$.

questions.text: Find the vector equation of a line passing through the origin and perpendicular to both the lines $\vec{r} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 2\hat{k} + \lambda(3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 2\hat{k})$ and $\vec{r} = \mu(\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k})$.
questions.topic: Equation of a Line in Space

answer.text: The required line passes through the origin and is perpendicular to both lines, so its direction is $\vec{b}=(3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+2\hat{k})\times(\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k})=6\hat{i}-\hat{j}-7\hat{k}$. Vector equation: $\vec{r}=\delta(6\hat{i}-\hat{j}-7\hat{k})$.

questions.text: Represent the equations of lines $l_1$ and $l_2$ in vector form and check whether they are intersecting or not. $l_1 : \dfrac{x + 3}{-3} = \dfrac{y - 1}{1} = \dfrac{z - 5}{5}$, $l_2 : \dfrac{x + 1}{-1} = \dfrac{2 - y}{-2} = \dfrac{z - 5}{5}$.
questions.topic: Equation of a Line in Space

answer.text: $l_1:\dfrac{x+3}{-3}=\dfrac{y-1}{1}=\dfrac{z-5}{5}$, i.e. $\vec{r}=(-3\hat{i}+\hat{j}+5\hat{k})+\lambda(-3\hat{i}+\hat{j}+5\hat{k})$; and $l_2:\dfrac{x+1}{-1}=\dfrac{2-y}{-2}=\dfrac{z-5}{5}$, i.e. $\vec{r}=(-\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+5\hat{k})+\mu(-\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+5\hat{k})$. Here $\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}$ and $\vec{b_1}\times\vec{b_2}=-5\hat{i}+10\hat{j}-5\hat{k}$. Since $(\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1})\cdot(\vec{b_1}\times\vec{b_2})=-10+10+0=0$, the lines are coplanar and hence intersecting.

questions.text: Opposite sides of a square are along the lines : $\vec{r} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 4\hat{k} + \lambda(2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 6\hat{k})$ and $\vec{r} = 3\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 5\hat{k} + \mu(2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 6\hat{k})$. Find the area of the square if direction ratios of other pair of opposite sides of the square are given by $<-3, 6, p>$. Also, find the value of $p$.
questions.topic: Direction Cosines and Direction Ratios of a Line

answer.text: The two sides lie along $\vec{r}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-4\hat{k}+\lambda\vec{b}$ and $\vec{r}=3\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-5\hat{k}+\mu\vec{b}$ with $\vec{b}=2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+6\hat{k}$. Here $\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ and $(\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1})\times\vec{b}=9\hat{i}-14\hat{j}+4\hat{k}$, so $|(\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1})\times\vec{b}|=\sqrt{293}$. The side length equals the distance between these parallel lines, $\dfrac{\sqrt{293}}{7}$, so the area of the square is $\dfrac{293}{49}$ square units. Since adjacent sides are perpendicular, $\langle -3,6,p\rangle\cdot\langle 2,3,6\rangle=0\Rightarrow-6+18+6p=0\Rightarrow p=-2$.

questions.text: Find a point on the line $\dfrac{x - 2}{3} = \dfrac{1 - y}{2} = \dfrac{z - 3}{2}$ at a distance of $\sqrt{2}$ units from the point $(1, 2, 3)$.

answer.text: $\dfrac{x-2}{3}=\dfrac{1-y}{2}=\dfrac{z-3}{2}=k\Rightarrow P(3k+2,\,-2k+1,\,2k+3)$; the given point is $Q(1,2,3)$. $|PQ|=\sqrt{2}\Rightarrow(3k+1)^2+(-2k-1)^2+(2k)^2=2\Rightarrow 17k^2+10k=0\Rightarrow k=0$ or $k=-\dfrac{10}{17}$. The required points are $(2,1,3)$ and $\left(\dfrac{4}{17},\dfrac{37}{17},\dfrac{31}{17}\right)$.

questions.text: Find the shortest distance between the lines $\vec{r} = (4 + \lambda)\hat{i} + (2\lambda - 1)\hat{j} - 3\lambda\hat{k}$ and $\vec{r} = (1 + 2\mu)\hat{i} + (2 - 5\mu)\hat{k} + (4\mu - 1)\hat{j}$.

answer.text: For the lines with $\vec{a_1}=4\hat{i}-\hat{j}$, $\vec{b_1}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-3\hat{k}$ and $\vec{a_2}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$, $\vec{b_2}=2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-5\hat{k}$: $\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1}=-3\hat{i}+2\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b_1}\times\vec{b_2}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}$, $|\vec{b_1}\times\vec{b_2}|=\sqrt{5}$. Shortest distance $=\dfrac{|(-3\hat{i}+2\hat{k})\cdot(2\hat{i}-\hat{j})|}{\sqrt{5}}=\dfrac{6}{\sqrt{5}}=\dfrac{6\sqrt{5}}{5}$.

questions.text: Find the equation of a line (in vector and cartesian form) that passes through the point of intersection of lines $\dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 2}{3} = \dfrac{z - 3}{4}$ and $\dfrac{x - 4}{5} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = z$ and is parallel to the vector $3\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 8\hat{k}$.
questions.topic: Equation of a Line in Space

answer.text: A general point on the first line is $P(2a+1,\,3a+2,\,4a+3)$ and on the second is $Q(5b+4,\,2b+1,\,b)$; equating gives $a=b=-1$, so the point of intersection is $(-1,-1,-1)$. The required line through it parallel to $3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-8\hat{k}$ is, in Cartesian form, $\dfrac{x+1}{3}=\dfrac{y+1}{2}=\dfrac{z+1}{-8}$, and in vector form $\vec{r}=(-\hat{i}-\hat{j}-\hat{k})+\lambda(3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-8\hat{k})$.

questions.text: Find the angle between the following pair of lines : $\dfrac{x - 2}{3} = \dfrac{y + 5}{2} = \dfrac{1 - z}{-6}$ and $\dfrac{x - 7}{1} = \dfrac{y}{2} = \dfrac{6 - z}{-2}$.

answer.text: The lines have direction ratios $\langle 3,2,6\rangle$ and $\langle 1,2,2\rangle$. $\cos\theta=\dfrac{3\cdot 1+2\cdot 2+6\cdot 2}{\sqrt{3^2+2^2+6^2}\,\sqrt{1^2+2^2+2^2}}=\dfrac{19}{7\cdot 3}=\dfrac{19}{21}$. Hence $\theta=\cos^{-1}\dfrac{19}{21}$.

questions.text: Find the foot of the perpendicular from the point $(0, 2, 3)$ on the line $\dfrac{-x - 3}{-5} = \dfrac{1 - y}{-2} = \dfrac{3z + 12}{9}$ and hence find the length of the perpendicular.

answer.text: $\dfrac{-x-3}{-5}=\dfrac{1-y}{-2}=\dfrac{3z+12}{9}\Leftrightarrow\dfrac{x+3}{5}=\dfrac{y-1}{2}=\dfrac{z+4}{3}=\lambda$; foot $P(5\lambda-3,\,2\lambda+1,\,3\lambda-4)$. The perpendicular from $(0,2,3)$ has direction $\langle 5\lambda-3,\,2\lambda-1,\,3\lambda-7\rangle\perp\langle 5,2,3\rangle\Rightarrow 5(5\lambda-3)+2(2\lambda-1)+3(3\lambda-7)=0\Rightarrow 38\lambda-38=0\Rightarrow\lambda=1$. Foot of perpendicular $(2,3,-1)$; length $=\sqrt{2^2+1^2+(-4)^2}=\sqrt{21}$.

questions.text: Find the value of $p$ if the shortest distance between the lines $\vec{r} = (\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}) + \lambda(\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k})$ and $\vec{r} = (p\hat{i} - \hat{j} - \hat{k}) + \mu(2\hat{i} + \hat{j} + 2\hat{k})$ is $\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{2}}$ units.

answer.text: For $\vec{a_1}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}$, $\vec{b_1}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ and $\vec{a_2}=p\hat{i}-\hat{j}-\hat{k}$, $\vec{b_2}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$: $\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1}=(p-1)\hat{i}-3\hat{j}-2\hat{k}$, $\vec{b_1}\times\vec{b_2}=-3\hat{i}+3\hat{k}$, $|\vec{b_1}\times\vec{b_2}|=3\sqrt{2}$. $\text{S.D.}=\dfrac{|(\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1})\cdot(\vec{b_1}\times\vec{b_2})|}{3\sqrt{2}}=\dfrac{|-3(p-1)-6|}{3\sqrt{2}}=\dfrac{|-3p-3|}{3\sqrt{2}}=\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{2}}\Rightarrow|-3p-3|=9\Rightarrow p=-4$ or $p=2$.

The probability distribution of a random variable $X$ is given below : (i) Find the value of $k$. (ii) Find $P(1 \leq X < 3)$. (iii) Find $E(X)$, the mean of $X$.
questions.topic: Random Variables and its Probability Distributions

answer.text:
(i) $\dfrac{k}{2}+\dfrac{k}{3}+\dfrac{k}{6}=1$ gives $k=1$
(ii) $P(1\le X<3)=\dfrac{k}{2}+\dfrac{k}{3}=\dfrac{5k}{6}=\dfrac{5}{6}$
(iii) $E(X)=\sum p_i x_i=1\cdot\dfrac{k}{2}+2\cdot\dfrac{k}{3}+3\cdot\dfrac{k}{6}=\dfrac{k}{2}+\dfrac{2k}{3}+\dfrac{k}{2}=\dfrac{5k}{3}=\dfrac{5}{3}$

questions.text: A and B are independent events such that $P(A \cap \bar{B}) = \dfrac{1}{4}$ and $P(\bar{A} \cap B) = \dfrac{1}{6}$. Find $P(A)$ and $P(B)$.

answer.text:
$P(A)\,P(\bar B)=\dfrac14$, \ $P(\bar A)\,P(B)=\dfrac16$
Let $P(A)=x$, $P(B)=y$.
$x(1-y)=\dfrac14$, \ $(1-x)y=\dfrac16\Rightarrow x-y=\dfrac{1}{12}$
Eliminating $y$, we get $12x^2-13x+3=0$ gives $x=\dfrac13,\ \dfrac34$
$P(A)=\dfrac13\Rightarrow P(B)=\dfrac14$; \ \ $P(A)=\dfrac34\Rightarrow P(B)=\dfrac23$

answer.text:
(i) $x+0{\cdot}21=0{\cdot}44\Rightarrow x=0{\cdot}23$
(ii) $0{\cdot}41+y+0{\cdot}44+0{\cdot}11=1\Rightarrow y=0{\cdot}04$
(iii)(a) $P\!\left(\dfrac{C}{B}\right)=\dfrac{P(C\cap B)}{P(B)}$; \ $P(B)=0{\cdot}09+0{\cdot}04+0{\cdot}23=0{\cdot}36$
$P\!\left(\dfrac{C}{B}\right)=\dfrac{0{\cdot}23}{0{\cdot}36}=\dfrac{23}{36}$

questions.text: A and B throw a die alternately till one of them gets a '6' and wins the game. Find their respective probabilities of winning, if A starts first.

answer.text:
$P(\text{getting a six})=\dfrac16$; $\ P(\text{not getting a six})=\dfrac56$
$P(A\text{ wins})=\dfrac16+\left(\dfrac56\right)^2\cdot\dfrac16+\left(\dfrac56\right)^4\cdot\dfrac16+\cdots=\dfrac{\frac16}{1-\frac{25}{36}}=\dfrac{6}{11}$
$P(B\text{ wins})=1-P(A\text{ wins})=1-\dfrac{6}{11}=\dfrac{5}{11}$

In order to assess this concept, a decimal comparison test was administered to the students of class VI through the following question : In the recently held Sports Day in the school, 5 students participated in a javelin throw competition. The distances to which they have thrown the javelin are shown below in the table. The students were asked to identify who has thrown the javelin the farthest. Based on the test attempted by the students, the teacher concludes that 40% of the students have the misconception in the concept of decimal comparison and the rest do not have the misconception. 80% of the students having misconception answered Bijoy as the correct answer in the paper. 90% of the students who are identified with not having misconception, did not answer Bijoy as their answer. On the basis of the above information, answer the following : (i) What is the probability of a student not having misconception but still answers Bijoy in the test ? (ii) What is the probability that a randomly selected student answers Bijoy as his answer in the test ? (iii)(a) What is the probability that a student who answered as Bijoy is having misconception ?  OR  (iii)(b) What is the probability that a student who answered as Bijoy is amongst students who do not have the misconception ?

answer.text:
Let $E_1$: student has a misconception, $E_2$: student does not have misconception, $A$: student answered Bijoy as correct.
$P(E_1)=\dfrac{40}{100},\ P(E_2)=\dfrac{60}{100};\ P(A|E_1)=\dfrac{80}{100},\ P(A|E_2)=\dfrac{10}{100}$
(i) $P(A|E_2)=\dfrac{10}{100}$ or $\dfrac{1}{10}$
(ii) $P(A)=P(E_1)P(A|E_1)+P(E_2)P(A|E_2)=\dfrac{40}{100}\times\dfrac{80}{100}+\dfrac{60}{100}\times\dfrac{10}{100}=\dfrac{38}{100}$ or $\dfrac{19}{50}$
(iii)(a) $P(E_1|A)=\dfrac{P(E_1)P(A|E_1)}{P(A)}=\dfrac{\frac{40}{100}\times\frac{80}{100}}{\frac{38}{100}}=\dfrac{16}{19}$

questions.text: If $P(A \cup B) = 0{\cdot}9$ and $P(A \cap B) = 0{\cdot}4$, then $P(\bar{A}) + P(\bar{B})$ is :

The probability that a student buys a colouring book is $0{\cdot}7$ and that she buys a box of colours is $0{\cdot}2$. The probability that she buys a colouring book, given that she buys a box of colours, is $0{\cdot}3$. Find the probability that the student : (i) Buys both the colouring book and the box of colours. (ii) Buys a box of colours given that she buys the colouring book.

answer.text:
Let $A$ be the event of buying a colouring book and $B$ be the event of buying a box of colours.
$P(A)=0{\cdot}7,\ P(B)=0{\cdot}2,\ P(A/B)=0{\cdot}3$
(i) $P\left(\dfrac{A}{B}\right)=\dfrac{P(A\cap B)}{P(B)}\Rightarrow0{\cdot}3=\dfrac{P(A\cap B)}{0{\cdot}2}\Rightarrow P(A\cap B)=0{\cdot}06$ or $\dfrac{3}{50}$
(ii) $P\left(\dfrac{B}{A}\right)=\dfrac{P(A\cap B)}{P(A)}=\dfrac{0{\cdot}06}{0{\cdot}7}=\dfrac{3}{35}$ or $0{\cdot}086$

questions.text: A person has a fruit box that contains 6 apples and 4 oranges. He picks out a fruit three times, one after the other, after replacing the previous one in the box. Find : (i) The probability distribution of the number of oranges he draws. (ii) The expectation of the random variable (number of oranges).
questions.topic: Random Variables and its Probability Distributions

answer.text:
Let $X$ be the random variable for the number of oranges. $X=0,1,2,3$
Let $A$ be the event that an orange is drawn. $P(A)=\dfrac{4}{10}=\dfrac25,\ P(\bar A)=1-\dfrac25=\dfrac35$. The probability distribution is shown below.
$E(X)=\sum p_ix_i=0\times\dfrac{27}{125}+1\times\dfrac{54}{125}+2\times\dfrac{36}{125}+3\times\dfrac{8}{125}=\dfrac{150}{125}$ or $\dfrac65$

questions.text: A gardener wanted to plant vegetables in his garden. Hence he bought 10 seeds of brinjal plant, 12 seeds of cabbage plant and 8 seeds of radish plant. The shopkeeper assured him of germination probabilities of brinjal, cabbage and radish to be 25%, 35% and 40% respectively. But before he could plant the seeds, they got mixed up in the bag and he had to sow them randomly. Based upon the above information, answer the following questions : (i) Calculate the probability of a randomly chosen seed to germinate. (ii) What is the probability that it is a cabbage seed, given that the chosen seed germinates ?

answer.text:
Let $A$: event that the chosen seed germinates, $B$: brinjal seed is chosen, $C$: cabbage seed is chosen, $R$: radish seed is chosen.
$P(B)=\dfrac{10}{30},\ P(C)=\dfrac{12}{30},\ P(R)=\dfrac{8}{30}$; $P\left(\dfrac{A}{B}\right)=\dfrac{25}{100},\ P\left(\dfrac{A}{C}\right)=\dfrac{35}{100},\ P\left(\dfrac{A}{R}\right)=\dfrac{40}{100}$
(i) $P(A)=P(B)P\left(\dfrac{A}{B}\right)+P(C)P\left(\dfrac{A}{C}\right)+P(R)P\left(\dfrac{A}{R}\right)=\dfrac{10}{30}\times\dfrac{25}{100}+\dfrac{12}{30}\times\dfrac{35}{100}+\dfrac{8}{30}\times\dfrac{40}{100}=\dfrac{990}{3000}$ or $\dfrac{33}{100}$
(ii) $P\left(\dfrac{C}{A}\right)=\dfrac{P(C)P\left(\frac{A}{C}\right)}{P(B)P\left(\frac{A}{B}\right)+P(C)P\left(\frac{A}{C}\right)+P(R)P\left(\frac{A}{R}\right)}=\dfrac{\frac{12}{30}\times\frac{35}{100}}{\frac{990}{3000}}=\dfrac{42}{99}$ or $\dfrac{14}{33}$

questions.text: A box has 4 green, 8 blue and 3 red pens. A student picks up a pen at random, checks its colour and replaces it in the box. He repeats this process 3 times. The probability that at least one pen picked was red is :

A person is Head of two independent selection committees I and II. If the probability of making a wrong selection in committee I is $0{\cdot}03$ and that in committee II is $0{\cdot}01$, then find the probability that the person makes the correct decision of selection : (i) in both committees (ii) in only one committee.

answer.text:
(i) $P(\text{correct decision in both committees})=(1-0{\cdot}03)(1-0{\cdot}01)=0{\cdot}9603$
(ii) $P(\text{correct decision in only one committee})=0{\cdot}03(1-0{\cdot}01)+(1-0{\cdot}03)(0{\cdot}01)=0{\cdot}0394$

questions.text: A shop selling electronic items sells smartphones of only three reputed companies A, B and C because chances of their manufacturing a defective smartphone are only 5%, 4% and 2% respectively. In his inventory he has 25% smartphones from company A, 35% smartphones from company B and 40% smartphones from company C. A person buys a smartphone from this shop. (i) Find the probability that it was defective. (ii) What is the probability that this defective smartphone was manufactured by company B ?

answer.text:
(i) $P(\text{defective smartphone})=0{\cdot}25\times0{\cdot}05+0{\cdot}35\times0{\cdot}04+0{\cdot}40\times0{\cdot}02=0{\cdot}0345$
(ii) $P(B/\text{Defective})=\dfrac{0{\cdot}35\times0{\cdot}04}{0{\cdot}25\times0{\cdot}05+0{\cdot}35\times0{\cdot}04+0{\cdot}40\times0{\cdot}02}=\dfrac{140}{345}$ or $\dfrac{28}{69}$

A coin is tossed and a card is selected at random from a well shuffled pack of 52 playing cards. The probability of getting head on the coin and a face card from the pack is :

10 identical blocks are marked with '0' on two of them, '1' on three of them, '2' on four of them and '3' on one of them and put in a box. If X denotes the number written on the block, then write the probability distribution of X and calculate its mean.
questions.topic: Random Variables and its Probability Distributions

answer.text:
Let $X$ denote the number written on the block ($X=0,1,2,3$). The probability distribution is shown below.
Mean $=E(X)=\sum p_ix_i=0\cdot\dfrac{2}{10}+1\cdot\dfrac{3}{10}+2\cdot\dfrac{4}{10}+3\cdot\dfrac{1}{10}=\dfrac{14}{10}=\dfrac75$ (or $1{\cdot}4$)

questions.text: In a village of 8000 people, 3000 go out of the village to work and 4000 are women. It is noted that 30% of women go out of the village to work. What is the probability that a randomly chosen individual is either a woman or a person working outside the village ?

answer.text:
$A=$ a randomly chosen person is a woman; $B=$ a randomly chosen person works outside the village.
$P(A)=\dfrac{4000}{8000}=\dfrac12,\ P(B)=\dfrac{3000}{8000}=\dfrac38,\ P(A\cap B)=\dfrac{1200}{8000}=\dfrac{3}{20}$
Required probability $=P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B)=\dfrac12+\dfrac38-\dfrac{3}{20}=\dfrac{29}{40}$

questions.text: Based upon the results of regular medical check-ups in a hospital, it was found that out of 1000 people, 700 were very healthy, 200 maintained average health and 100 had a poor health record. Let $A_1$ : People with good health, $A_2$ : People with average health, and $A_3$ : People with poor health. During a pandemic, the data expressed that the chances of people contracting the disease from category $A_1$, $A_2$ and $A_3$ are 25%, 35% and 50%, respectively. Based upon the above information, answer the following questions : (i) A person was tested randomly. What is the probability that he/she has contracted the disease ? (ii) Given that the person has not contracted the disease, what is the probability that the person is from category $A_2$ ?

answer.text:
Let $A$: person contracted the disease.
$P(A)=P(A_1)P(A|A_1)+P(A_2)P(A|A_2)+P(A_3)P(A|A_3)=\dfrac{7}{10}\left(\dfrac{25}{100}\right)+\dfrac{2}{10}\left(\dfrac{35}{100}\right)+\dfrac{1}{10}\left(\dfrac{50}{100}\right)=\dfrac{295}{1000}=0{\cdot}295$ or $\dfrac{59}{200}$
(ii) $P(A_2|\bar A)=\dfrac{P(A_2)P(\bar A/A_2)}{P(A_1)P(\bar A/A_1)+P(A_2)P(\bar A/A_2)+P(A_3)P(\bar A/A_3)}=\dfrac{\frac{2}{10}\times\frac{65}{100}}{\frac{7}{10}\times\frac{75}{100}+\frac{2}{10}\times\frac{65}{100}+\frac{1}{10}\times\frac{50}{100}}=\dfrac{2\times13}{7\times15+2\times13+1\times10}=\dfrac{26}{141}$

questions.text: In the following question, a statement of Assertion (A) is followed by a statement of Reason (R). Choose the correct answer.
questions.assertion: In an experiment of throwing an unbiased die, the probability of getting a prime number given that number appearing on the die being odd is $\dfrac{2}{3}$.
questions.reason: For any two events A and B, $P(A|B) = \dfrac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)}$.
ar_options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

answer.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

questions.text: Out of two bags, bag I contains 3 red and 4 white balls and bag II contains 8 red and 6 white balls. A die is thrown. If it shows a number less than 3 then a ball is drawn at random from bag I, otherwise a ball is drawn at random from bag II. Find the probability that the ball drawn from one of the bags is a red ball.

answer.text: Let $E_1$: the number on the die is $<3$; $E_2$: the number on the die is $\ge 3$; $A$: a red ball is drawn. Then $P(E_1)=\dfrac{2}{6}$, $P(A/E_1)=\dfrac{3}{7}$, $P(E_2)=\dfrac{4}{6}$, $P(A/E_2)=\dfrac{8}{14}$. Required probability $=P(A)=P(E_1)P(A/E_1)+P(E_2)P(A/E_2)=\dfrac{2}{6}\times\dfrac{3}{7}+\dfrac{4}{6}\times\dfrac{8}{14}=\dfrac{11}{21}$.

questions.text: The probability of simultaneous occurrence of atleast one of the two events X and Y is $a$. If the probability that exactly one of the events X, Y occurs is $b$, prove that $P(X') + P(Y') = 2 - 2a + b$.

answer.text: $P(X\cup Y)=a$ and $P(X\cup Y)-P(X\cap Y)=b$, hence $P(X\cap Y)=a-b$. Then $P(X')+P(Y')=[1-P(X)]+[1-P(Y)]=2-[P(X)+P(Y)]=2-[P(X\cup Y)+P(X\cap Y)]=2-[a+(a-b)]=2-2a+b$.

questions.text: In an online jackpot, there is one first prize of Rs. 3,00,000, two second prizes of Rs. 2,00,000 each and three third prizes of Rs. 50,000 each. A total of 1,00,000 jackpot tickets each costing Rs. 100 were sold there by raising a fund of Rs. 1,00,00,000. Rohan bought one ticket. Based on the given information, answer the following questions : (i) What are the possible amounts, the person can win ? (ii)(a) What is the probability that the person wins atleast Rs. 2,00,000 ?  OR  (ii)(b) What is the probability that the person does not win any amount ? (iii) In another jackpot, Rohan also bought a ticket having a prize money of Rs. 5,00,000. The chances of winning the jackpot are 1 in 1,00,000. Find the probability that on exactly one of tickets he wins the jackpot.

answer.text: One first prize of ₹$3{,}00{,}000$, two second prizes of ₹$2{,}00{,}000$ each and three third prizes of ₹$50{,}000$ each; $1{,}00{,}000$ tickets sold. (i) Possible winning amounts: ₹$3{,}00{,}000$, ₹$2{,}00{,}000$, ₹$50{,}000$. (ii)(a) $P(\text{win at least }₹2{,}00{,}000)=\dfrac{3}{1{,}00{,}000}$. OR (ii)(b) $P(\text{no win})=1-\dfrac{6}{1{,}00{,}000}=\dfrac{99994}{100000}$. (iii) In another jackpot (prize ₹$5{,}00{,}000$, chance $1$ in $1{,}00{,}000$), $P(\text{exactly one of the two tickets wins})=\dfrac{6}{100000}\times\dfrac{99999}{100000}+\dfrac{99994}{100000}\times\dfrac{1}{100000}=\dfrac{699988}{10^{10}}$.

questions.text: For two events A and B such that $P(A) \neq 0$ and $P(B) \neq 1$, $P(A'/B') =$

answer.text: $\dfrac{1 - P(A \cup B)}{P(B')}$

questions.text: The probability of hitting the target by a trained sniper is three times the probability of not hitting the target on a stormy day due to high wind speed. The sniper fired two shots on a stormy day when wind speed was very high. Find the probability that (i) target is hit (ii) atleast one shot misses the target.

answer.text: Let $P(\text{not hitting})=p$; then $P(\text{hitting})=3p$. $p+3p=1\Rightarrow p=\dfrac{1}{4}$, so $P(H)=\dfrac{3}{4}$ and $P(\overline{H})=\dfrac{1}{4}$. For two shots: (i) $P(\text{target is hit})=1-P(\overline{H}\,\overline{H})=1-\dfrac{1}{4}\times\dfrac{1}{4}=\dfrac{15}{16}$. (ii) $P(\text{at least one shot misses})=1-P(HH)=1-\dfrac{3}{4}\times\dfrac{3}{4}=\dfrac{7}{16}$.

questions.text: Mother, Father and Son line up at random for a family picture. Let events E : Son on one end and F : Father in the middle. Find $P(E/F)$.

answer.text: Mother $(M)$, Father $(F)$, Son $(S)$ line up at random; the sample space $\{MFS,MSF,FMS,FSM,SMF,SFM\}$ has $6$ arrangements. Let $E$: son on one end, $F$: father in the middle. Then $P(E\cap F)=\dfrac{2}{6}$ and $P(F)=\dfrac{2}{6}$, so $P(E|F)=\dfrac{P(E\cap F)}{P(F)}=1$ (given the father is in the middle, the son must be at an end).

questions.text: Smoking increases the risk of lung problems. A study revealed that 170 in 1000 males who smoke develop lung complications, while 120 out of 1000 females who smoke develop lung related problems. In a colony, 50 people were found to be smokers of which 30 are males. A person is selected at random from these 50 people and tested for lung related problems. Based on the given information, answer the following questions : (i) What is the probability that selected person is a female ? (ii) If a male person is selected, what is the probability that he will not be suffering from lung problems ? (iii)(a) A person selected at random is detected with lung complications. Find the probability that selected person is a female.  OR  (iii)(b) A person selected at random is not having lung problems, find the probability that the person is a male.

answer.text: Of $50$ smokers, $30$ are male $(M)$ and $20$ are female $(F)$; $P(L|M)=\dfrac{170}{1000}=\dfrac{17}{100}$ and $P(L|F)=\dfrac{120}{1000}=\dfrac{12}{100}$. (i) $P(F)=\dfrac{20}{50}=\dfrac{2}{5}$. (ii) $P(\text{not suffering}\mid\text{male})=P(L'|M)=1-\dfrac{17}{100}=\dfrac{83}{100}$. (iii)(a) By Bayes' theorem, $P(F|L)=\dfrac{P(F)P(L|F)}{P(M)P(L|M)+P(F)P(L|F)}=\dfrac{\frac{2}{5}\cdot\frac{12}{100}}{\frac{3}{5}\cdot\frac{17}{100}+\frac{2}{5}\cdot\frac{12}{100}}=\dfrac{24}{75}=\dfrac{8}{25}$. OR (iii)(b) $P(M|L')=\dfrac{\frac{3}{5}\cdot\frac{83}{100}}{\frac{3}{5}\cdot\frac{83}{100}+\frac{2}{5}\cdot\frac{88}{100}}=\dfrac{249}{425}$.

questions.text: If E and F are two independent events such that $P(E) = \dfrac{3}{10}$, $P(E \cup F) = \dfrac{1}{2}$, then $P(E|F) - P(F|E)$ is equal to :

A survey was conducted on the patients who have undergone knee replacement surgeries. It was found that robotic knee replacement surgery is 90% successful. On a particular day, three robotic surgeries were performed on patients A, B and C one after another. Assuming that the success and failure of each surgery are independent of each other, find the probability that : (i) only one surgery was successful, (ii) at most two surgeries were successful.

answer.text: $P(\text{success})=\dfrac{9}{10}$, $P(\text{failure})=\dfrac{1}{10}$; three independent surgeries. (i) $P(\text{exactly one successful})=3\cdot\dfrac{9}{10}\cdot\dfrac{1}{10}\cdot\dfrac{1}{10}=\dfrac{27}{1000}$. (ii) $P(\text{at most two successful})=1-P(\text{all three successful})=1-\left(\dfrac{9}{10}\right)^3=1-\dfrac{729}{1000}=\dfrac{271}{1000}$.

questions.text: A survey was conducted to find the success rate of students who take a gap year (drop a year) after Class XII and then pass the entrance examination. According to the data collected, 40% of the students appearing in the examination were droppers (gap-year students) and the remaining were regular Class XII students. Among the droppers, 5% passed the examination, while among the regular students, 10% passed. Based on the above information, answer the following questions : (i) Find the probability that a randomly chosen student is a regular student. (ii) A student is selected at random from the group of dropper students. What is the probability that this student did not pass ? (iii)(a) A student selected at random qualified the examination. Find the probability that student is not a dropout.  OR  (iii)(b) A student selected at random did not qualify the examination. Find the probability that the student was a regular student.

answer.text: $40\%$ of the students appearing were dropouts and $60\%$ were regular; of the dropouts $5\%$ qualify, and of the regulars $10\%$ qualify. (i) $P(\text{regular})=\dfrac{3}{5}$. (ii) $P(\text{not qualify}\mid\text{dropout})=\dfrac{95}{100}=\dfrac{19}{20}$. (iii)(a) By Bayes' theorem, $P(\text{not dropout}\mid\text{qualified})=\dfrac{\frac{60}{100}\cdot\frac{10}{100}}{\frac{40}{100}\cdot\frac{5}{100}+\frac{60}{100}\cdot\frac{10}{100}}=\dfrac{3}{4}$. OR (iii)(b) $P(\text{regular}\mid\text{not qualified})=\dfrac{\frac{60}{100}\cdot\frac{90}{100}}{\frac{40}{100}\cdot\frac{95}{100}+\frac{60}{100}\cdot\frac{90}{100}}=\dfrac{27}{46}$.

questions.text: A box contains 4 red, 5 blue and 1 green marble. A child randomly takes out a marble from the box, notes down the colour and puts it back in the box. If the activity is repeated 3 times, what is the probability that at least one marble is red ?

In a school, the probability of holding a debate competition is $\dfrac{1}{3}$ and that of a quiz competition is $\dfrac{2}{3}$. In the two participating teams, A has 4 girls and 6 boys and B has 7 girls and 3 boys. If a debate competition is held, the students are selected from team A and for the quiz competition they are selected from team B. If only two students are to be chosen from the teams, then find the probability that one will be a girl and the other a boy.

answer.text: $P(\text{debate }D)=\dfrac{1}{3}$, $P(\text{quiz }Q)=\dfrac{2}{3}$. Team A has $4$ girls and $6$ boys; Team B has $7$ girls and $3$ boys; two students are chosen, and $E$ is the event of one girl and one boy. $P(E|D)=2\cdot\dfrac{4}{10}\cdot\dfrac{6}{9}=\dfrac{8}{15}$ and $P(E|Q)=2\cdot\dfrac{7}{10}\cdot\dfrac{3}{9}=\dfrac{7}{15}$. Hence $P(E)=\dfrac{1}{3}\cdot\dfrac{8}{15}+\dfrac{2}{3}\cdot\dfrac{7}{15}=\dfrac{22}{45}$.

questions.text: An NGO organises a charity event in which they decide to distribute woollen caps to protect children from winter. The caps to be distributed are in three separate boxes, Box I has 30 red caps, Box II has 20 red and 10 green caps, and Box III has 30 green caps. The probability that a Box $i$ is selected and a cap picked out is $\dfrac{i}{6}$, where $i = 1, 2, 3$. Based on the above information, answer the following questions : A person selects a cap. (i) What is the probability that he selects a red cap ? (ii) If he selects a green cap, what is the probability that the cap has come from Box II ?

answer.text: Box I has $30$ red caps, Box II has $20$ red and $10$ green, Box III has $30$ green; $P(B_i)=\dfrac{i}{6}$ for $i=1,2,3$. (i) $P(\text{red})=\dfrac{1}{6}\cdot 1+\dfrac{2}{6}\cdot\dfrac{2}{3}+\dfrac{3}{6}\cdot 0=\dfrac{7}{18}$. (ii) $P(\text{green})=1-\dfrac{7}{18}=\dfrac{11}{18}$; by Bayes' theorem, $P(\text{Box II}\mid\text{green})=\dfrac{\frac{2}{6}\cdot\frac{1}{3}}{\frac{11}{18}}=\dfrac{2}{11}$.

questions.text: If $3P(A) = P(B) = \dfrac{3}{5}$ and $P(A|B) = \dfrac{2}{3}$, then $P(A \cap B)$ is :
A die is rolled. Consider events : $A = \{1, 2, 5\}$, $B = \{3, 5\}$, $C = \{2, 3, 4, 5\}$ and hence find : (i) $P(A|C)$ and $P(C|A)$ (ii) $P(A \cup B|C)$ and $P(A \cap B|C)$.

answer.text: A die is rolled with $A=\{1,2,5\}$, $B=\{3,5\}$, $C=\{2,3,4,5\}$. (i) $P(A|C)=\dfrac{n(A\cap C)}{n(C)}=\dfrac{2}{4}=\dfrac{1}{2}$; $P(C|A)=\dfrac{n(C\cap A)}{n(A)}=\dfrac{2}{3}$. (ii) $P(A\cap B\mid C)=\dfrac{n(A\cap B\cap C)}{n(C)}=\dfrac{1}{4}$; $P(A\cup B\mid C)=\dfrac{n((A\cup B)\cap C)}{n(C)}=\dfrac{3}{4}$.

questions.text: A box contains 6 cards numbered 1 to 6. A student is asked to pick up two cards, one by one after replacement and note down the numbers on the cards. Let A be the event of getting sum of the numbers on two cards as 10, and B, the event of a number other than 4 on the first card selected. Find $P(A \text{ and } B)$ and find whether the events A and B are independent events or not.

answer.text: Two cards numbered $1$–$6$ are drawn with replacement. $A$: sum $=10=\{(4,6),(6,4),(5,5)\}$, $n(A)=3$; $B$: first card $\neq 4$, $n(B)=30$. $A\cap B=\{(6,4),(5,5)\}$, so $P(A\cap B)=\dfrac{2}{36}=\dfrac{1}{18}$. Also $P(A)=\dfrac{3}{36}=\dfrac{1}{12}$, $P(B)=\dfrac{30}{36}=\dfrac{5}{6}$, so $P(A)\cdot P(B)=\dfrac{5}{72}\neq\dfrac{1}{18}$. Hence $A$ and $B$ are not independent.

questions.text: There are three types of vaccines $A_1$, $A_2$, $A_3$, available in the market to protect the population of the country from spread of certain infection. According to a survey conducted, it was found that 25% of the population was given Vaccine $A_1$, 35% of the population was given Vaccine $A_2$ and 40% of the population was given Vaccine $A_3$. The survey also stated that the probabilities that Vaccines $A_1$, $A_2$ and $A_3$ would protect against the infection were 60%, 55% and 50% respectively. Based on the above information, answer the following questions : Find the probability that : (i) The person taking vaccine $A_2$ will get infected. (ii) If a person is chosen randomly, he/she will be protected from the infection. (iii)(a) The person was given Vaccine $A_1$, given that the randomly chosen person is infected.  OR  (iii)(b) The person was given Vaccine $A_3$, given that the randomly chosen person is not infected.

answer.text: Vaccines: $P(A_1)=0{\cdot}25$, $P(A_2)=0{\cdot}35$, $P(A_3)=0{\cdot}40$; protection $60\%$, $55\%$, $50\%$ respectively (so infection $40\%$, $45\%$, $50\%$). (i) $P(A_2\text{ person infected})=45\%=0{\cdot}45$. (ii) $P(\text{protected})=0{\cdot}25(0{\cdot}60)+0{\cdot}35(0{\cdot}55)+0{\cdot}40(0{\cdot}50)=\dfrac{5425}{10000}=0{\cdot}5425$. (iii)(a) By Bayes' theorem, $P(A_1\mid\text{infected})=\dfrac{0{\cdot}25(0{\cdot}40)}{0{\cdot}25(0{\cdot}40)+0{\cdot}35(0{\cdot}45)+0{\cdot}40(0{\cdot}50)}=\dfrac{1000}{4575}=\dfrac{40}{183}$. OR (iii)(b) $P(A_3\mid\text{not infected})=\dfrac{0{\cdot}40(0{\cdot}50)}{0{\cdot}25(0{\cdot}60)+0{\cdot}35(0{\cdot}55)+0{\cdot}40(0{\cdot}50)}=\dfrac{2000}{5425}=\dfrac{80}{217}$.
